requirements.text: Until a concrete CAN backend is linked, rcp_can_bridge_send() shall return RCP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED rather than attempting an unconfigured transmission, and shall leave *out_response untouched.

requirements.title: default_config() returns documented defaults
requirements.text: rcp_can_default_config() shall return this module's documented default configuration values.

requirements.title: bridge_send() returns RCP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED when stub
requirements.text: Until a concrete DDS backend is linked, rcp_dds_bridge_send() shall return RCP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED rather than attempting an unconfigured transmission, and shall leave *out_response untouched.

requirements.title: default_config() returns documented defaults
requirements.text: rcp_dds_default_config() shall return this module's documented default configuration values.

requirements.title: bridge_send() returns RCP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED when stub
requirements.text: Until a concrete MQTT backend is linked, rcp_mqtt_bridge_send() shall return RCP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED rather than attempting an unconfigured transmission, and shall leave *out_response untouched.

requirements.title: default_config() returns documented defaults
requirements.text: rcp_mqtt_default_config() shall return this module's documented default configuration values.

requirements.title: bridge_send() returns RCP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED when stub
requirements.text: Until a concrete LIN backend is linked, rcp_lin_bridge_send() shall return RCP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED rather than attempting an unconfigured transmission, and shall leave *out_response untouched.

requirements.title: default_config() returns documented defaults
requirements.text: rcp_lin_default_config() shall return this module's documented default configuration values.

requirements.title: bridge_send() returns RCP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED when stub
requirements.text: Until a concrete UDS backend is linked, rcp_uds_bridge_send() shall return RCP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED rather than attempting an unconfigured transmission, and shall leave *out_response untouched.

requirements.title: default_config() returns documented defaults
requirements.text: rcp_uds_default_config() shall return this module's documented default configuration values.

requirements.title: bridge_send() returns RCP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED when stub
requirements.text: Until a concrete DoIP backend is linked, rcp_doip_bridge_send() shall return RCP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED rather than attempting an unconfigured transmission, and shall leave *out_response untouched.

requirements.title: default_config() returns documented defaults
requirements.text: rcp_doip_default_config() shall return this module's documented default configuration values.

requirements.title: acquire() returns a zeroed buffer of the requested size
requirements.text: rcp_loan_pool_acquire(pool, size) shall return a loan whose payload.len == size and whose payload.data bytes are all zero.

requirements.title: acquire() reuses a same-or-larger pooled buffer before allocating fresh
requirements.text: rcp_loan_pool_acquire() shall pop and reuse a free-list entry whose capacity is >= the requested size, when one is available, before calling calloc().

requirements.title: acquire() with size 0 returns a valid, empty loan
requirements.text: rcp_loan_pool_acquire(pool, 0) shall return a non-NULL loan with payload.len == 0.

requirements.title: rcp_loan_return() releases the buffer without freeing the loan
requirements.text: rcp_loan_return() shall return the loan's buffer to its pool's free list and clear release_fn, without freeing the rcp_loan_t itself.

requirements.title: rcp_loan_release() returns the buffer and frees the loan
requirements.text: rcp_loan_release() shall call rcp_loan_return() and then free the rcp_loan_t.

requirements.title: rcp_loan_return() is idempotent
requirements.text: Calling rcp_loan_return() more than once on the same loan shall be safe and shall not double-free the underlying buffer.

requirements.title: A returned buffer is available to a later acquire() of the same or smaller size
requirements.text: A buffer released via rcp_loan_return()/rcp_loan_release() shall be eligible for reuse by a subsequent rcp_loan_pool_acquire() call requesting a size <= its capacity.

requirements.title: pool_destroy() frees every pooled buffer
requirements.text: rcp_loan_pool_destroy() shall free every buffer currently in pool's free list, then pool itself, without leaking.

requirements.title: rcp_loan_pool_new() allocates an empty pool
requirements.text: rcp_loan_pool_new() shall return a heap-allocated rcp_loan_pool_t with no loaned buffers and its own mutex initialized, or NULL on allocation failure.

requirements.title: Discoverer interface for server discovery
requirements.text: rcp_mdns_discoverer_t shall define the abstract interface for mDNS-based RC Server discovery.

requirements.title: start() fires Added event for each discovered record
requirements.text: Discoverer::start() shall invoke the callback with EventType::Added for each discovered ServerInfo.

requirements.title: stop() terminates discovery
requirements.text: Discoverer::stop() shall cause the discoverer to stop emitting events.

requirements.title: StaticDiscoverer emits configured records
requirements.text: StaticDiscoverer::start() shall emit all configured ServerInfo entries synchronously before returning.

requirements.title: ServerInfo carries stream_id, host, and port
requirements.text: ServerInfo shall carry the rcp_stream_id_t identifying the RC Server, host string, port number, and service instance name.

requirements.title: instance_name follows _rcp-tc18._udp.local convention
requirements.text: make_instance_name() shall produce names of the form '<server_stream_id as 16 hex digits>.<host>._rcp-tc18._udp.local'.

requirements.title: Announcer interface for server registration
requirements.text: rcp_mdns_Announcer shall define the abstract interface for announcing an RC Server via the local mDNS responder.

requirements.title: withdraw() removes mDNS record
requirements.text: Announcer::withdraw(server_stream_id) shall remove the mDNS record for the given RC Server stream_id.

requirements.title: encode_entry_request() records a pending request
requirements.text: rcp_powerstate_manager_encode_entry_request() shall encode a SleepCMD request via ep_wakeup.h and, on success, remember its transaction_num for the addressed endpoint; it shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t, recording no pending state, for an unregistered endpoint or for any target_mode other than RCP_PWRMODE_SLEEP -- including RCP_PWRMODE_STANDBY, which has no SleepCMD wire encoding at all (TC18 §13.7.2.3 Figure 22; see REQ-WAKEUP-010).
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.3 Figure 22 (Endpoint sleep request), TC18.txt L4160-4166 -- corrected 2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group E, superseding this entry's prior (incorrect) reading of target_mode as wire-encodable

requirements.title: apply_entry_response() applies StandBy/Sleep on ENTRY_OK
requirements.text: rcp_powerstate_manager_apply_entry_response() shall, on a decoded RCP_PWRMODE_ENTRY_OK matching the endpoint's pending transaction_num, apply the pending target_mode via rcp_pwrmode_transition() and clear the pending request.

requirements.title: apply_entry_response() leaves mode unchanged on ENTRY_REFUSED
requirements.text: rcp_powerstate_manager_apply_entry_response() shall not change the endpoint's mirrored mode when the decoded result is RCP_PWRMODE_ENTRY_REFUSED, returning RCP_POWERSTATE_ERR_ENTRY_REFUSED.

requirements.title: apply_entry_response() rejects a mismatched transaction number
requirements.text: rcp_powerstate_manager_apply_entry_response() shall return RCP_POWERSTATE_ERR_UNEXPECTED_TXN without changing any state when there is no pending request for the endpoint or the decoded transaction_num does not match it.

requirements.title: wake_via_network() classifies hot/cold from the endpoint's own real handshake state, matching wake_via_pin()
requirements.text: rcp_powerstate_manager_wake_via_network() shall move a Sleep-ing endpoint to RCP_PWRMODE_NORMAL, reporting RCP_PWRMODE_START_HOT iff the endpoint's own handshake state (as built up by rcp_powerstate_manager_handshake_begin()/_apply_wakeup_echo()/_handshake_resume_queues(), the same path-agnostic three-step API rcp_powerstate_manager_wake_via_pin() requires) is complete, and RCP_PWRMODE_START_COLD otherwise; it shall return RCP_POWERSTATE_ERR_TRANSITION without changing mode if the endpoint is not currently in RCP_PWRMODE_SLEEP. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H): this entry previously required an unconditional RCP_PWRMODE_START_HOT report, matching a real bug where the function fabricated an always-immediately-complete handshake internally instead of consulting the endpoint's real state -- a genuine safety-relevant divergence from TC18 §12.4.1's own requirement that a network wake run the identical real handshake a pin wake does (REQ-PWRMODE-020's own primary-source correction, which this function never got updated to match).
requirements.tc18: §12.4.1 ("a TC14/TC10 wake-up request on the network...will directly check for the network availability and proceed as before"), TC18.txt L2304-L2305 -- same basis as REQ-PWRMODE-020's own correction

requirements.title: handshake_begin() starts step (a)
requirements.text: rcp_powerstate_manager_handshake_begin() shall (re)initialize the endpoint's handshake with the given repeat limit and attempt rcp_pwrmode_handshake_iface_reenabled() on it, returning false for an unregistered endpoint.

requirements.title: apply_wakeup_echo() drives step (b)
requirements.text: rcp_powerstate_manager_apply_wakeup_echo() shall decode the given bytes as a WakeUp echo and feed the result into the endpoint's own rcp_pwrmode_handshake_wakeup_attempt(), returning false for an unregistered endpoint.

requirements.title: wake_via_pin() honors the handshake's hot/cold classification
requirements.text: rcp_powerstate_manager_wake_via_pin() shall move a Sleep-ing endpoint to RCP_PWRMODE_NORMAL, reporting RCP_PWRMODE_START_HOT only when the endpoint's handshake has reached RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_COMPLETE and RCP_PWRMODE_START_COLD otherwise, and shall return RCP_POWERSTATE_ERR_TRANSITION without changing mode if the endpoint is not currently in RCP_PWRMODE_SLEEP.

requirements.title: Callback fires on every attempted transition
requirements.text: The power event callback shall be invoked, across all registered endpoints, on every attempted mode transition -- successful or not.

requirements.title: rcp_powerstate_strerror() returns unique human-readable name
requirements.text: rcp_powerstate_strerror() shall return a unique, non-empty name for each defined rcp_powerstate_errc_t constant, and a non-NULL name for any other value.

requirements.title: rcp_powerstate_manager_new() initializes every tracked endpoint to NORMAL with no pending request
requirements.text: rcp_powerstate_manager_new(endpoints, n_endpoints) shall allocate a manager tracking exactly n_endpoints endpoints, each initialized to RCP_PWRMODE_NORMAL with no pending power-mode request and a freshly-initialized wake handshake; it shall return NULL on allocation failure.

requirements.title: rcp_powerstate_manager_mode() reports a tracked endpoint's power mode, NORMAL if untracked
requirements.text: rcp_powerstate_manager_mode(m, addr) shall return the tracked power mode for addr, or RCP_PWRMODE_NORMAL when addr is not tracked by m.

requirements.title: rcp_powerstate_manager_encode_wakeup_probe() encodes a wakeup probe for a tracked endpoint only
requirements.text: rcp_powerstate_manager_encode_wakeup_probe(m, addr, transaction_num) shall encode a wakeup message addressed to addr's byte_bus_id carrying transaction_num when addr is tracked by m, and shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t (data == NULL) when it is not.

requirements.title: rcp_powerstate_manager_handshake_resume_queues() applies the resume-queues transition, false if untracked
requirements.text: rcp_powerstate_manager_handshake_resume_queues(m, addr) shall apply the tracked endpoint's wake-handshake resume-queues transition and return its result when addr is tracked by m, and shall return false without applying any transition when it is not.

requirements.title: rcp_powerstate_manager_destroy() releases every owned resource
requirements.text: rcp_powerstate_manager_destroy(m) shall be a safe no-op when m is NULL; otherwise it shall free its entries, callbacks, and callback_ctx arrays and destroy its mutex before freeing m itself.

requirements.title: Token bucket with configurable rate and burst, per endpoint
requirements.text: rcp_ratelimit_limiter_t shall maintain an independent token bucket per registered (stream_id, byte_bus_id) endpoint address, refilling at cfg.rate tokens/second up to cfg.burst.

requirements.title: Tokens refilled based on elapsed time
requirements.text: rcp_ratelimit_limiter_allow() shall refill an endpoint's bucket by (elapsed_seconds * cfg.rate) tokens, capped at cfg.burst, before evaluating admission.

requirements.title: allow() returns false when the bucket is exhausted
requirements.text: rcp_ratelimit_limiter_allow() shall return false, consuming no token, when an endpoint's bucket holds fewer than 1.0 tokens and the request is not safety-exempt.

requirements.title: Safety-tagged requests exempt when configured
requirements.text: rcp_ratelimit_limiter_allow() shall return true without consuming a token when request_type is safety-tagged (rcp_e2e_is_safety_request()) and cfg.exempt_safety is true.

requirements.title: Safety-tagged requests are not exempt when not configured
requirements.text: rcp_ratelimit_limiter_allow() shall apply normal bucket admission to a safety-tagged request_type when cfg.exempt_safety is false.

requirements.title: Each endpoint address has an independent bucket
requirements.text: Exhausting one (stream_id, byte_bus_id) address's bucket shall not affect the admission outcome for a different address, even one sharing the same stream_id.

requirements.title: First use of an address lazily seeds a full bucket
requirements.text: rcp_ratelimit_limiter_allow() shall, on the first call naming a given addr, create that endpoint's bucket seeded with cfg.burst tokens before evaluating admission.

requirements.title: allow() consumes exactly one token per admitted, non-exempt call
requirements.text: A successful, non-safety-exempt rcp_ratelimit_limiter_allow() call shall decrement the endpoint's bucket by exactly 1.0 tokens.

requirements.title: destroy() frees every tracked bucket
requirements.text: rcp_ratelimit_limiter_destroy() shall free every per-endpoint bucket rl tracks, then rl itself, without leaking.

requirements.title: rcp_ratelimit_default_config() returns the documented defaults
requirements.text: rcp_ratelimit_default_config() shall return rate = 100.0, burst = 20, and exempt_safety = true.

requirements.title: rcp_ratelimit_limiter_new() allocates a limiter with cfg and no tracked buckets
requirements.text: rcp_ratelimit_limiter_new(cfg) shall return a heap-allocated rcp_ratelimit_limiter_t configured with cfg and no per-address token buckets yet tracked, or NULL on allocation failure.

requirements.title: pair_new() creates two cross-wired AVTPDU transports
requirements.text: rcp_shmem_avtp_pair_new() shall return two rcp_avtp_transport_t sides, each starting at refcount 1 and sharing the caller-supplied time_sync_supported value and a single pair of bounded FIFOs.

requirements.title: A's send() is delivered to B's recv() in FIFO order
requirements.text: Frames sent via one side of a pair shall be delivered to the other side's recv() calls in the order they were sent.

requirements.title: B's send() is delivered to A's recv()
requirements.text: The pair's two directions shall be independent: a frame sent by one side shall never be observed by that same side's own recv().

requirements.title: recv() returns RCP_ERR_TIMEOUT when nothing is queued
requirements.text: recv() shall return RCP_ERR_TIMEOUT once the calling context's deadline elapses while its own inbound queue remains empty.

requirements.title: send()/recv() on a closed side return RCP_ERR_CLOSED
requirements.text: Once close() has been called on a side, that side's own send() shall return RCP_ERR_CLOSED immediately, and its recv() shall return RCP_ERR_CLOSED once its already-queued items (if any) have been drained.

requirements.title: send() rejects once its own outgoing queue is full
requirements.text: send() shall return RCP_ERR_BUSY without enqueuing when its own outgoing queue already holds queue_capacity items.

requirements.title: recv() into a too-small buffer leaves the item queued
requirements.text: recv() shall return RCP_ERR_BUSY, without removing the item from its queue, when the next queued item's length exceeds the caller-supplied buffer capacity.

requirements.title: releasing one side leaves the other usable
requirements.text: Releasing one side's last reference shall not itself close or invalidate the other side's own send()/recv(), which remain usable until that other side is itself closed.

requirements.title: the shared pair state is freed only once both sides are released
requirements.text: The internal state shared by a pair shall be freed exactly once, only after both sides' own refcounts have independently reached zero, regardless of release order.

requirements.title: default PCP map mirrors rcp_sched_kind_rank()
requirements.text: rcp_tsn_default_pcp_map() shall assign each rcp_sched_kind_t the PCP value rcp_sched_kind_rank() returns for that kind.

requirements.title: pcp_for() fails safe on an out-of-range kind
requirements.text: rcp_tsn_pcp_for() shall return the map's own RCP_SCHED_KIND_STANDARD entry for any kind value outside rcp_sched_kind_t's defined range, never a fabricated higher class.

requirements.title: classify_frame() classifies Standard and repurposed ACF_GBB frames, failing safe on malformed input
requirements.text: rcp_tsn_classify_frame() shall classify an ACF_ABB (or non-repurposed ACF_GBB) frame as RCP_SCHED_KIND_STANDARD, a repurposed ACF_GBB frame by its request_type opcode via rcp_sched_classify(), and any short, bad-subtype, or bad-message-type frame as RCP_SCHED_KIND_STANDARD.

requirements.title: send() tags socket_fd's SO_PRIORITY from the classified frame's kind, then delegates
requirements.text: send() shall, when socket_fd is not -1, set SO_PRIORITY to the PCP value the configured map assigns to the outgoing frame's classified rcp_sched_kind_t, and shall in every case delegate the send to the inner transport.

requirements.title: recv() delegates to the inner transport unmodified
requirements.text: recv() shall forward its call, and return the inner transport's own result, unmodified.

requirements.title: close() delegates to the inner transport
requirements.text: close() shall forward its call, and return the inner transport's own result, unmodified.

requirements.title: the constructor retains inner and mirrors its time_sync_supported
requirements.text: rcp_tsn_avtp_transport_new() shall retain a reference to inner and set the returned transport's own base.time_sync_supported to inner's.

requirements.title: rcp_tsn_default_config() returns the documented defaults
requirements.text: rcp_tsn_default_config() shall return the default PCP map (rcp_tsn_default_pcp_map()), vlan_id = 0, and cycle_ns = 0.

requirements.title: dial() connects a UDP socket to a fixed peer
requirements.text: rcp_udp_avtp_transport_dial() shall create a UDP socket and connect() it to the given host:port, returning an rcp_avtp_transport_t wrapping it.

requirements.title: bind() binds a UDP socket to a local address
requirements.text: rcp_udp_avtp_transport_bind() shall create a UDP socket and bind() it to the given addr:port, binding INADDR_ANY when addr is NULL or empty.

requirements.title: ok() distinguishes success from a socket/connect/bind failure
requirements.text: rcp_udp_avtp_transport_ok() shall return true only for a transport whose underlying socket was created and (for dial()) connected, or (for bind()) bound, successfully.

requirements.title: port()/addr_string() report the transport's own bound local address
requirements.text: rcp_udp_avtp_transport_port() and rcp_udp_avtp_transport_addr_string() shall report the local port/address the transport's own socket is actually bound to, including an OS-assigned ephemeral port after port 0 was requested.

requirements.title: dialed-mode send()/recv() round trip over loopback
requirements.text: A frame sent by a dialed transport shall be received, unmodified, by a bound transport's recv() listening on that same peer address.

requirements.title: bound-mode recv() learns the peer from the received datagram
requirements.text: A bound transport's recv() shall record the sending address of each received datagram as the peer its own subsequent send() calls target.

requirements.title: bound-mode send() before a peer is learned returns RCP_ERR_BUSY
requirements.text: A bound transport's send() shall return RCP_ERR_BUSY, without sending, until its own recv() has learned a peer address.

requirements.title: bound-mode send() after learning a peer delivers to it
requirements.text: Once a bound transport's recv() has learned a peer address, its own subsequent send() calls shall deliver to that address.

requirements.title: recv() returns RCP_ERR_TIMEOUT once the context deadline elapses
requirements.text: recv() shall return RCP_ERR_TIMEOUT once the calling context's deadline elapses with no datagram received.

requirements.title: recv() into a too-small buffer returns RCP_ERR_BUSY
requirements.text: recv() shall return RCP_ERR_BUSY, without writing into the caller's buffer, when a received datagram's length exceeds the supplied buffer capacity; the oversized datagram itself is not retrievable afterward, matching UDP's own no-guaranteed-delivery contract.

requirements.title: send()/recv() return RCP_ERR_CLOSED once close() has been called
requirements.text: Once close() has been called on a transport, its own send() and recv() shall both return RCP_ERR_CLOSED.

requirements.title: close() unblocks a concurrent in-progress recv()
requirements.text: Calling close() on a transport while a different thread is blocked inside that same transport's recv() shall cause that recv() call to return RCP_ERR_CLOSED without the underlying socket being invalidated out from under it.

requirements.title: time_sync_supported is recorded on the returned transport
requirements.text: The time_sync_supported value passed to rcp_udp_avtp_transport_dial()/_bind() shall be recorded on the returned transport's own base.time_sync_supported field.

requirements.title: Windows stub: ok() false and every operation fails without crashing
requirements.text: On a platform with no winsock implementation, dial()/bind() shall return a non-NULL transport whose ok() reports false and whose send()/recv() return RCP_ERR_CLOSED without crashing.

requirements.title: Keeper re-evaluates every registered stream periodically
requirements.text: rcp_watchdog_keeper_t shall re-run rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate() for every registered stream at the configured poll interval.

requirements.title: Elapsed time measured from the last kick
requirements.text: The elapsed_since_last_kick_ms argument passed to rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate() shall be the time since the stream's most recent kick (or since Keeper construction if never kicked).

requirements.title: kick() resets a stream's elapsed-since-last-kick clock
requirements.text: rcp_watchdog_keeper_kick() shall reset the named stream's last-kick time to the current time, and shall return false without changing any state if the stream was not registered.

requirements.title: status() returns the most recently computed result
requirements.text: rcp_watchdog_keeper_status() shall return the rcp_e2e_wd_result_t most recently computed for the named stream.

requirements.title: status() returns an all-false result for an unregistered stream
requirements.text: rcp_watchdog_keeper_status() shall return an rcp_e2e_wd_result_t with every field false for a stream_id not registered with the Keeper.

requirements.title: Callback fires on every result change
requirements.text: The event callback shall be invoked with the new rcp_e2e_wd_result_t whenever a stream's computed watchdog result changes.

requirements.title: Close stops the background thread
requirements.text: Keeper::close() shall cause the background re-evaluation thread to terminate without hanging, and shall be idempotent.

requirements.title: A disabled watchdog never overflows
requirements.text: A stream registered with rx_wd_enable == false shall never report overflowed == true, regardless of elapsed time since its last kick.

requirements.title: Construction establishes each stream's initial verdict synchronously
requirements.text: rcp_watchdog_keeper_new() shall compute each registered stream's initial rcp_e2e_wd_result_t before returning, so rcp_watchdog_keeper_status() never observes a stale placeholder for an already-registered stream.

requirements.title: rcp_wallclock_ms() returns wall-clock epoch milliseconds
requirements.text: rcp_wallclock_ms() shall return the number of milliseconds elapsed since the Unix epoch, per the host's wall-clock (calendar) time source.

requirements.title: relay_protocol_string() returns a unique name per protocol
requirements.text: relay_protocol_string() shall return a unique, non-empty string for each defined relay_protocol_t constant, matching the RELAY spec's protocol identifier names (e.g. "RCP").

requirements.title: relay_message_t lifecycle: init, free, set_id are safe and non-leaking
requirements.text: relay_message_init() shall zero a relay_message_t to a safely-freeable state; relay_message_free() shall release all owned fields (id, payload, meta) and be safe to call repeatedly; relay_message_set_id() shall deep-copy the given id, replacing (and freeing) any prior value.

requirements.title: relay_message_t meta map: set upserts, get looks up, both deep-copy
requirements.text: relay_message_set_meta() shall deep-copy key and value, replacing any existing entry with the same key rather than appending a duplicate; relay_message_get_meta() shall return the value for a given key, or NULL if absent.

requirements.title: rcp_message_to_request() maps a Message to a protocol-native request per §15.7.5
requirements.text: rcp_message_to_request() shall pack a relay_message_t's payload and meta fields into a protocol-native request for the given rcp_adapt_op_t, per this module's own per-operation field table, addressed to the given byte_bus_id (or, for RCP_ADAPT_OP_DISCOVERY, framed as a full NTSCF AVTPDU addressed via requester_stream_id) and self-identified by the given transaction_num, reporting RCP_ADAPT_ERR_ENCODE on any packing failure.

requirements.title: rcp_response_to_message() maps a protocol-native response to a Message per §15.7.5
requirements.text: rcp_response_to_message() shall unpack a protocol-native response frame for the given rcp_adapt_op_t into a relay_message_t, per this module's own per-operation field table, validating the frame decodes for the expected byte_bus_id and reporting RCP_ADAPT_ERR_DECODE otherwise.

requirements.title: rcp_adapt_op_kind()/_string()/_from_string() classify and round-trip every operation
requirements.text: rcp_adapt_op_kind() shall report the endpoint-type family (rcp_adapt_ep_kind_t) each rcp_adapt_op_t value belongs to; rcp_adapt_op_string() shall return a unique, non-empty canonical name for each defined rcp_adapt_op_t value; rcp_adapt_op_from_string() shall parse that name back to the same value, and shall report false for any unrecognized or NULL name.

requirements.title: Adapter send() maps a message to a request for the bound op and transmits it, discarding any reply
requirements.text: The relay Caller adapter's send() shall resolve the operation named by the given message's meta["rcp.adapt.op"], fail with RCP_ADAPT_ERR_ENCODE if that operation's rcp_adapt_op_kind() does not match the adapter's own bound kind, otherwise pack and transmit the corresponding request via the wrapped rcp_avtp_transport_t without waiting for a reply.

requirements.title: Adapter call() maps a request, transmits it, and maps the one reply frame back
requirements.text: The relay Caller adapter's call() shall perform the same operation resolution and request packing as send(), transmit the request, block (subject to ctx) for exactly one reply frame from the wrapped transport, and on success map that frame back to *out via rcp_response_to_message().

requirements.title: Adapter subscribe() reports not-supported: no native TC18 periodic status stream exists
requirements.text: The relay Caller adapter's subscribe() shall always return RCP_ADAPT_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED, since TC18 defines no generic periodic Status-equivalent stream for any endpoint type to forward.

requirements.title: rcp_adapt_strerror() returns a unique human-readable message
requirements.text: rcp_adapt_strerror() shall return a unique, non-empty message for each defined rcp_adapt_errc_t constant.

requirements.title: rcp_adapt() binds a transport/address/kind without blocking or connecting
requirements.text: rcp_adapt() shall retain the given rcp_avtp_transport_t and return a relay Caller bound to the given byte_bus_id, local_stream_id, and endpoint-type kind immediately, without blocking or transmitting any traffic itself.

requirements.title: RCP_SPEC_VERSION aliases RELAY_SPEC_VERSION
requirements.text: RCP_SPEC_VERSION shall be defined and shall equal RELAY_SPEC_VERSION, per the RELAY spec's required package-level SpecVersion export (§17 requirement 12, §19.4).

requirements.title: relay_strerror() returns unique human-readable message
requirements.text: relay_strerror() shall return a unique, non-empty message for each defined relay_errc_t constant.

requirements.title: version command emits a schema-conformant document
requirements.text: rcp_cli_run() shall, given the 'version' command, print a document (JSON or text per --format) containing the tool name, RCP_VERSION, RELAY_SPEC_VERSION, and language/runtime fields, conforming to RELAY spec/schemas/cli-version.json.

requirements.title: capabilities command emits a schema-conformant document
requirements.text: rcp_cli_run() shall, given the 'capabilities' command, always print a JSON document listing the tool's implemented commands (including at least version/capabilities/status), transports, interfaces, and adapt status, conforming to RELAY spec/schemas/cli-capabilities.json.

requirements.title: status command emits a schema-conformant document
requirements.text: rcp_cli_run() shall, given the 'status' command, print a document (JSON or text per --format) containing tool/version/healthy/connected/endpoint/details fields, conforming to RELAY spec/schemas/cli-status.json, and shall return exit code 0 when healthy.

requirements.title: Unknown command or missing argument returns exit code 2
requirements.text: rcp_cli_run() shall return RCP_CLI_INVALID_ARGS (2) for an empty argument list, an unrecognized command, or an unrecognized/incomplete --format value, per RELAY spec §11.3 exit code conventions.

requirements.title: --format text|json selects the document encoding
requirements.text: rcp_cli_run() shall default to text output when --format is absent, honor --format json / --format text when present, and reject any other --format value.

requirements.title: CLI entry point forwards process arguments to rcp_cli_run()
requirements.text: The c-rcp executable's main() shall forward argv[1..argc) and stdout/stderr to rcp_cli_run() unmodified and return its exit code, per the RELAY spec's CLI contract (§11.3).

requirements.title: Gauge/counter sink implementations accept a metric without side effects beyond recording
requirements.text: A conforming rcp_metrics_sink_vtable_t::record_gauge/record_counter implementation shall have no observable side effect beyond whatever bookkeeping it documents (e.g. InMemorySink's are no-ops).

requirements.title: Announcer destroy dispatches through its vtable
requirements.text: rcp_mdns_announcer_destroy() shall invoke the announcer's vtable destroy() function and shall be a no-op when passed NULL.

requirements.title: rcp_mdns_discoverer_destroy() dispatches to the discoverer's own vtable destroy function
requirements.text: rcp_mdns_discoverer_destroy(d) shall be a safe no-op when d is NULL; otherwise it shall call d's own vtable destroy function, so every concrete discoverer implementation (e.g. the static discoverer) releases exactly the resources it itself owns.

requirements.title: rcp_mdns_static_discoverer_new() builds a discoverer over a fixed, caller-supplied record set
requirements.text: rcp_mdns_static_discoverer_new(records, count) shall allocate a discoverer that reports exactly the count caller-supplied records (copied by value) as already-discovered, requiring no network activity; it shall return NULL on allocation failure.

requirements.title: Relay caller retain increments refcount and returns the same pointer
requirements.text: rcp_relay_caller_retain() shall increment the caller's refcount and return the same pointer passed in, and shall be a no-op returning NULL when passed NULL.

requirements.title: Message channel reports its closed state
requirements.text: relay_message_channel_is_closed() shall report whether the channel has been closed, reflecting the state set by its close operation.

requirements.title: Span duration is computed as end minus start
requirements.text: rcp_span_duration_ms() shall return span->end_ms - span->start_ms.

requirements.title: rcp_noop_metrics_sink() returns a sink that discards everything recorded to it
requirements.text: rcp_noop_metrics_sink() shall return a rcp_metrics_sink_t whose span/gauge/counter recording functions all discard their arguments without side effects.

requirements.title: rcp_in_memory_sink_new() allocates an empty in-memory span sink
requirements.text: rcp_in_memory_sink_new() shall return a heap-allocated rcp_in_memory_sink_t with no spans recorded and its own mutex initialized, or NULL on allocation failure.

requirements.title: rcp_in_memory_sink_as_sink() adapts an in-memory sink to the generic sink interface
requirements.text: rcp_in_memory_sink_as_sink(s) shall return a rcp_metrics_sink_t whose vtable records spans into s (and discards gauges/counters) and whose ctx is s.

requirements.title: rcp_in_memory_sink_span_count() reports the number of spans recorded so far
requirements.text: rcp_in_memory_sink_span_count(s) shall return the number of spans recorded into s since its creation.

requirements.title: rcp_in_memory_sink_spans() copies up to cap recorded spans and returns the true count
requirements.text: rcp_in_memory_sink_spans(s, out, cap) shall copy min(recorded_count, cap) recorded spans into out, in recording order, and return the true recorded count (which may exceed cap, signalling truncation to the caller).

requirements.title: rcp_in_memory_sink_destroy() releases every owned resource
requirements.text: rcp_in_memory_sink_destroy(s) shall be a safe no-op when s is NULL; otherwise it shall destroy s's mutex and free its recorded-spans array before freeing s itself.

requirements.title: Native errors report equivalence to RELAY common-error sentinels
requirements.text: rcp_errc_to_relay_errc() shall report true and the corresponding relay_errc_t for RCP_ERR_CLOSED and RCP_ERR_TIMEOUT, and false for RCP_OK and any rcp_errc_t value with no RELAY common-error equivalent.

requirements.title: NTSCF AVTP subtype value
requirements.text: The AVTPDU subtype byte (offset 0) of every NTSCF header shall equal RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_NTSCF (0x82), the IEEE 1722 base-standard subtype for the Non-Time-Synchronous Control Format.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 6 ("NTSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1130-1138; example wire trace confirming subtype=0x82, TC18.txt L4247-4258

requirements.title: TSCF AVTP subtype value
requirements.text: The AVTPDU subtype byte (offset 0) of every TSCF header shall equal RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_TSCF (0x05), the IEEE 1722 base-standard subtype for the Time-Synchronous Control Format.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 5 ("TSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1121-1128; example wire trace confirming subtype=0x05, TC18.txt L4210-4222

requirements.title: NTSCF header round-trip
requirements.text: rcp_avtp_decode_ntscf() applied to the output of rcp_avtp_encode_ntscf() shall recover the original sv, version, sequence_num, stream_id, and payload bytes unchanged.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 6 ("NTSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1130-1138

requirements.title: TSCF header round-trip
requirements.text: rcp_avtp_decode_tscf() applied to the output of rcp_avtp_encode_tscf() shall recover the original sv, version, mr, tv, tu, sequence_num, stream_id, avtp_timestamp, and payload bytes unchanged.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 5 ("TSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1121-1128

requirements.title: NTSCF decode rejects a frame shorter than the fixed header
requirements.text: rcp_avtp_decode_ntscf() shall return RCP_AVTP_ERR_SHORT_FRAME if given fewer than RCP_AVTP_NTSCF_HEADER_LEN bytes.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 6's fixed header length ("NTSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1130-1138

requirements.title: TSCF decode rejects a frame shorter than the fixed header
requirements.text: rcp_avtp_decode_tscf() shall return RCP_AVTP_ERR_SHORT_FRAME if given fewer than RCP_AVTP_TSCF_HEADER_LEN bytes.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 5's fixed header length ("TSCF-Header Version 0"), TC18.txt L1121-1128

requirements.title: NTSCF decode rejects a mismatched subtype
requirements.text: rcp_avtp_decode_ntscf() shall return RCP_AVTP_ERR_BAD_SUBTYPE if byte 0 of the input is not RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_NTSCF, including when it is RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_TSCF.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 (NTSCF subtype=0x82 vs TSCF subtype=0x05 distinguish the two header forms), TC18.txt L1118-1138

requirements.title: TSCF decode rejects a mismatched subtype
requirements.text: rcp_avtp_decode_tscf() shall return RCP_AVTP_ERR_BAD_SUBTYPE if byte 0 of the input is not RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_TSCF, including when it is RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_NTSCF.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 (NTSCF subtype=0x82 vs TSCF subtype=0x05 distinguish the two header forms), TC18.txt L1118-1138

requirements.title: Decoders reject a declared payload length exceeding the supplied buffer
requirements.text: rcp_avtp_decode_ntscf() and rcp_avtp_decode_tscf() shall return RCP_AVTP_ERR_SHORT_FRAME whenever the header's declared data-length field describes a payload extending past the end of the supplied buffer.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figures 5/6's ntscf_data_length/tscf_data_length header fields, TC18.txt L1121-1138; example wire trace showing ntscf_data_length header field, TC18.txt L4247-4251

requirements.title: stream_id packs to and unpacks from its 64-bit on-wire form
requirements.text: rcp_stream_id_from_u64(rcp_stream_id_to_u64(id)) shall recover a stream_id equal (per rcp_stream_id_equal()) to the original id for any MAC and unique_id, and rcp_stream_id_make() shall construct a stream_id from a given MAC and unique_id unchanged.

requirements.title: stream_id equality compares both MAC and unique_id
requirements.text: rcp_stream_id_equal() shall return false if either the MAC or the unique_id differs between its two arguments, and true only if both match.

requirements.title: AVTP address equality requires a matching byte_bus_id, not just stream_id
requirements.text: rcp_avtp_addr_equal() shall return false for two addresses that share a stream_id but differ in byte_bus_id, and true only when both the stream_id and byte_bus_id match.

requirements.title: rcp_avtp_peek_subtype() reads the subtype byte without a full header
requirements.text: rcp_avtp_peek_subtype() shall report the AVTPDU's subtype byte (offset 0) from a buffer as short as 1 byte, and shall return RCP_AVTP_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a zero-length buffer.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 (subtype is byte 0 of both NTSCF Figure 6 and TSCF Figure 5), TC18.txt L1118-1138

requirements.title: TSCF-without-time-sync is dropped under the default (DROP) policy
requirements.text: rcp_avtp_should_drop_tscf() shall return true if and only if subtype equals RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_TSCF, server_time_sync_supported is false, and unsupported_time_sync_policy equals RCP_AVTP_TSCF_FALLBACK_DROP (this function's own default/original disposition, matching every pre-issue-#431 caller); it shall return false for RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_NTSCF regardless of server_time_sync_supported or policy, and false for RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_TSCF when server_time_sync_supported is true. As of issue #431 (REQ-AVTP-021), the drop is no longer unconditional -- a caller may instead pass RCP_AVTP_TSCF_FALLBACK_IGNORE per TC18 §13.3's own configurable alternative; this entry pins the unchanged DROP-policy behavior specifically.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 ("In case time-synchronization is not supported, AVTPDUs having a TSCF header are dropped, and no response send."), TC18.txt L1140

requirements.title: rcp_avtp_strerror() returns a unique human-readable message
requirements.text: rcp_avtp_strerror() shall return a unique, non-empty message for each defined rcp_avtp_errc_t constant, including RCP_AVTP_OK.

requirements.title: AVTP transport refcounting releases exactly at zero
requirements.text: rcp_avtp_transport_retain() shall increment a transport's refcount and return the same pointer; rcp_avtp_transport_release() shall invoke the transport's destroy() callback only once its refcount reaches zero, and never before.

requirements.title: Loopback transport delivers frames in FIFO order
requirements.text: A frame enqueued via the loopback transport's send() shall be returned by a subsequent recv() unchanged and in the same relative order as other queued frames.

requirements.title: Loopback transport recv() honors a context deadline
requirements.text: The loopback transport's recv() shall return RCP_ERR_TIMEOUT if no frame becomes available before the given rcp_context_t's deadline elapses.

requirements.title: Loopback transport rejects operations after close()
requirements.text: After the loopback transport's close() has been called, send() shall return RCP_ERR_CLOSED, and recv() shall return RCP_ERR_CLOSED once any already-queued frames are exhausted.

requirements.title: Loopback transport enforces its configured queue capacity
requirements.text: The loopback transport's send() shall return RCP_ERR_BUSY once the number of undelivered queued frames reaches the capacity given to rcp_avtp_loopback_transport_new().

requirements.title: TSCF-without-time-sync ignore-vs-drop is caller-configurable (§13.3)
requirements.text: As of issue #431, rcp_avtp_should_drop_tscf() and rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() shall each accept an rcp_avtp_tscf_fallback_t unsupported_time_sync_policy parameter governing a TSCF-headed AVTPDU received while server_time_sync_supported is false: RCP_AVTP_TSCF_FALLBACK_DROP (value 0, the default for every rcp_mock_server_t and the behavior of every caller predating this parameter) shall drop the frame; RCP_AVTP_TSCF_FALLBACK_IGNORE shall NOT drop it, and rcp_mock_server_dispatch_tscf()'s own dispatch_plain_inner() helper shall then admit the request with its presentation-time gate suppressed (tv forced false before rcp_server_endpoint_admit()), matching TC18 §13.3's own "executed as if no presentation time were included" wording. rcp_mock_server_set_tscf_unsupported_time_sync_policy() sets this policy on an rcp_mock_server_t; both mock.c call sites of rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() (dispatch_plain_inner(), rcp_mock_server_dispatch_multi_response()) thread it through. This policy has no effect on HW_UNCONFIGURED's/HW_CONFIGURED's own separate, unconditional (time-sync-independent) TSCF-drop rules.
requirements.tc18: §13.3 ("Requests may come within an AVTPDU with a presentation time (i.e. TSCF header). In case the RC Server does not support time synchronization, the presentation time shall be ignored, and the request(s) executed as if no presentation time were included or dropped depending on the configuration of the RC Server."), TC18.txt L4035-4038

requirements.title: TSCF reserved-bytes-all-zero queues as NTSCF or drops, per configuration (§13.3)
requirements.text: rcp_avtp_decode_tscf() shall populate rcp_avtp_tscf_header_t's own reserved0 (wire bytes 16-19) and reserved1 (wire bytes 22-23) fields from the decoded frame; rcp_avtp_tscf_reserved_all_zero() shall return true iff both are zero. rcp_mock_server_dispatch_tscf() shall accept a caller-supplied tscf_reserved_all_zero boolean (the caller's own rcp_avtp_tscf_reserved_all_zero() result against a real decoded TSCF header) and, whenever avtp_subtype is RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_TSCF and tscf_reserved_all_zero is true, shall consult srv's own rcp_avtp_tscf_fallback_t policy (rcp_mock_server_set_tscf_unsupported_time_sync_policy(), the same shared policy knob REQ-AVTP-021 uses): RCP_AVTP_TSCF_FALLBACK_DROP shall drop the frame (RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_DROPPED, *out_response left zeroed); RCP_AVTP_TSCF_FALLBACK_IGNORE shall process the frame as if avtp_subtype had genuinely been RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_NTSCF all along -- a full substitution of both avtp_subtype and tv, not merely a suppressed presentation-time gate, matching this rule's own literal "queued as if the header was in NTSCF format" wording (distinct from REQ-AVTP-021's own narrower "ignore only the presentation time" wording for the unsupported-time-sync rule).
requirements.tc18: §13.3 ("If the reserved bytes in the header are all zero, then the request shall be queued as if the header was in NTSCF format or dropped, depending on configuration."), TC18.txt L4039-4040

requirements.title: TSCF tu=1 (uncertain timestamp) is treated identically to tu=0 (§13.3)
requirements.text: No admission or dispatch function in this codebase (rcp_server_endpoint_admit(), rcp_mock_server_dispatch_tscf(), and every sibling dispatch entry point) shall take a tu parameter or otherwise branch on rcp_avtp_tscf_header_t's own tu field -- there is no separate tu=1 code path to diverge from tu=0's, which is this library's own honestly-achievable form of TC18's "this shall be executed as if tu = 0" rule. rcp_avtp_decode_tscf() shall still faithfully decode tu into out_hdr for a caller's own inspection. test_avtp.c's/test_mock.c's own REQ-AVTP-023 tests dispatch two byte-identical requests differing only in their own wire tu bit and assert byte-identical dispatch outcomes, directly observing this deliberate equivalence rather than merely inferring it from tu's absence as a parameter.
requirements.tc18: §13.3 ("In case the time stamp is uncertain (i.e. tu = 1), then this shall be executed as if tu = 0."), TC18.txt L4040-4041

requirements.title: rcp_acf_strerror() returns a unique human-readable message
requirements.text: rcp_acf_strerror() shall return a unique, non-empty message for each defined rcp_acf_errc_t constant, including RCP_ACF_OK.

requirements.title: Response classification selects among Acknowledge/Write/Read/Error
requirements.text: rcp_acf_classify_response() shall return RCP_ACF_RESP_ACKNOWLEDGE whenever hdr->evt equals RCP_ACF_EVT_ACKNOWLEDGE (0xF), regardless of hdr->op or hdr->err, per TC18 Table 15/§11.3.1 -- a rejected Acknowledge (err=1) is still an Acknowledge, not an Error Response. Otherwise it shall return RCP_ACF_RESP_ERROR whenever hdr->err is set regardless of hdr->op, and otherwise shall return RCP_ACF_RESP_WRITE for RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE, RCP_ACF_RESP_READ for RCP_ACF_OP_READ, and RCP_ACF_RESP_ACKNOWLEDGE for RCP_ACF_OP_NONE (an encode-only value never produced by decode).

requirements.title: Encoders write the correct acf_msg_type regardless of the caller-supplied header
requirements.text: rcp_acf_encode_abb() shall write RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_ABB and rcp_acf_encode_gbb() shall write RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_GBB at offset 0 of the encoded message, independent of any acf_msg_type value the caller's header struct happens to carry.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Table 4 ("acf_msg_type 0x0E (ABB message)"), TC18.txt L1152-1153; ACF_GBB acf_msg_type=0x0D, e.g. TC18.txt L1447

requirements.title: Decoders reject a frame shorter than the fixed header
requirements.text: rcp_acf_decode_abb() shall return RCP_ACF_ERR_SHORT_FRAME if given fewer than RCP_ACF_ABB_HEADER_LEN bytes, and rcp_acf_decode_gbb() shall return RCP_ACF_ERR_SHORT_FRAME if given fewer than RCP_ACF_GBB_HEADER_LEN bytes.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Figure 7's fixed byte_message_info header, TC18.txt L1142-1149

requirements.title: acf_msg_length is recomputed from the actual payload length on encode
requirements.text: rcp_acf_encode_abb() and rcp_acf_encode_gbb() shall derive the encoded acf_msg_length field from payload_len, ignoring any acf_msg_length value present in the caller-supplied header.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Table 4 ("acf_msg_length: number of quadlets of data contained in this message"), TC18.txt L1154

requirements.title: ACF_ABB decode rejects a mismatched acf_msg_type
requirements.text: rcp_acf_decode_abb() shall return RCP_ACF_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE if byte 0 of the input is not RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_ABB, including when it is RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_GBB.
requirements.tc18: ABB acf_msg_type=0x0E vs GBB acf_msg_type=0x0D distinguish the two ACF message forms, TC18.txt L1153,L1447

requirements.title: ACF_GBB decode rejects a mismatched acf_msg_type
requirements.text: rcp_acf_decode_gbb() shall return RCP_ACF_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE if byte 0 of the input is not RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_GBB, including when it is RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_ABB.
requirements.tc18: ABB acf_msg_type=0x0E vs GBB acf_msg_type=0x0D distinguish the two ACF message forms, TC18.txt L1153,L1447

requirements.title: Decoders reject a declared payload length exceeding the supplied buffer
requirements.text: rcp_acf_decode_abb() and rcp_acf_decode_gbb() shall return RCP_ACF_ERR_SHORT_FRAME whenever the header's declared acf_msg_length describes a payload extending past the end of the supplied buffer.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Table 4's acf_msg_length field, TC18.txt L1154

requirements.title: byte_message_info header round-trip
requirements.text: rcp_acf_decode_abb() applied to the output of rcp_acf_encode_abb(), and rcp_acf_decode_gbb() applied to the output of rcp_acf_encode_gbb(), shall each recover the original byte_bus_id, evt, op, transaction_num, and payload bytes unchanged, and rcp_acf_decode_gbb() shall additionally recover the original message_timestamp unchanged whenever mtv indicates a valid timestamp.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Figure 7/Table 4's byte_message_info fields, TC18.txt L1142-1170

requirements.title: ACF_GBB encode zeroes the timestamp region for an untimed message
requirements.text: rcp_acf_encode_gbb() shall write an all-zero message_timestamp region whenever hdr->info.mtv equals RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED, regardless of the value held in hdr->message_timestamp.

requirements.title: Timestamp-validity folding rule
requirements.text: rcp_acf_gbb_is_timed() shall return true only when info.mtv equals RCP_ACF_MTV_VALID; it shall return false for RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED, the only other wire state -- mtv is a single wire bit (TC18 Table 4) with no third 'uncertain' state on the wire. An earlier revision of this header modeled such a state (RCP_ACF_MTV_UNCERTAIN) in a 2-bit field of its own invention that had no real TC18 encoding, and it has since been removed. A caller that needs to represent 'timestamp present but not trustworthy' must fold that into RCP_ACF_MTV_UNTIMED, the same not-confidently-timed treatment rcp_acf_gbb_is_timed() already gives it.

requirements.title: rcp_acf_peek_msg_type() reads the acf_msg_type byte without a full header decode
requirements.text: rcp_acf_peek_msg_type() shall report the ACF message's acf_msg_type byte (offset 0) from a buffer as short as 1 byte, and shall return RCP_ACF_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a zero-length buffer.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Figure 7 (acf_msg_type is byte 0 of byte_message_info), TC18.txt L1142-1153

requirements.title: Encoded ACF_ABB/ACF_GBB message length matches header length plus payload
requirements.text: rcp_acf_encode_abb() shall produce a frame of exactly RCP_ACF_ABB_HEADER_LEN + payload_len bytes, and rcp_acf_encode_gbb() shall produce a frame of exactly RCP_ACF_GBB_HEADER_LEN + payload_len bytes, with RCP_ACF_GBB_HEADER_LEN equal to RCP_ACF_ABB_HEADER_LEN plus the 8-byte message_timestamp field.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Figure 7 (ABB byte_message_info, no timestamp), TC18.txt L1142-1149; ACF_GBB's additional 8-byte message_timestamp, e.g. TC18.txt L1447-1451

requirements.title: byte_message_info round-trips its remaining flag and count fields unchanged
requirements.text: rcp_acf_decode_abb() and rcp_acf_decode_gbb() shall recover the original pad, hs, cs, rsp, err, ms, and read_size_or_segment_num field values unchanged from what rcp_acf_encode_abb()/rcp_acf_encode_gbb() encoded.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Figure 7/Table 4's byte_message_info fields, TC18.txt L1142-1170

requirements.title: rcp_acf_pack_header()/rcp_acf_unpack_header() implement byte_message_info per TC18 Table 4 bit-for-bit
requirements.text: rcp_acf_pack_header() and rcp_acf_unpack_header() shall pack/unpack the 8-octet byte_message_info header exactly per the governing specification Figure 7/Table 4 bit layout (acf_msg_type/acf_msg_length sharing octets 0-1, pad/mtv/byte_bus_id[10:8] in octet 2, byte_bus_id[7:0] in octet 3, evt/hs/cs in octet 4, transaction_num in octet 5, op/rsp/err/ms/read_size_or_segment_num[11:8] in octet 6, read_size_or_segment_num[7:0] in octet 7), and rcp_acf_pad_len() shall compute the zero-pad octet count needed to bring a given unpadded length up to a whole number of quadlets.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Figure 7 / Table 4 ("ABB message standard request" / "Usage of ABB message for standard requests"), TC18.txt L1142-1170

requirements.title: Lifecycle states have their defined on-wire byte values
requirements.text: RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED, RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED, and RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED shall have the numeric values 0x00, 0x55, and 0xAA respectively.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2 Table 36, svr_lifecycle_state row ("0x00: HW_UNCONFIGURED / 0x55: HW_CONFIGURED / 0xAA: RCP_CONFIGURED"), TC18.txt L4388-4390 -- corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256): the prior citation (§12.3, TC18.txt L2063) pointed only to the sentence naming the three states, not to where their numeric wire values are actually defined; code itself (include/rcp/lifecycle.h:122-124) was always correct against the right source, only the citation was wrong

requirements.title: HW_CFG_INCONSISTENT triggers on a missing HW pin mapping
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_check_hw_cfg() shall return RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_HW_CFG_INCONSISTENT whenever any endpoint with ep_used set has hw_pin_mapped unset, regardless of the state of any other endpoint.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("All EPs configured to be used (ep_used set to 1) match to pin mapping in the HW_config... If not plausible the request will be rejected and an error response sent with HW_CFG_INCONSITENT."), TC18.txt L2547-2550

requirements.title: HW_CFG_INCONSISTENT triggers on a missing configured request stream
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_check_hw_cfg() shall return RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_HW_CFG_INCONSISTENT whenever any endpoint with ep_used set has has_request_stream unset.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("All EPs configured to be used have a configuration for the request queue... If not plausible the request will be rejected and an error response sent with HW_CFG_INCONSITENT."), TC18.txt L2548-2550

requirements.title: HW_CFG_INCONSISTENT does not trigger when every used endpoint is plausibly configured
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_check_hw_cfg() shall return RCP_LIFECYCLE_OK when every endpoint with ep_used set has both hw_pin_mapped and has_request_stream set, ignoring endpoints with ep_used unset, and shall treat a NULL snapshot as inconsistent rather than vacuously plausible.
requirements.tc18: §13.1 ("An endpoint may be used or not used in a specific instantiation of a RC Server"), TC18.txt L3900

requirements.title: RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT triggers on a missing stream/byte_bus_id association
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_check_rcp_cfg() shall return RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT whenever any endpoint with ep_used set has has_stream_assoc unset.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Each EP used has at least one stream_id/byte_bus_id association... If not plausible the request will be rejected and an error response sent with RCP_CFG_INCONSITENT"), TC18.txt L2568-2572

requirements.title: RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT triggers on a request stream missing its response stream
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_check_rcp_cfg() shall return RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT whenever any request stream with configured set has has_response_stream unset.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Each response stream configured is assigned to at least one request stream... If not plausible the request will be rejected and an error response sent with RCP_CFG_INCONSITENT"), TC18.txt L2570-2572

requirements.title: RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT does not trigger when every used endpoint and configured request stream is plausibly associated
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_check_rcp_cfg() shall return RCP_LIFECYCLE_OK when every endpoint with ep_used set has has_stream_assoc set and every request stream with configured set has has_response_stream set, and shall treat a NULL snapshot as inconsistent rather than vacuously plausible.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Only if the configuration so far is plausible the state will be advanced. Plausibility check contains a check that: Each EP used has at least one stream_id/byte_bus_id association..."), TC18.txt L2566-2568

requirements.title: HW_UNCONFIGURED to HW_CONFIGURED is gated by the HW_CFG_INCONSISTENT check
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_transition() shall move *state from RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED to RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED only when rcp_lifecycle_check_hw_cfg() returns RCP_LIFECYCLE_OK for the supplied snapshot, and shall otherwise leave *state unchanged and return the check's RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_HW_CFG_INCONSISTENT result.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("...the life-cycle state can be advanced to HW_CONFIGURED... Only if the configuration so far is plausible the state will be advanced... If not plausible the request will be rejected and an error response sent with HW_CFG_INCONSITENT."), TC18.txt L2544-2550

requirements.title: HW_CONFIGURED to RCP_CONFIGURED is gated by the RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT check
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_transition() shall move *state from RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED to RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED only when rcp_lifecycle_check_rcp_cfg() returns RCP_LIFECYCLE_OK for the supplied snapshot, and shall otherwise leave *state unchanged and return the check's RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT result.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("...the life-cycle state can be advanced to RCP_CONFIGURED... Only if the configuration so far is plausible the state will be advanced... If not plausible the request will be rejected and an error response sent with RCP_CFG_INCONSITENT"), TC18.txt L2562-2572

requirements.title: HW_CONFIGURED to HW_UNCONFIGURED demotion is unconditional
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_transition() shall move *state from RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED to RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED and return RCP_LIFECYCLE_OK regardless of the supplied snapshot, including a NULL snapshot.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Besides advancing the state it is also possible to go back to state HW_UNCONFIGURED via a write request to the server functional configuration entry svr_lifecycle_state." -- no plausibility gate is described for this direction), TC18.txt L2574-2577

requirements.title: RCP_CONFIGURED to HW_UNCONFIGURED full-reset demotion is unconditional
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_transition() shall move *state from RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED to RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED and return RCP_LIFECYCLE_OK regardless of the supplied snapshot, including a NULL snapshot.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Besides advancing the state it is also possible to go back to state HW_UNCONFIGURED via a write request..."), TC18.txt L2574-2577 -- NOTE: TC18's Figure 17 state-transition chart additionally gates this specific demotion on all other EPs being idle ("other EPs are not Idle -> send error response EPs_NOT_IDLE", TC18.txt L2501-2502); that gate is a known, separately-tracked gap, see REQ-LIFECYCLE-022 (not this requirement, which documents the mechanism c-RCP actually implements)

requirements.title: Unmodeled lifecycle transitions are rejected
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_transition() shall return RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_INVALID_TRANSITION and leave *state unchanged for any requested transition other than HW_UNCONFIGURED->HW_CONFIGURED, HW_CONFIGURED->RCP_CONFIGURED, HW_CONFIGURED->HW_UNCONFIGURED, RCP_CONFIGURED->HW_UNCONFIGURED, or a same-state transition -- including HW_UNCONFIGURED->RCP_CONFIGURED and RCP_CONFIGURED->HW_CONFIGURED.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("A request to advance the state directly to RCP_CONFIGURED will be rejected with an error response."), TC18.txt L2545; corroborated by Figure 17's state-transition chart naming no other transitions, TC18.txt L2432-2517

requirements.title: A same-state lifecycle transition is a no-op success
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_transition() shall return RCP_LIFECYCLE_OK and leave *state unchanged whenever target equals the current *state, for all three lifecycle states, regardless of the supplied snapshot.

requirements.title: HW_UNCONFIGURED accepts an ACF_ABB request at the discovery byte_bus_id under NTSCF
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() shall return true for RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED when avtp_subtype is RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_NTSCF, acf_msg_type is RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_ABB, and byte_bus_id equals RCP_LIFECYCLE_DISCOVERY_BYTE_BUS_ID.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("In this state only AVTPDUs having a NTSCF header are accepted... Within the stream only requests ACF_ABB are supported for configuration, and all requests need to be directed to EP0 via the discovery byte_bus_id 0x00."), TC18.txt L2539-2541

requirements.title: HW_UNCONFIGURED silently drops any misaddressed frame, and rejects (with a response) a non-ABB request correctly addressed to EP0
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() shall return RCP_LIFECYCLE_DROP for RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED whenever avtp_subtype is not RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_NTSCF or byte_bus_id does not equal RCP_LIFECYCLE_DISCOVERY_BYTE_BUS_ID. When avtp_subtype is RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_NTSCF and byte_bus_id equals RCP_LIFECYCLE_DISCOVERY_BYTE_BUS_ID but acf_msg_type is not RCP_ACF_MSG_TYPE_ABB, rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() shall instead return RCP_LIFECYCLE_REJECT, not RCP_LIFECYCLE_DROP -- this entry's own original text (predating the REQ-LIFECYCLE-033 fix, which widened rcp_lifecycle_should_accept()'s return type from a boolean to the three-way rcp_lifecycle_accept_t ACCEPT/DROP/REJECT) claimed a uniform silent-drop outcome across all three conditions; the acf_msg_type condition alone, with the other two satisfied, now produces a REJECT with an RCP_ERROR_REQUEST_REJECTED wire response instead, per REQ-LIFECYCLE-033.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("In this state only AVTPDUs having a NTSCF header are accepted... Within the stream only requests ACF_ABB are supported for configuration, and all requests need to be directed to EP0 via the discovery byte_bus_id 0x00."), TC18.txt L2539-2541 -- governs the avtp_subtype and byte_bus_id conditions only (both still produce RCP_LIFECYCLE_DROP); the acf_msg_type condition no longer does, since TC18 §12.7's more specific EP0-scoped rule ("REQUEST_REJECTED", TC18.txt L2830) was found to override §12.3.1.1's general "all other requests are dropped without further response" for exactly the case of a non-ABB message correctly addressed to EP0 -- see REQ-LIFECYCLE-033 (implemented) for the fix and full reconciliation between the two sections.

requirements.title: HW_UNCONFIGURED drops any TSCF-headed frame regardless of time-sync support
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() shall return false for RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED whenever avtp_subtype is RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_TSCF, regardless of the value of time_sync_supported.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("In this state only AVTPDUs having a NTSCF header are accepted and all others are dropped without further response." -- TSCF is one of those "others"), TC18.txt L2539

requirements.title: RCP_CONFIGURED applies the ordinary TSCF/time-sync drop rule; HW_CONFIGURED drops TSCF unconditionally
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() shall return false for RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED whenever rcp_avtp_should_drop_tscf() would return true for the given time_sync_supported and avtp_subtype, and shall otherwise return true for that state. RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED instead drops every TSCF-headed frame unconditionally, regardless of what rcp_avtp_should_drop_tscf() would return -- see REQ-LIFECYCLE-028 for that stricter, separately-tracked rule. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256): this entry's own formal "shall" text and title previously claimed the ordinary rule applied to HW_CONFIGURED too, which the code has never done since REQ-LIFECYCLE-028 landed (src/lifecycle.c:245, `if (avtp_subtype == RCP_AVTP_SUBTYPE_TSCF) return RCP_LIFECYCLE_DROP;`, inside the HW_CONFIGURED branch, unconditional) -- only this entry's own citation footnote acknowledged the divergence in prose; the normative text did not.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 ("In case time-synchronization is not supported, AVTPDUs having a TSCF header are dropped, and no response send."), TC18.txt L1140 -- same general rule as REQ-AVTP-014, now correctly scoped to RCP_CONFIGURED only; TC18 §12.3.1.2 separately specifies HW_CONFIGURED drops TSCF unconditionally regardless of time-sync support, formally tracked at REQ-LIFECYCLE-028

requirements.title: HW_GENERIC fields are writable only via the discovery stream while HW_UNCONFIGURED, and read-only thereafter
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() shall return true for RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC only when state is RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED and writer.via_discovery_stream is true, shall return false for that field kind for any other writer context while still RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED, and shall return false for that field kind unconditionally in both RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED and RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256): this entry's own text previously said HW_UNCONFIGURED writability held "for every writer context", which stopped being true once REQ-LIFECYCLE-026/035's fix (src/lifecycle.c:308) gated it on writer.via_discovery_stream -- the HW_CONFIGURED/RCP_CONFIGURED read-only half of this entry's own text was, and remains, correct.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("In this state access to the HW configuration of the RC Server shall have been concluded and as such all access to the HW_config and EP_generic_config are locked."), TC18.txt L2553-2554; §12.3.1.1 ("All configurations must be run via the stream which was used for discovery."), TC18.txt L2537, the basis for the HW_UNCONFIGURED via_discovery_stream gate (REQ-LIFECYCLE-026/035)

requirements.title: FUNCTIONAL_W fields require an authorized writer once HW_CONFIGURED or RCP_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() shall return false for RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W in RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED for every writer context; shall return true in RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED if and only if writer.via_root_client_ep0 or writer.via_owning_stream is true; and shall return true in RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED if and only if writer.via_root_client_ep0, writer.via_owning_stream, or writer.via_discovery_stream is true -- one condition wider than the RCP_CONFIGURED case. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256): this entry's own text previously claimed HW_CONFIGURED writability held "for every writer context", contradicted by both the code (REQ-LIFECYCLE-030/036's authorization gate, src/lifecycle.c:284-291,311-319) and this project's own test (test_lifecycle.c's test_functional_w_hw_configured_requires_authorization_or_discovery_stream()).
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3 ("...only write access to the EP's functional configurations is allowed via their dedicated stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations or via root client access EP0... Write access to some parameters might be prohibited in this life-cycle state, this is marked by * in the R/W-column of the respective tables."), TC18.txt L2581-2582, L2601-2602; §12.3.1.2 (TC18.txt L2552), the basis for HW_CONFIGURED's wider via_discovery_stream allowance (REQ-LIFECYCLE-030/036)

requirements.title: FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR fields require the same authorized writer as FUNCTIONAL_W while HW_CONFIGURED, and are permanently locked once RCP_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() shall return false for RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR in RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED for every writer context, including one with both via_root_client_ep0 and via_owning_stream set; shall return true unconditionally in RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED; and shall return true in RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED if and only if writer.via_root_client_ep0, writer.via_owning_stream, or writer.via_discovery_stream is true -- the same gate REQ-LIFECYCLE-019 applies to FUNCTIONAL_W. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256): this entry's own text previously claimed unconditional HW_CONFIGURED writability, contradicted by REQ-LIFECYCLE-036's later fix (src/lifecycle.c:321-335), which gated this same branch identically to FUNCTIONAL_W's own HW_CONFIGURED case. The RCP_CONFIGURED permanent-lock half of this entry's own text was, and remains, correct.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3 ("Write access to some parameters might be prohibited in this life-cycle state, this is marked by * in the R/W-column of the respective tables (W*: write prohibited in depending on lifecycle state.)"), TC18.txt L2601-2602 -- TC18's W* marker is general; c-RCP's split into FUNCTIONAL_W (conditionally writable via authorization) versus FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR (unconditionally locked once RCP_CONFIGURED) is this implementation's own refinement of which W* fields fall into which case, not itself named in the cited text

requirements.title: A disabled endpoint queues submitted requests instead of executing them
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_submit() shall return false and append a copy of the submitted request to ep's queue (incrementing the value rcp_server_endpoint_queue_len() reports) whenever ep->ep_enable is false at the time of the call.
requirements.tc18: §13.7's Table 35 (Table 32 in TC18 0.5.1_RC1) ("0x0002.0 ep_enable ... indicating if the endpoint is enabled to executed requests from its request storage"), TC18.txt L4300-4304 -- citation-drift correction: the existing text says "§12.3's Table 32", but §12.3 is TC18's Lifecycle chapter, unrelated; Table 32 (RC1 numbering, Table 35 under the current 0.5.1_RC5 numbering used by the authoritative PDF) is actually defined under §13.7 Types of endpoints (TC18.txt L4293), confirmed against both TC18.txt and a fresh pdftotext extraction of OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf.

requirements.title: An enabled endpoint reports immediate execution without touching its queue
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_submit() shall return true and leave rcp_server_endpoint_queue_len() unchanged whenever ep->ep_enable is true at the time of the call.
requirements.tc18: §13.7's Table 35 (Table 32 in TC18 0.5.1_RC1) ("0x0002.0 ep_enable ... indicating if the endpoint is enabled to executed requests from its request storage"), TC18.txt L4300-4304 -- same citation-drift correction as REQ-SRV-001/003: §12.3 is Lifecycle, not where Table 32/35 lives (§13.7).

requirements.title: Re-enabling an endpoint drains its queued requests in FIFO order
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_drain_one() shall return false and leave the queue untouched while ep->ep_enable is false, and after rcp_server_endpoint_set_enable() sets ep->ep_enable to true, repeated calls to rcp_server_endpoint_drain_one() shall dequeue every previously-queued request in the same order it was submitted, returning false once the queue is empty.
requirements.tc18: §13.7's Table 35 (Table 32 in TC18 0.5.1_RC1) ("0x0002.0 ep_enable ... indicating if the endpoint is enabled to executed requests from its request storage"), TC18.txt L4300-4304 -- same citation-drift correction as REQ-SRV-001/002.

requirements.title: rcp_lifecycle_strerror() returns a unique human-readable message
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_strerror() shall return a distinct, non-empty, non-NULL string for each of RCP_LIFECYCLE_OK, RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_HW_CFG_INCONSISTENT, RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT, and RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_INVALID_TRANSITION.

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_is_ep0() identifies EP0 by index
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_is_ep0() shall return true if and only if ep_index equals RCP_REGMAP_EP0_INDEX.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("all requests need to be directed to EP0 via the discovery byte_bus_id 0x00"), TC18.txt L2163-2164

requirements.title: EP0 shares its index with the discovery byte_bus_id
requirements.text: RCP_REGMAP_EP0_INDEX shall equal RCP_LIFECYCLE_DISCOVERY_BYTE_BUS_ID, since EP0 and the discovery channel are reached through the same address.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("all requests need to be directed to EP0 via the discovery byte_bus_id 0x00"), TC18.txt L2163-2164

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_general_init() zero-initializes with no root client granted
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_general_init() shall set every field of its argument to zero except svr_root_client_index, which it shall set to RCP_REGMAP_NO_ROOT_CLIENT.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2 Table 36 ("svr_root_client_index... 0: no stream has 'root' write access"), TC18.txt L4385-4387

requirements.title: RETIRED -- svr_implemented_options bit assignments are pairwise distinct (citation found incorrect, see REQ-RMAP-030)
requirements.text: RETIRED as of REQ-RMAP-030's primary-source verification milestone. This requirement's own shared citation (§12.9.1.1, TC18.txt L2033-2036, quoting "Optional support of compound requests comes as bundle of...") was checked directly against the primary-source PDF (OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC.pdf, §12.9.1.1, page 64, "Handling multiple requests in incoming messages") and found to be a genuine misattribution: that section is entirely about an RC Server processing multiple ACF-type requests packed into one AVTPDU frame (multicast reception, byte_bus_id/stream_id matching, TSCF/NTSCF header rules) -- it says nothing about svr_implemented_options, feature advertisement, or any bit-pairing rule at all. The six-bit, three-forced-pair grouping this requirement (and its four siblings, REQ-RMAP-005..008) described, and the rcp_regmap_options_group_consistent() function (src/regmap.c) that enforced it, had no TC18 basis and have been removed outright (not deprecated-then-removed; there was no correct behavior to preserve a transition window for). This requirement's own specific claim ("the six RCP_REGMAP_OPT_* bitmask constants shall each occupy a distinct bit position") described an invented layout that no longer exists. The correct behavior -- five independent bits, matching TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 exactly -- is now REQ-RMAP-030's own responsibility; see that entry.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1.1 (citation found incorrect -- see text), TC18.txt L2033-2036

This requirement's own specific claim ("rcp_regmap_options_group_consistent() shall return true when options is 0") pinned one accept-case of a function that has now been deleted outright -- there is no pairing rule left to be consistent or inconsistent with. See REQ-RMAP-030 for the correct, primary-source-verified replacement design.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1.1 (citation found incorrect -- see text), TC18.txt L2033-2036

See REQ-RMAP-030 for the correct, primary-source-verified replacement design.

requirements.title: RETIRED -- rcp_regmap_options_group_consistent() rejects a partially-set feature group (citation found incorrect, see REQ-RMAP-030)
requirements.text: RETIRED as of REQ-RMAP-030's primary-source verification milestone. This requirement's own shared citation (§12.9.1.1, TC18.txt L2033-2036, quoting "Optional support of compound requests comes as bundle of...") was checked directly against the primary-source PDF (OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC.pdf, §12.9.1.1, page 64, "Handling multiple requests in incoming messages") and found to be a genuine misattribution: that section is entirely about an RC Server processing multiple ACF-type requests packed into one AVTPDU frame (multicast reception, byte_bus_id/stream_id matching, TSCF/NTSCF header rules) -- it says nothing about svr_implemented_options, feature advertisement, or any bit-pairing rule at all. See REQ-RMAP-030 for the correct, primary-source-verified replacement design, under which every bit is independently settable.

requirements.tc18: §12.9.1.1 (citation found incorrect -- see text), TC18.txt L2033-2036

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() grants via_root_client_ep0 for the root client through EP0
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() shall set via_root_client_ep0 true when via_ep0 is true, svr_root_client_index is not RCP_REGMAP_NO_ROOT_CLIENT, and requesting_stream_index equals svr_root_client_index.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Write access via EP0 to other EPs configuration is only possible for a configured 'root client' of via the discovery stream."), TC18.txt L2184

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() withholds via_root_client_ep0 while no root client is granted
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() shall set via_root_client_ep0 false whenever svr_root_client_index equals RCP_REGMAP_NO_ROOT_CLIENT, regardless of via_ep0 or requesting_stream_index.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Write access via EP0 to other EPs configuration is only possible for a configured 'root client' of via the discovery stream."), TC18.txt L2184

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() grants via_owning_stream to an endpoint's owning stream
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() shall set via_owning_stream true when ep_client is non-NULL, ep_client->has_owning_stream is true, and requesting_stream_index equals ep_client->owning_stream_index.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("...functional configuration of each individual EP shall be accessible for read and write...via requests having the stream_id and byte_bus_id that is assigned to the respective EP by the configuration (see 12.7.8)."), TC18.txt L2182-2183

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() withholds via_owning_stream with no owning stream on record
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() shall set via_owning_stream false when ep_client is NULL or ep_client->has_owning_stream is false.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("...functional configuration of each individual EP shall be accessible for read and write...via requests having the stream_id and byte_bus_id that is assigned to the respective EP by the configuration (see 12.7.8)."), TC18.txt L2182-2183

requirements.title: HW pin-property bit assignments are pairwise distinct
requirements.text: The six RCP_REGMAP_PIN_PROP_* bitmask constants shall each occupy a distinct bit position.

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_named_signal_string() never returns NULL
