requirements.text: rcp_sched_frame_timing_consistent() shall return true whenever is_tscf is false, and shall return true whenever count == 0, regardless of member_is_timed's contents.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1.1 ("As the AVTPDU has either a TSCF or NTSCF header a mixture of requests with and without presentation time in a single frame is not possible. A presentation time from a TSCF header will be applied to all ACFtypes within the frame."), TC18.txt L3622-3624

requirements.title: rcp_sched_frame_timing_consistent() rejects a TSCF frame mixing timed and untimed members
requirements.text: For is_tscf == true and count > 0, rcp_sched_frame_timing_consistent() shall return true iff every entry in member_is_timed[0..count) equals member_is_timed[0], and false otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1.1 ("As the AVTPDU has either a TSCF or NTSCF header a mixture of requests with and without presentation time in a single frame is not possible. A presentation time from a TSCF header will be applied to all ACFtypes within the frame."), TC18.txt L3622-3624

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_strerror() never returns NULL and gives every error code a distinct message
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_strerror() shall return a non-NULL string for every rcp_e2e_errc_t value, including unrecognized ones, with each defined error code mapped to a distinct message.

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_crc32() implements the fixed CRC32 parameter set (poly 0xF4ACFB13, init/xorout 0xFFFFFFFF, refin/refout true)
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_crc32() shall compute a 32-bit CRC using polynomial 0xF4ACFB13, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF, with both input and output reflection enabled, verified against the published CRC-32/AUTOSAR check value 0x1697D06A over the ASCII bytes "123456789".
requirements.tc18: §13.6 Table 34 ("CRC32 Polynomial": Polynomial=0xF4ACFB13, Width=32bit, Initial Value=0xFFFFFFFF, Final XOR=0xFFFFFFFF, Input reflection=TRUE, Output reflection=TRUE), OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf p.87 (TC18.txt's own "Table 31" reflects the bundled file's pre-RC5 pagination; the parameter values themselves are unchanged, per ROADMAP.md's own prior confirmation)

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_compute_crc() covers stream_id, avtp_timestamp, and the ACF header-and-payload region, in that order
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_compute_crc() shall return the same value as calling rcp_e2e_crc32() over the concatenation of stream_id (8 bytes, big-endian), avtp_timestamp (4 bytes, big-endian -- the AVTPDU header's own 32-bit field, which TC18 13.6 requires to be included in the calculation and to be filled with all zeros under an NTSCF header), and acf_frame[0..acf_frame_len). The width was previously recorded here as 8 bytes, which neither src/e2e.c (a uint32_t parameter serialised by put_u32) nor include/rcp/e2e.h ever implemented and which no AVTPDU header field has. CLOSED 2026-08-14 (issue #420): rcp_e2e_compute_crc() itself is unchanged -- a pure 'cover exactly what acf_frame[0..acf_frame_len) is handed as' primitive -- but rcp_e2e_wrap() (REQ-E2E-042) now calls it over only the real, unpadded header-and-payload prefix, excluding acf.c's own trailing 0x00 quadlet-alignment pad octets, matching "the entire payload (except padding)" above; previously rcp_e2e_wrap() called it over the whole already-padded frame, incorrectly folding those pad octets into the CRC.
requirements.tc18: §13.6 ("In Safe command mode a CRC32 is calculated per ACF type across specific fields of an AVTPDU header, ACF header, and the entire payload (except padding)." -- the covered header fields are shown via Figure 20/21's highlighting, not named in the 0.5.1_RC5 running prose), OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf p.87-88

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_length_with_crc() applies the length-accounting pre-adjustment
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_length_with_crc() shall return payload_len + RCP_E2E_CRC_LEN, saturating at SIZE_MAX rather than wrapping when payload_len is within RCP_E2E_CRC_LEN of SIZE_MAX.
requirements.tc18: §13.6 ("When calculating the CRC, it needs to be considered that adding the CRC to the byte_msg_payload increases the acf_msg_length by 1."), OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf p.88

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_wrap() appends a big-endian CRC32 trailer computed via rcp_e2e_compute_crc()
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_wrap() shall return an owned rcp_bytes_t equal to acf_frame[0..acf_frame_len) followed by RCP_E2E_CRC_LEN big-endian bytes holding rcp_e2e_compute_crc(stream_id, avtp_timestamp, acf_frame, acf_frame_len).
requirements.tc18: §13.6 Figure 20/Figure 21 ("CRC32" trailer quadlet in the ACF_ABB/ACF_GBB message layout; renumbered from Figure 19/20 in TC18.txt's own pre-RC5 revision), OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf p.88-89

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_wrap() fails safe on invalid input or allocation failure
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_wrap() shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t (data=NULL, len=0) when acf_frame is NULL while acf_frame_len != 0, or when the internal allocation fails.

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_unwrap() rejects a frame shorter than the CRC32 trailer
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_unwrap() shall return RCP_E2E_ERR_SHORT_FRAME whenever frame_len < RCP_E2E_CRC_LEN.
requirements.tc18: §13.6 (implicit: a frame produced under this mechanism always carries a 4-octet CRC32 trailer per Table 34/Figure 20-21, so any frame shorter than that trailer cannot be a valid E2E-protected message), OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf p.87-89 -- the specific "for ms=0..." sentence TC18.txt quotes was replaced in 0.5.1_RC5 (see REQ-E2E-010)

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_unwrap() reports CRC_ERROR on a mismatched trailer
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_unwrap() shall return RCP_E2E_ERR_CRC_MISMATCH whenever the trailing RCP_E2E_CRC_LEN bytes of frame do not equal rcp_e2e_compute_crc(stream_id, avtp_timestamp, frame, frame_len - RCP_E2E_CRC_LEN); a caller receiving this code shall skip executing the request the frame carries.
requirements.tc18: §13.6 ("If a request is received by an endpoint that is in 'Safe command mode' and the CRC does not match, the request is not executed, and an error response is generated with error code: CRC_ERROR."), OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf p.87

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_unwrap() round-trips a frame produced by rcp_e2e_wrap()
requirements.text: For a frame produced by rcp_e2e_wrap(stream_id, avtp_timestamp, acf_frame, acf_frame_len), rcp_e2e_unwrap() called with the same stream_id and avtp_timestamp shall return RCP_E2E_OK with *out_acf_frame/*out_acf_frame_len describing exactly acf_frame[0..acf_frame_len).
requirements.tc18: §13.6 ("The CRC calculation for request and response follows the identical scheme."), TC18.txt L3828

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_fragment_carries_crc() implements the fragmentation/CRC interaction rule
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_fragment_carries_crc() shall return is_last_fragment unmodified, modeling that only a multi-segment message's final fragment carries a CRC.
requirements.tc18: §13.6 ("Fragmentation, if applied to a message, happens after CRC calculation. So, the CRC is only calculated once and will be transmitted in the last segment."), OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf p.89

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_is_safety_request() tests request_type's MSB
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_is_safety_request() shall return true iff (request_type & 0x80) != 0, covering RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_COMPOUND_SAFETY (0x8F), RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_COMPOUND_WAIT_SAFETY (0x8B), and RCP_REQUEST_TYPE_TRIGGERED_SAFETY (0x8E).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("If the MSB of the identifier (0x8x) is set the request is treated as a safety request and will not be deleted when the EP needs to go to safe state." -- 0.5.1_RC5's own tracked-change comment marks this a "clarification to TI_012", replacing the older "will only be executed...In normal operation these requests stay in the queue and are not executed" sentence entirely), OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf p.25

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_request_may_execute() gates safety-tagged requests on the endpoint's safe-state flag
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_request_may_execute() shall return endpoint_in_safe_state whenever rcp_e2e_is_safety_request(request_type) is true.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("If the MSB of the identifier (0x8x) is set the request is treated as a safety request and will not be deleted when the EP needs to go to safe state." -- NOTE: this replaces, not merely rewords, the older "will only be executed...In normal operation these requests stay in the queue and are not executed" sentence this requirement's execution-gating model is actually built on; the new sentence's plain meaning is about queue-purge survival, not execution admission -- see rationale, flagged for dedicated follow-up, not resolved here), OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf p.25

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_request_may_execute() always permits a non-safety-tagged request_type
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_request_may_execute() shall return true whenever rcp_e2e_is_safety_request(request_type) is false, regardless of endpoint_in_safe_state.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("If the MSB of the identifier (0x8x) is set the request is treated as a safety request and will not be deleted when the EP needs to go to safe state." -- non-safety-tagged requests, i.e. MSB clear, are the ordinary always-executable case; see REQ-E2E-012's rationale for the same underlying citation-drift finding), OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf p.25

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_watchdog_purge_should_keep() implements the watchdog-purge-vs-safety-survive rule
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_watchdog_purge_should_keep() shall return rcp_e2e_is_safety_request(request_type).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 ("If a watch-dog overflow is configured to trigger a safe state and execute a safety operation, compound requests with 0x0F will be cleared from the queue while the requests with 0x8F remain active after watch-dog overflow as they belong to the safety sequence to be executed based on the watch-dog triggering." -- renumbered from §11.2.2.1 in TC18.txt's own pre-RC5 revision because 0.5.1_RC5 inserts a new draft "Trigger request" section before it; quoted text itself is unchanged), OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf p.28

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_watchdog_purge_classify() applies the purge rule across a caller-supplied array
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_watchdog_purge_classify() shall write rcp_e2e_watchdog_purge_should_keep(request_types[i]) into out_keep[i] for every i in [0, count).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 ("...compound requests with 0x0F will be cleared from the queue while the requests with 0x8F remain active after watch-dog overflow..." -- renumbered from §11.2.2.1 in TC18.txt's own pre-RC5 revision, see REQ-E2E-014's rationale), OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf p.28

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_measure_valid() recognizes exactly the two defined rcp_e2e_measure_t values
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_measure_valid() shall return true iff rx_safety_measure equals RCP_E2E_MEASURE_FORCE_HIGH_IMPEDANCE or RCP_E2E_MEASURE_SEQUENCER, and false for any other byte value.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 ("a safe state may be enforced. The safe state to enter can be chosen via the Safety_Measure parameter"), TC18.txt L2935

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_endpoint_in_safe_state() always reports true for the force-high-impedance measure
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_endpoint_in_safe_state() shall return true whenever rx_safety_measure == RCP_E2E_MEASURE_FORCE_HIGH_IMPEDANCE, regardless of table, safestate_sequencer, or safe_sequencer_state.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 -- the specific rx_safety_measure row this citation quotes no longer exists in 0.5.1_RC5's restructured 0x000D bit layout (now rx_enforce_crc/rx_enforce_sequence/rx_enforce_watchdog/rx_enforce_request_filing/Reserved/rx_stream_status); this is the same "genuinely unresolved" gap already documented in e2e.h's own file header (2026-08-11 investigation) -- RCP_E2E_MEASURE_FORCE_HIGH_IMPEDANCE/_SEQUENCER remain a deliberate safe-superset abstraction with no current 1:1 TC18 0.5.1_RC5 wire field, OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf p.66

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_endpoint_in_safe_state() polls the configured sequencer for the sequencer-based measure
requirements.text: For rx_safety_measure == RCP_E2E_MEASURE_SEQUENCER and a valid safestate_sequencer index into a non-NULL table, rcp_e2e_endpoint_in_safe_state() shall return true iff rcp_sequencer_get_state(table, safestate_sequencer, ...) reports a state equal to safe_sequencer_state.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 (rx_safestate_seqencer/rx_safe_sequencer_state at 0x000E/0x000F are unchanged from RC1); NOTE: rx_safety_measure (formerly 0x000D.6) is RESERVED as of TC18 0.5.1_RC4/RC5 with no confirmed 1:1 replacement -- already investigated and left open in this codebase's own regmap.h file header ('TC18 0.5.1_RC5 terminology drift', task #97). TC18.txt L2885-2887, L2906-2911 reflect the superseded 0.5.1_RC (RC1) wording, not current RC5.

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_endpoint_in_safe_state() fails closed on an unrecognized measure or an invalid sequencer index
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_endpoint_in_safe_state() shall return false when rx_safety_measure is not a value recognized by rcp_e2e_measure_valid(), when table is NULL for RCP_E2E_MEASURE_SEQUENCER, or when safestate_sequencer does not address a valid entry in table.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24; NOTE: rx_safety_measure (formerly 0x000D.6, 'a 1-bit field with only two defined values') is RESERVED as of TC18 0.5.1_RC4/RC5 -- already investigated, genuinely ambiguous, left open in regmap.h's own file header (task #97). TC18.txt L2885-2887 reflects the superseded 0.5.1_RC (RC1) wording.

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_crc_error_action() maps rx_enforce_e2e to the correct CRC-error action
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_crc_error_action() shall return RCP_E2E_CRC_ACTION_LATCH_STREAM_FAULT iff rx_enforce_e2e is true, and RCP_E2E_CRC_ACTION_DROP_REQUEST otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("rx_enforce_e2e ... 0b: stream is not blocked, when CRC check at EP fails (EP drops the request if CRC check fails) / 1b: stream is blocked until released, when CRC check at EP fails. Safe state will be entered"), TC18.txt L2861-2867

requirements.title: PARTIAL: rcp_e2e_stream_fault_on_crc_error() always signals skip-this-request and latches under rx_enforce_e2e, but nothing in the dispatch path calls it
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED, FIXED 2026-08-12 (issue #201 batch 9): rcp_e2e_stream_fault_on_crc_error() itself was always correct and directly unit-tested; the gap was that nothing in the dispatch path called it. New rcp_e2e_stream_fault_tracker_t (e2e.h/e2e.c) is a caller-owned, keyed-by-stream_id wrapper holding one rcp_e2e_stream_fault_t per stream (a real server may have more than one). rcp_mock_server_dispatch_e2e()/_dispatch_frame_e2e() now (1) check rcp_e2e_stream_fault_tracker_is_faulted() for stream_id BEFORE plain-command-mode delegation, CRC validation, or admission -- returning the new RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_STREAM_FAULTED with a real Table 30 POCI_FAILURE error response -- and (2) record every CRC mismatch they detect via rcp_e2e_stream_fault_tracker_on_crc_error(), keyed to a new per-endpoint rcp_mock_server_set_endpoint_rx_enforce_e2e() stand-in bit (this test double's own in-process stand-in for the real per-request-stream register, matching req_crc_enable's own established stand-in pattern). Wiring is opt-in via rcp_mock_server_set_stream_fault_tracker() (tracker may be NULL, the default, to disable entirely). This closes the "stream is blocked until released" half of rx_enforce_e2e's Table 24 consequence -- a second, third, Nth request on a faulted stream is now genuinely rejected until rcp_e2e_stream_fault_tracker_reset() releases it. The Table 24 sentence's OTHER consequence, "Safe state will be entered," is REQ-E2E-045's own separate, still-open gap (a cross-endpoint safe-state escalation this library's single-endpoint-scoped data model has no orchestrator for) -- not addressed by this fix, and not conflated with it.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("rx_enforce_e2e ... 1b: stream is blocked until released, when CRC check at EP fails. Safe state will be entered"), TC18.txt L2865-2867

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_stream_fault_on_crc_error() leaves f unchanged for the drop-request action
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_stream_fault_on_crc_error() shall leave f->faulted unmodified whenever rcp_e2e_crc_error_action(rx_enforce_e2e) == RCP_E2E_CRC_ACTION_DROP_REQUEST.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("rx_enforce_e2e ... 0b: stream is not blocked, when CRC check at EP fails (EP drops the request if CRC check fails)"), TC18.txt L2861-2864

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_stream_fault_reset() clears a latched fault
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_stream_fault_reset() shall set f->faulted to false, and rcp_e2e_stream_fault_is_faulted() shall report false immediately afterward.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("rx_enforce_e2e ... 1b: stream is blocked until released..."), TC18.txt L2865-2867 -- the counterpart release mechanism this blocked/latched state implies

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate() never reports an overflow while the per-stream watchdog is disabled
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate() shall set overflowed to false whenever rx_wd_enable is false, regardless of elapsed_since_last_kick_ms or rx_wd_timeout_ms.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 ("...enable Watchdog for this Stream" / "WatchDog time out for this Stream in clock tics"), TC18.txt L2855-2856, L2875-2877

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate() reports an overflow once the elapsed time reaches the configured timeout
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate() shall set overflowed to true iff rx_wd_enable is true and elapsed_since_last_kick_ms >= rx_wd_timeout_ms.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 ("...the watchdog is reset with each request received from this RC Client. If the watchdog exceeds its threshold again it can be selected if a safety measure shall be taken and if so which."), TC18.txt L2937-2939

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate() gates enter_safe_state on rx_wd_safestate_enable
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate() shall set enter_safe_state to (overflowed && rx_wd_safestate_enable).
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("rx_wd_safestate_enable ... bring all endpoints for this Stream to safe state if WD triggers"), TC18.txt L2878-2880

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate() gates notify on rx_wd_info_enable independently of enter_safe_state
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate() shall set notify to (overflowed && rx_wd_info_enable), independent of the value computed for enter_safe_state.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24; NOTE: rx_wd_info_enable (formerly 0x000D.7) is REPLACED in RC5 by rx_stream_status, a different mechanism (a passive aggregate status bit reacting to any of 4 fault causes) with no clean 1:1 mapping back to the old per-cause active notification concept -- already investigated, genuinely ambiguous, left open in regmap.h's own file header (task #97); see also REQ-E2E-046 (the new bit's own, separately-tracked requirement). TC18.txt L2889-2891 reflects the superseded 0.5.1_RC (RC1) wording.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_trigger_fires() evaluates the transmission-done trigger
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_trigger_fires() shall return false for trigger RCP_EP_LIN_TRIGGER_NONE regardless of tx_done_event and trailing_time_expired, and shall return true for trigger RCP_EP_LIN_TRIGGER_TX_DONE if and only if both tx_done_event and trailing_time_expired are true (false otherwise). Corrected 2026-08-13: this entry's own text previously described a 'tx_done_event unchanged' result for TX_DONE and omitted trailing_time_expired entirely, which went stale when REQ-LINEP-023 (issue #201) added trailing_time_expired as a second, caller-classified boolean input and changed TX_DONE's evaluation to an AND of both conditions per TC18 §13.7.10.1 ('a transmission has been finalized, AND the configured trailing time has expired'); the code and its test (test_trigger_fires, tests/test_ep_lin.c) were already correct -- only this entry's own text had gone stale.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.10.1 ("The LIN EP issues a trigger when a transmission has been finalized, and the configured trailing time has expired."), TC18.txt L5694-5695

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_functional_cfg_init() zero-initializes cfg
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_functional_cfg_init() shall set every rcp_regmap_ep_functional_cfg_t flag in cfg->common to false, cfg->lin_clk_divider to 0, and cfg->trigger to RCP_EP_LIN_TRIGGER_NONE (0), regardless of cfg's prior contents.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_functional_cfg_writable() denies every writer while HW_UNCONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_functional_cfg_writable() shall return false for lifecycle state RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED regardless of writer.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("...all access to the HW_config and EP_generic_config are locked."), TC18.txt L2553-2554

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_functional_cfg_writable() requires an authorized writer while HW_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_functional_cfg_writable() shall return true for lifecycle state RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED if and only if writer.via_root_client_ep0, writer.via_owning_stream, or writer.via_discovery_stream is true, and false for an unauthorized writer. Corrected 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group F): this entry previously claimed "regardless of writer", superseded by REQ-LIFECYCLE-030/036's authorization-gating fix (issue #198) -- the code and this module's own test (test_functional_cfg_writable_hw_configured_requires_authorization_or_discovery_stream, tests/test_ep_lin.c) were already correct; only this entry's own text had gone stale.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Write access via EP0 to other EPs configuration is only possible for a configured 'root client' of via the discovery stream."), TC18.txt L2560

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_functional_cfg_writable() requires authorization while RCP_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_functional_cfg_writable() shall return false for lifecycle state RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED when writer has neither via_root_client_ep0 nor via_owning_stream set, and true when either is set.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2601-2602 (W* marker convention)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_set_clk_divider() rejects an unauthorized write
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_set_clk_divider() shall leave cfg->lin_clk_divider unchanged and return false when rcp_ep_lin_functional_cfg_writable() denies the write for the given state/writer.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.10.2 Table 55 (lin_clk_divider, 0x0008, "generate Lin bit time"), TC18.txt L5713

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_set_clk_divider() applies an authorized write
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_set_clk_divider() shall set cfg->lin_clk_divider to lin_clk_divider and return true when rcp_ep_lin_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes the write for the given state/writer.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.10.2 Table 55 (lin_clk_divider register), TC18.txt L5713; writability per §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2601-2602 (W* marker convention)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_set_trigger() rejects an unauthorized write
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_set_trigger() shall leave cfg->trigger unchanged and return false when rcp_ep_lin_functional_cfg_writable() denies the write for the given state/writer. CLARIFIED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group C): the write-authorization behavior is TC18-derived (§12.3.1.3's W* marker convention, delegated via rcp_ep_lin_functional_cfg_writable()); `trigger` itself has no TC18 basis at all -- unlike SPI/PWM_OUT/PWM_IN, TC18 defines no trigger-outputs table for LIN. See ep_lin.h's own file header.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2601-2602 (W* marker convention) -- governs the write-authorization behavior; `trigger` itself is this module's own original design with no TC18 counterpart (see ep_lin.h's file header)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_set_trigger() applies an authorized write
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_set_trigger() shall set cfg->trigger to trigger and return true when rcp_ep_lin_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes the write for the given state/writer. CLARIFIED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group C): the write-authorization behavior is TC18-derived (§12.3.1.3's W* marker convention); `trigger` itself has no TC18 basis at all -- see REQ-LINEP-013 and ep_lin.h's own file header.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2601-2602 (W* marker convention) -- governs the write-authorization behavior; `trigger` itself is this module's own original design with no TC18 counterpart (see ep_lin.h's file header)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_strerror() returns a distinct, non-NULL message per error code
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_strerror() shall return a non-NULL, non-empty, and distinct string for each of RCP_EP_LIN_OK, RCP_EP_LIN_ERR_SHORT_FRAME, RCP_EP_LIN_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE, RCP_EP_LIN_ERR_WRONG_BUS, and RCP_EP_LIN_ERR_WRONG_OP, and a non-NULL string for any other value.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_encode_command_request() encodes the read direction, evt=0, and carries the raw payload unmodified
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_encode_command_request() shall encode an ACF_ABB message addressed to byte_bus_id with op RCP_ACF_OP_READ (the reply-expected direction), evt = 0 (Table 33 constrains a plain LIN request's evt[2:0] to 000b; there is no client-selectable comparison mode), transaction_num set to transaction_num, and payload equal to tx_data[0..tx_len) byte for byte.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_decode_command_request() round-trips a valid command request
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_decode_command_request() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_lin_encode_command_request() for byte_bus_id == expected_bus_id, return RCP_EP_LIN_OK and recover the raw tx payload and transaction_num unchanged.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.10.3 Figure 39 (lin request/response format), TC18.txt L5719-5736; "the LIN endpoint checks each received message against the byte_msg_payload and if a match under the conditions given by evt[2:0] is found a reply is sent if op = 0" (§13.7.10.1), TC18.txt L5691-5693; evt[2:0] plain-request rule per §13.5 Table 33 (LIN's row-2 group, only evt=111b defined), TC18.txt L4083-4093

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_decode_command_request() rejects a malformed, misaddressed, or non-plain frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_decode_command_request() shall return RCP_EP_LIN_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame too short for the ACF_ABB fixed header or its declared payload length, RCP_EP_LIN_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE when the frame is not an ACF_ABB message, RCP_EP_LIN_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id, RCP_EP_LIN_ERR_WRONG_OP when op is not RCP_ACF_OP_READ, and RCP_EP_LIN_ERR_BAD_EVT when evt[2:0] != 000b (REQ-LINEP-027).
requirements.tc18: §13.7.10.3 Figure 39 (lin request/response format), TC18.txt L5719-5736; general ACF frame-validation basis

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_encode_response() selects ACF_ABB or ACF_GBB by the timed flag
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_encode_response() shall encode an ACF_ABB message when timed is false, and an ACF_GBB message with message_timestamp set to timestamp and mtv RCP_ACF_MTV_VALID when timed is true, in both cases with op RCP_ACF_OP_READ, byte_bus_id set to byte_bus_id, transaction_num set to transaction_num, and payload equal to rx_data[0..rx_len) byte for byte.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.10.3 Figure 39 (lin request/response format), TC18.txt L5719-5736

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_decode_response() round-trips an untimed (ACF_ABB) response
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_decode_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_lin_encode_response() with timed false, return RCP_EP_LIN_OK, recover the rx payload and transaction_num unchanged, report out_timed false, and report out_timestamp 0.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.10.3 Figure 39 (lin request/response format), TC18.txt L5719-5736; response timed/untimed ACF_GBB/ACF_ABB convention shared with every prior endpoint type

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_decode_response() round-trips a timed (ACF_GBB) response
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_decode_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_lin_encode_response() with timed true, return RCP_EP_LIN_OK, recover the rx payload and transaction_num unchanged, report out_timed true, and report out_timestamp equal to the original timestamp.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.10.3 Figure 39 (lin request/response format), TC18.txt L5719-5736; response timed/untimed ACF_GBB/ACF_ABB convention shared with every prior endpoint type

requirements.title: rcp_ep_lin_decode_response() rejects a malformed or misaddressed frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_lin_decode_response() shall return RCP_EP_LIN_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame too short for its applicable ACF fixed header and RCP_EP_LIN_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.10.3 Figure 39 (lin request/response format), TC18.txt L5719-5736; general ACF frame-validation basis for the response wire format

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_frame_format_valid() accepts exactly the six FrameFormat values Table 54 defines
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_frame_format_valid() shall return true for v in 0..5 and false for any value above 5.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_frame_format_is_xl() identifies the two CAN XL variants
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_frame_format_is_xl() shall return true for RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_XL_CLASSICAL_PL and RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_XL_NEW_PL, and false for every other value.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_frame_format_id_width() reports the correct arbitration-id width per format
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_frame_format_id_width() shall return RCP_EP_CAN_ID_WIDTH_EXTENDED_29 for RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_CEFF and RCP_EP_CAN_FRAME_FEFF, and RCP_EP_CAN_ID_WIDTH_BASE_11 for every other value including an invalid format.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 ("Sending remote frames is not supported. In case the CAN ID is 11bits, then it shall be right aligned in the CAN ID field."), TC18.txt L5887; §13.7.11.2 Table 56, TC18.txt L5764-5836

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_arbitration_id_valid() bounds an identifier against its format's id width
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_arbitration_id_valid() shall return true iff format is rcp_ep_can_frame_format_valid() and id does not exceed 0x7FF (BASE_11 formats) or 0x1FFFFFFF (EXTENDED_29 formats), and false for an invalid format regardless of id.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 ("In case the CAN ID is 11bits, then it shall be right aligned in the CAN ID field."), TC18.txt L5887

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_frame_format_max_data_len() reports each frame kind's own data ceiling
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_frame_format_max_data_len() shall return 8 for CBFF/CEFF, 64 for FBFF/FEFF, RCP_EP_CAN_XL_MAX_DATA_LEN (2048) for both CAN XL variants, and 0 for an invalid format.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 ("For CAN XL this can be up to 2054 bytes (2048 + 6, see below)... The 'CAN data' field includes the additional data (RRS, SDT, VCID, AF (in total 6 bytes)- see ISO11898-1) needed for CAN XL frames"), TC18.txt L5859-5860, L5888-5889

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_xl_filter_index_valid() accepts exactly the defined filter-table indices
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_xl_filter_index_valid() shall return true for index in 0..RCP_EP_CAN_XL_MAX_FILTERS-1 and false for index >= RCP_EP_CAN_XL_MAX_FILTERS.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.2 Table 56 (four "acceptance filter" entries: acceptance filter 1-4, each 32 bit R/W), TC18.txt L5801-5815

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_functional_cfg_init() zero-initializes every functional-config field
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_functional_cfg_init() shall zero cfg->common's flags, every bit-timing register set, delay_comp_enable/_offset, exec_delay_clk_divider, and every xl_filters[] entry.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_functional_cfg_writable() reuses server.h's field-writability authorization
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_functional_cfg_writable() shall return exactly rcp_server_field_writable(state, RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W, writer).
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("...all access to the HW_config and EP_generic_config are locked."), TC18.txt L2553-2554; §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2601-2602 (W* marker convention)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_set_arbitration_timing() is gated by functional-config authorization
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_set_arbitration_timing() shall apply timing to cfg->arbitration_timing and return true iff rcp_ep_can_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes the write for state/writer, leaving cfg unchanged and returning false otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.2 Table 56 ("CAN bit time register 1 ... Defines bit times for Classical CAN"), TC18.txt L5795; §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2601-2602 (W* marker convention)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_set_fd_data_timing() is gated by functional-config authorization
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_set_fd_data_timing() shall apply timing to cfg->fd_data_timing and return true iff rcp_ep_can_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes the write for state/writer, leaving cfg unchanged and returning false otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.2 Table 56 ("CAN bit time register 2 ... Defines bit times for CAN FD"), TC18.txt L5796; §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2601-2602 (W* marker convention)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_set_xl_data_timing() is gated by functional-config authorization
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_set_xl_data_timing() shall apply timing to cfg->xl_data_timing and return true iff rcp_ep_can_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes the write for state/writer, leaving cfg unchanged and returning false otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.2 Table 56 ("CAN bit time register 3 ... Defines bit times for CAN XL"), TC18.txt L5797; §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2601-2602 (W* marker convention)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_set_delay_compensation() is gated by functional-config authorization
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_set_delay_compensation() shall apply enable/offset to cfg->delay_comp_enable/cfg->delay_comp_offset and return true iff rcp_ep_can_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes the write for state/writer, leaving cfg unchanged and returning false otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.2 Table 56 ("TDCC register ... delay compensation control"), TC18.txt L5798; §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2601-2602 (W* marker convention)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_set_exec_delay_clk_divider() is gated by functional-config authorization
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_set_exec_delay_clk_divider() shall apply divider to cfg->exec_delay_clk_divider and return true iff rcp_ep_can_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes the write for state/writer, leaving cfg unchanged and returning false otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.2 Table 56 ("can_clk_divider ... generate CAN_CLK time reference"), TC18.txt L5792; §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2601-2602 (W* marker convention)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_set_xl_filter() validates the filter index and functional-config authorization
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_set_xl_filter() shall apply filter to cfg->xl_filters[index] and return true iff index is rcp_ep_can_xl_filter_index_valid() and rcp_ep_can_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes the write for state/writer, leaving cfg unchanged and returning false otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.2 Table 56 (four "acceptance filter" entries: acceptance filter 1-4), TC18.txt L5801-5815; §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2601-2602 (W* marker convention)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_strerror() returns a non-null, distinct message for every error code
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_strerror() shall return a non-null, non-empty string for every rcp_ep_can_errc_t value, distinct across all defined values, and a non-null string for an undefined value.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_encode_frame_request() enforces frame-format, id, length, and xl_header preconditions
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_encode_frame_request() shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t if frame_format is not rcp_ep_can_frame_format_valid(), arbitration_id is not rcp_ep_can_arbitration_id_valid() for frame_format, tx_len exceeds rcp_ep_can_frame_format_max_data_len(frame_format), or xl_header's presence does not match rcp_ep_can_frame_format_is_xl(frame_format); otherwise it shall encode an ACF_ABB request with evt left at 0 (TC18 Table 33's plain-request value for CAN's endpoint-type row) and frame_format packed into the payload's leading quadlet's top 3 bits alongside arbitration_id (TC18 §13.7.11.3 Figure 39), followed by this module's own xl-header/data layout. FIXED (v0.109.0): previously packed frame_format into evt[2:0] instead, a wire position TC18 does not assign it (see REQ-CANEP-031's corrected text).

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_request() rejects a malformed, misaddressed, wrong-evt, malformed-selector, or bad-arbitration-id frame
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_request() shall return RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame too short for the ACF_ABB fixed header, its declared payload length, the 4-byte leading quadlet, or the full frame_format-dependent prefix length; RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE if b is not an ACF_ABB message; RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id; RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_WRONG_OP when op is not RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE; RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_BAD_EVT when evt[2:0] is not 0b000 (TC18 §13.5 Table 33's only legal value for a plain request in CAN's endpoint-type row); RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_BAD_FRAME_FORMAT when the leading quadlet's top 3 bits are not rcp_ep_can_frame_format_valid(); and RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_BAD_ARBITRATION_ID when the leading quadlet's low 29 bits are not rcp_ep_can_arbitration_id_valid() for that frame_format.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_request() round-trips a well-formed frame's fields
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_request() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_can_encode_frame_request(), return RCP_EP_CAN_OK and recover frame_format, arbitration_id, xl_header (iff frame_format is a CAN XL variant), the tx data bytes, and transaction_num unchanged.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_encode_frame_response() enforces the same preconditions as the request encoder and supports timed/untimed encoding
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_encode_frame_response() shall apply the same frame-format/id/length/xl_header preconditions as rcp_ep_can_encode_frame_request() (substituting rx_data/rx_len), encoding as ACF_ABB when timed is false and as ACF_GBB with message_timestamp set to timestamp when timed is true.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_response() rejects a malformed, misaddressed, wrong-evt, malformed-selector, or bad-arbitration-id frame across both ACF_ABB and ACF_GBB
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_response() shall return RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame too short for the applicable fixed header, its declared payload length, the 4-byte leading quadlet, or the full frame_format-dependent prefix length; RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_WRONG_BUS when byte_bus_id != expected_bus_id; RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_BAD_EVT when evt[2:0] is not 0b000 (TC18 §13.5 Table 33's only legal value for a plain response in CAN's endpoint-type row); RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_BAD_FRAME_FORMAT when the leading quadlet's top 3 bits are not rcp_ep_can_frame_format_valid(); and RCP_EP_CAN_ERR_BAD_ARBITRATION_ID when the leading quadlet's low 29 bits are not rcp_ep_can_arbitration_id_valid() for that frame_format -- regardless of whether the message is ACF_ABB or ACF_GBB.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_response() reports timed/untimed status and timestamp correctly
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_can_encode_frame_response() with timed false, report out_timed false and out_timestamp 0; given one produced with timed true, report out_timed true and out_timestamp equal to the original timestamp.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_response() round-trips a well-formed frame's fields
requirements.text: rcp_ep_can_decode_frame_response() shall, given a frame produced by rcp_ep_can_encode_frame_response(), return RCP_EP_CAN_OK and recover frame_format, arbitration_id, xl_header (iff frame_format is a CAN XL variant), the rx data bytes, and transaction_num unchanged.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_symbol_encode() frames a nibble as a 5-bit even-parity symbol
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_symbol_encode() shall return a value in 0..31 whose bit 4 equals the even parity of bits [3:0], with bits [3:0] equal to the input nibble masked to its own low 4 bits.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_symbol_decode() validates a symbol's parity bit
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_symbol_decode() shall return true and set *out_nibble to bits [3:0] of the symbol iff bit 4 equals the even parity of bits [3:0], and shall return false otherwise.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_bitframe_encoded_len() reports two symbols per content octet
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_bitframe_encoded_len(data_len, append_crc) shall return 2 * (data_len + (append_crc ? 1 : 0)).

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_encode_bitframe() produces only valid, round-trippable symbols
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_encode_bitframe() shall produce exactly rcp_ep_iseled_bitframe_encoded_len(data_len, append_crc) octets, each holding a value in 0..31 that rcp_ep_iseled_symbol_decode() accepts.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_encode_bitframe() appends the CRC-8 trailer when append_crc is true
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_encode_bitframe() shall, when append_crc is true, frame rcp_ep_iseled_crc8(data, data_len) as one extra trailing content octet after the data octets and before symbol expansion.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_crc8() is a deterministic, input-sensitive CRC-8
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_crc8() shall return the same value for the same input, shall return 0x00 for a zero-length input, and shall return a different value for two inputs that differ in content.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_requires_isp_n() reflects the device-provided-clock mode
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_requires_isp_n() shall return true iff use_rcv_clk is true. CORRECTED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group G): this entry previously stated the opposite polarity (false iff use_rcv_clk is true), matching a real inverted-polarity bug in rcp_ep_iseled_requires_isp_n()'s own implementation that this fix corrects. TC18 Table 55 documents iseled_use_rcv_clk itself as "Use clock provided by ISELED 1st device instead of FreqSync pattern" -- true selects the device-provided clock, which arrives on ISP_N; ISP_N is unneeded only in the false case (Freq_Sync pattern).
requirements.tc18: §13.7.12.2 Table 58, TC18.txt L5950-5952 ("iseled_use_rcv_clk ... Use clock provided by ISELED 1st device instead of FreqSync pattern"); §13.7.12.2 ("For receiving ISELED frames on the ISP_P Pin of the interface either a clock synchronization via the Freq_Sync pattern can be done or data sampling based on the clock provided on the ISP_N pin. If the Freq_Sync pattern is used it is not necessary to connect the ISP_N of the EP to a physical Pin."), TC18.txt L5964-5966

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_trigger_fires() evaluates the single transmission-complete trigger
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_trigger_fires() shall return false for RCP_EP_ISELED_TRIGGER_NONE regardless of tx_complete_event, and for RCP_EP_ISELED_TRIGGER_TX_COMPLETE shall return the value of tx_complete_event.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.12.1 ("The ISELED endpoint creates a single trigger event, when transmission of a data packet has been completed on the ISELED network."), TC18.txt L5913-5914

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_functional_cfg_init() zero-initializes the functional config
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_functional_cfg_init() shall set every rcp_regmap_ep_functional_cfg_t flag false, iseled_bit_clk_divider to 0, iseled_use_rcv_clk and iseled_crc_enable to false, and trigger to RCP_EP_ISELED_TRIGGER_NONE.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_functional_cfg_writable() wraps server.h's field-writability authorization
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_functional_cfg_writable() shall return the result of rcp_server_field_writable() called with kind RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.12.2 Table 58 (iseled_ep_options, 0x0003, R/W*), TC18.txt L5934-5936; W* marker convention per §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2601-2602

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_set_bit_clk_divider() is gated by functional-config writability
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_set_bit_clk_divider() shall apply the write and return true iff rcp_ep_iseled_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes it for the given state/writer, and shall leave cfg unchanged and return false otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.12.2 Table 58 (iseled_clk_divider, 0x0006, 8 bit, R/W, "generate ISELED_CLK time reference should be nominal 2MHz"), TC18.txt L5940-5942; writability per §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2601-2602

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_set_use_rcv_clk() is gated by functional-config writability
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_set_use_rcv_clk() shall apply the write and return true iff rcp_ep_iseled_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes it for the given state/writer, and shall leave cfg unchanged and return false otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.12.2 Table 58 (iseled_use_rcv_clk, 0x0007.4, R/W, "Use clock provided by ISELED 1st device instead of FreqSync pattern"), TC18.txt L5950-5952; writability per §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2601-2602

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_set_crc_enable() is gated by functional-config writability
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_set_crc_enable() shall apply the write and return true iff rcp_ep_iseled_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes it for the given state/writer, and shall leave cfg unchanged and return false otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.12.1 ("The optional CRC generation as specified in the ISLED standard can be enabled. If so, the CRC will be generated and attached to the write messages to the ISELED network."), TC18.txt L5910-5912; writability per §12.3.1.3, TC18.txt L2601-2602

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_set_trigger() is gated by functional-config writability
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_set_trigger() shall apply the write and return true iff rcp_ep_iseled_functional_cfg_writable() authorizes it for the given state/writer, and shall leave cfg unchanged and return false otherwise.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_strerror() never returns NULL and is distinct per code
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_strerror() shall return a non-NULL, non-empty string for every rcp_ep_iseled_errc_t value (including an unknown value), with a distinct string for each defined value.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_decode_bitframe() rejects an odd symbol count
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_decode_bitframe() shall return RCP_EP_ISELED_ERR_ODD_SYMBOL_COUNT iff symbol_count is odd.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_decode_bitframe() rejects an invalid symbol
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_decode_bitframe() shall return RCP_EP_ISELED_ERR_BAD_SYMBOL iff any symbol in symbols[0..symbol_count) fails rcp_ep_iseled_symbol_decode().

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_decode_bitframe() rejects too few symbols when a CRC trailer is expected
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_decode_bitframe() shall return RCP_EP_ISELED_ERR_SHORT_FRAME iff expect_crc is true and symbol_count yields fewer than one reconstructed content octet.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_decode_bitframe() rejects a native ISELED CRC-8 mismatch
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_decode_bitframe() shall return RCP_EP_ISELED_ERR_CRC_MISMATCH iff expect_crc is true and the trailing reconstructed octet does not equal rcp_ep_iseled_crc8() of the preceding reconstructed octets.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_decode_bitframe() round-trips rcp_ep_iseled_encode_bitframe()'s output
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_decode_bitframe() shall, for symbols produced by rcp_ep_iseled_encode_bitframe(data, data_len, append_crc) with matching expect_crc, return RCP_EP_ISELED_OK and populate *out_data with exactly data[0..data_len).

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_encode_command_request() carries the caller's plain payload verbatim as ACF_OP_WRITE
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_encode_command_request() shall encode an ACF_ABB frame addressed to byte_bus_id with op RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE and payload exactly tx_data[0..tx_len), unmodified.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.12.3 Figure 41 (iseled request format -- Instruction/Address/Data payload, ACF_ABB op=write), TC18.txt L5981-5995

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_decode_command_request() validates and decodes an ACF-level command request
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_decode_command_request() shall return RCP_EP_ISELED_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame shorter than the ACF_ABB header or its declared payload, RCP_EP_ISELED_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE for a non-ACF_ABB frame, RCP_EP_ISELED_ERR_WRONG_BUS for a mismatched byte_bus_id, RCP_EP_ISELED_ERR_WRONG_OP for an op other than RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE, RCP_EP_ISELED_ERR_BAD_EVT when evt[2:0] is not 0b000 (TC18 §13.5 Table 33's only legal value for a plain request in ISELED's endpoint-type row; every other value shall be rejected with error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD at the dispatch layer), and otherwise RCP_EP_ISELED_OK with the plain payload and transaction number populated.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_encode_response() encodes timed and untimed responses
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_encode_response() shall encode an ACF_GBB frame with message_timestamp set to timestamp and mtv RCP_ACF_MTV_VALID when timed is true, and an ACF_ABB frame otherwise, in both cases with payload exactly rx_data[0..rx_len) and op RCP_ACF_OP_READ.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.12.3 Figure 42 (iseled response format -- Address/Data[11:0]/CRC payload), TC18.txt L6014-6018; response rsp bit per §11.3 Table 17, TC18.txt L2260

requirements.title: rcp_ep_iseled_decode_response() validates and decodes either ACF_ABB or ACF_GBB responses
requirements.text: rcp_ep_iseled_decode_response() shall accept either an ACF_ABB or ACF_GBB frame, return RCP_EP_ISELED_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame too short for the applicable header or declared payload, RCP_EP_ISELED_ERR_WRONG_BUS for a mismatched byte_bus_id, and otherwise RCP_EP_ISELED_OK with the plain payload, transaction number, and timed/timestamp populated.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.12.3 Figure 42 (iseled response format), TC18.txt L6014-6018; timed/untimed ACF_GBB/ACF_ABB response convention shared with every prior endpoint type

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_addr_valid() validates a Clause-22/Clause-45 MDIO address
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_addr_valid() shall return false for any prtad above RCP_EP_MDIO_PRTAD_MAX, for a RCP_EP_MDIO_CLAUSE_22 address with a nonzero devad or a regad above RCP_EP_MDIO_CLAUSE22_REGAD_MAX, for a RCP_EP_MDIO_CLAUSE_45 address with devad above RCP_EP_MDIO_DEVAD_MAX, and for any other clause value; true otherwise. CORRECTED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group D): the field widths this function validates (5-bit prtad/devad/Clause-22-regad) are independently public knowledge of IEEE 802.3 Clause 22/45, per ep_mdio.h's own file header ("Two addressing modes: Clause-22 MMD and Clause-45 MMS") -- not values TC18 §13.7.13 itself defines (TC18's own mdio_address field is only described as "As per IEEE & OA SPI spec", §13.7.13.3 Table 57, with no field-width breakdown of its own). The previous citation ("An RC Server implementation with an integrated PHY may allow access...") described an unrelated sentence about integrated-PHY access, not address-field validation; corrected to cite the actual TC18 basis for this endpoint's existence and its own honest field-width disclosure.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.13.1, TC18.txt L6033-6037 (MDIO EP's own existence and topic area); §13.7.13.3 Table 60 (mdio_address: "As per IEEE & OA SPI spec"), TC18.txt L6085 -- TC18 defers this field's own width to an external IEEE/OA reference this codebase does not reproduce, per ep_mdio.h's own file header

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_burst_next_regad() computes the next burst register address
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_burst_next_regad() shall return regad+1 wrapped modulo 32 for RCP_EP_MDIO_CLAUSE_22, regad+1 wrapped modulo 65536 for RCP_EP_MDIO_CLAUSE_45, and regad unchanged for any other clause value. NOTE (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group D): this wraparound rule -- and the whole burst/post-increment-addressing concept it implements -- is this module's own original engineering design (ep_mdio.h's own file header, "Single-word and burst addressing": "this module's own generalization of the well-known MDIO post-increment addressing idiom... not a spec-mandated behavior"), not derived from TC18 §13.7.13's own text, which describes no burst/word_count concept at all -- Table 57's mdio_mode field instead selects access width via 4 discrete values. Corrected from carrying no citation at all (implying an undisclosed TC18 conformance basis) to an honestly-cited entry, matching ep_iseled.h's own precedent of keeping ASIL-B for a module's original engineering design that is nonetheless directly relied upon by this endpoint type's own safety-relevant address-space bounds.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.13.1, TC18.txt L6033-6037 (cited only as attribution for which general topic area -- MDIO management access -- motivated this endpoint type's existence, per ep_mdio.h's own file header; not as a source for this specific burst-addressing design)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_word_encode() encodes a 16-bit register word as two big-endian octets
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_word_encode() shall write word's high byte to out[0] and word's low byte to out[1]. NOTE (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group D): the big-endian byte order this encodes is this module's own original engineering choice (ep_mdio.h's own file header, "Wire layout"), consistent with -- but not itself specified by -- TC18 §13.7.13.3's mdio_payload field, whose own internal byte order TC18 does not spell out. Corrected from carrying no citation at all to an honestly-cited entry.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.13.3 Table 60 (mdio_payload field), TC18.txt L6086 -- this module's own byte-order choice for that field, not itself specified by the cited text

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_word_decode() decodes two big-endian octets as a 16-bit register word
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_word_decode() shall return (in[0] << 8) | in[1]. NOTE (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group D): the inverse of REQ-MDIO-003's own byte-order choice -- see that entry's own note.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.13.3 Table 60 (mdio_payload field), TC18.txt L6086 -- this module's own byte-order choice for that field, not itself specified by the cited text

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_pack_len() computes the packed byte length of a word count
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_pack_len() shall return word_count * 2. NOTE (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group D): pure arithmetic over this module's own word_count/burst concept -- see REQ-MDIO-002's own note on that concept's non-TC18-derived origin. Corrected from carrying no citation at all to an honestly-cited entry.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.13.1, TC18.txt L6033-6037 (cited only as attribution for which general topic area motivated this endpoint type's existence; see REQ-MDIO-002)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_pack_words() packs a register-word array into a big-endian byte buffer
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_pack_words() shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t when word_count is 0 or on allocation failure, and otherwise a newly allocated buffer of rcp_ep_mdio_pack_len(word_count) octets holding each word's rcp_ep_mdio_word_encode() result in order.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_word_count_of() derives a word count from a packed byte length
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_word_count_of() shall return false and leave *out_word_count untouched when byte_len is odd, and otherwise return true with *out_word_count set to byte_len / 2. NOTE (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group D): the inverse of REQ-MDIO-005's own word-count/byte-length relationship -- see that entry's own note. Corrected from carrying no citation at all to an honestly-cited entry.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.13.1, TC18.txt L6033-6037 (cited only as attribution for which general topic area motivated this endpoint type's existence; see REQ-MDIO-002/005)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_unpack_word_at() reads one packed register word by index
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_unpack_word_at() shall return rcp_ep_mdio_word_decode() applied to data[2*word_index .. 2*word_index+2). NOTE (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group D): a pure index-into-packed-words helper over this module's own word-packing layout -- see REQ-MDIO-002/003's own notes. Corrected from carrying no citation at all to an honestly-cited entry.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.13.1, TC18.txt L6033-6037 (cited only as attribution for which general topic area motivated this endpoint type's existence; see REQ-MDIO-002/003/005)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_functional_cfg_init() zero-initializes an MDIO functional config
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_functional_cfg_init() shall zero-initialize cfg and initialize cfg->common via rcp_regmap_ep_functional_cfg_init(), leaving every common flag false.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_functional_cfg_writable() delegates to the shared field-authorization logic
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_functional_cfg_writable() shall return rcp_server_field_writable(state, RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W, writer).

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_strerror() returns a non-NULL message for every error code
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_strerror() shall return a non-NULL, non-empty, distinct message for each rcp_ep_mdio_errc_t value, and a non-NULL message for any unrecognized value.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_encode_read_request() encodes this module's own ACF_ABB MDIO read request payload
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_encode_read_request() shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t when !rcp_ep_mdio_addr_valid(addr) or word_count is 0 or exceeds RCP_EP_MDIO_MAX_BURST_WORDS, and otherwise encode an ACF_ABB message with op RCP_ACF_OP_READ whose payload is a leading mdio_mode octet (REQ-MDIO-021) followed by addr's clause/prtad/devad/regad fields and word_count, all as specified. NOTE (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group D; UPDATED 2026-08-12, issue #201): this payload layout is this module's own original design (mdio_mode + clause/prtad/devad/regad/word_count) for the address portion, NOT TC18 §13.7.13.3 Figure 43/Table 60's own unspecified mdio_address wire width -- see REQ-MDIO-021, now PARTIAL: the mdio_mode field itself is real and wire-encoded, closing that half of the original gap, but the address portion's own exact bit layout remains a documented, still-open remainder (REQ-MDIO-021's own text). This entry's own function is correctly implemented against its own documented contract.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.13.3 Figure 43/Table 60, TC18.txt L6065-6088 -- the real TC18 wire layout this function's own payload does not match; see REQ-MDIO-021

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_decode_read_request() validates and decodes this module's own ACF-level MDIO read request payload
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_decode_read_request() shall return RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame shorter than the ACF_ABB header, its declared payload, or the 8-byte (mdio_mode octet + 7-byte address/word_count) request prefix; RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE for a non-ACF_ABB frame; RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_WRONG_BUS for a mismatched byte_bus_id; RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_WRONG_OP for an op other than RCP_ACF_OP_READ; RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_MMS when the decoded mdio_mode octet is an MMS value (REQ-MDIO-021's own still-open remainder); RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_BAD_EVT when evt[2:0] is not 0b000 (the value REQ-ACF-023 resolves, after cross-checking TC18's own Figure 33 worked example, as the legal plain-request value for this Table 33 row -- see that entry for the full resolution of Table 33's own apparent internal inconsistency); RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_BAD_ADDR when the decoded address fails rcp_ep_mdio_addr_valid(); RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_BAD_WORD_COUNT when the decoded word_count is 0 or exceeds RCP_EP_MDIO_MAX_BURST_WORDS; and otherwise RCP_EP_MDIO_OK with the address, word count, and transaction number populated. NOTE (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group D; UPDATED 2026-08-12, issue #201): the address portion's own payload layout this decodes is this module's own original design, not TC18's own unspecified wire width -- see REQ-MDIO-012's own note and REQ-MDIO-021 (now PARTIAL).
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33, TC18.txt L4069-4116 (evt[2:0] legality, resolved at REQ-ACF-023); §13.7.13.3 Figure 43/Table 60, TC18.txt L6065-6088 (the real wire layout this function's own payload does not match; see REQ-MDIO-021)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_encode_read_response() encodes timed and untimed MDIO read responses using this module's own packed-words payload
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_encode_read_response() shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t when word_count exceeds RCP_EP_MDIO_MAX_BURST_WORDS or on allocation failure, and otherwise encode an ACF_GBB frame with message_timestamp set to timestamp and mtv RCP_ACF_MTV_VALID when timed is true, or an ACF_ABB frame otherwise, in both cases with payload rcp_ep_mdio_pack_words(words, word_count) and op RCP_ACF_OP_READ. NOTE (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group D): the response payload's own packed-word layout is this module's own original design, paired with REQ-MDIO-012's own request-side gap -- see that entry's note and REQ-MDIO-021.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.13.3 Figure 43/Table 60, TC18.txt L6065-6088 (the real TC18 mdio_payload field this response's own packed-word layout does not literally match in framing, though the underlying 16/32-bit register data is the same concept; see REQ-MDIO-021)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_decode_read_response() validates and decodes either ACF_ABB or ACF_GBB MDIO read responses in this module's own packed-words layout
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_decode_read_response() shall accept either an ACF_ABB or ACF_GBB frame, return RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame too short for the applicable header or declared payload, RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_WRONG_BUS for a mismatched byte_bus_id, RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_BAD_WORD_COUNT for an odd payload length or more than RCP_EP_MDIO_MAX_BURST_WORDS words, and otherwise RCP_EP_MDIO_OK with the packed word bytes, word count, transaction number, and timed/timestamp populated. NOTE (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group D): see REQ-MDIO-014's own note and REQ-MDIO-021 for this payload layout's own non-TC18-wire-format basis.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.13.3 Figure 43/Table 60, TC18.txt L6065-6088 (see REQ-MDIO-021)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_encode_write_request() encodes this module's own ACF_ABB MDIO write request payload
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_encode_write_request() shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t when !rcp_ep_mdio_addr_valid(addr), word_count is 0 or exceeds RCP_EP_MDIO_MAX_BURST_WORDS, or on allocation failure, and otherwise encode an ACF_ABB message with op RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE whose payload is a leading mdio_mode octet (REQ-MDIO-021) followed by addr's clause/prtad/devad/regad fields and rcp_ep_mdio_pack_words(words, word_count). NOTE (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group D; UPDATED 2026-08-12, issue #201): the write-side counterpart of REQ-MDIO-012 -- see that entry's own note and REQ-MDIO-021 (now PARTIAL) for this payload layout's basis.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.13.3 Figure 43/Table 60, TC18.txt L6065-6088 (see REQ-MDIO-021)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_decode_write_request() validates and decodes this module's own ACF-level MDIO write request payload
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_decode_write_request() shall return RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame shorter than the ACF_ABB header, its declared payload, or the 6-byte (mdio_mode octet + 5-byte address prefix) request prefix; RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_BAD_MSG_TYPE for a non-ACF_ABB frame; RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_WRONG_BUS for a mismatched byte_bus_id; RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_WRONG_OP for an op other than RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE; RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_MMS when the decoded mdio_mode octet is an MMS value (REQ-MDIO-021's own still-open remainder); RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_BAD_EVT when evt[2:0] is not 0b000 (the value REQ-ACF-023 resolves, after cross-checking TC18's own Figure 33 worked example, as the legal plain-request value for this Table 33 row -- see that entry for the full resolution of Table 33's own apparent internal inconsistency); RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_BAD_ADDR when the decoded address fails rcp_ep_mdio_addr_valid(); RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_BAD_WORD_COUNT when the trailing words region's byte length is odd, is 0, or represents more than RCP_EP_MDIO_MAX_BURST_WORDS words; and otherwise RCP_EP_MDIO_OK with the address, packed word bytes, word count, and transaction number populated. NOTE (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group D; UPDATED 2026-08-12, issue #201): the address portion's own payload layout this decodes is this module's own original design, not TC18's own unspecified wire width -- see REQ-MDIO-016's own note and REQ-MDIO-021 (now PARTIAL).
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33, TC18.txt L4069-4116 (evt[2:0] legality, resolved at REQ-ACF-023); §13.7.13.3 Figure 43/Table 60, TC18.txt L6065-6088 (see REQ-MDIO-021)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_encode_write_response() encodes timed and untimed MDIO write responses using this module's own packed-words payload
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_encode_write_response() shall return a zeroed rcp_bytes_t when accepted_word_count exceeds RCP_EP_MDIO_MAX_BURST_WORDS or on allocation failure, and otherwise encode an ACF_GBB frame with message_timestamp set to timestamp and mtv RCP_ACF_MTV_VALID when timed is true, or an ACF_ABB frame otherwise, in both cases with payload rcp_ep_mdio_pack_words(accepted_words, accepted_word_count) and op RCP_ACF_OP_WRITE. NOTE (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group D): the write-response counterpart of REQ-MDIO-014 -- see that entry's own note and REQ-MDIO-021.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.13.3 Figure 43/Table 60, TC18.txt L6065-6088 (see REQ-MDIO-021)

requirements.title: rcp_ep_mdio_decode_write_response() validates and decodes either ACF_ABB or ACF_GBB MDIO write responses in this module's own packed-words layout
requirements.text: rcp_ep_mdio_decode_write_response() shall accept either an ACF_ABB or ACF_GBB frame, return RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_SHORT_FRAME for a frame too short for the applicable header or declared payload, RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_WRONG_BUS for a mismatched byte_bus_id, RCP_EP_MDIO_ERR_BAD_WORD_COUNT for an odd payload length or more than RCP_EP_MDIO_MAX_BURST_WORDS words, and otherwise RCP_EP_MDIO_OK with the accepted packed word bytes, word count, transaction number, and timed/timestamp populated. NOTE (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group D): see REQ-MDIO-018's own note and REQ-MDIO-021 for this payload layout's own non-TC18-wire-format basis.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.13.3 Figure 43/Table 60, TC18.txt L6065-6088 (see REQ-MDIO-021)

requirements.title: rcp_pwrmode_string() returns a unique human-readable name
requirements.text: rcp_pwrmode_string() shall return a unique, non-empty name for each defined rcp_pwrmode_t constant, and a non-NULL name for any other value.

requirements.title: rcp_pwrmode_strerror() returns a non-NULL message for every error code
requirements.text: rcp_pwrmode_strerror() shall return a non-NULL, non-empty message for each rcp_pwrmode_errc_t value, and a non-NULL message for any unrecognized value.

requirements.title: rcp_pwrmode_cold_start_lifecycle_target() names the cold-start re-init target
requirements.text: rcp_pwrmode_cold_start_lifecycle_target() shall return RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED.
requirements.tc18: §12.4.1 ("After a cold start the RC Server will be in its configured lifecycle state."), TC18.txt L2665 -- NOTE: TC18 requires restoring the actually-configured state, not always HW_UNCONFIGURED; that divergence is a known, separately-tracked gap, see REQ-PWRMODE-014 (not this requirement, which documents the mechanism c-RCP actually implements)

requirements.title: rcp_pwrmode_transition() implements the general power-mode transition table
requirements.text: rcp_pwrmode_transition() shall succeed with RCP_PWRMODE_START_HOT for Normal<->StandBy and for a mode transitioning to itself; shall succeed with RCP_PWRMODE_START_COLD for Normal/StandBy->Sleep, any mode->Unpowered, and Unpowered->Normal; and shall fail with RCP_PWRMODE_ERR_INVALID_TRANSITION (leaving *mode unchanged) for Sleep->Normal and for any other transition not named above.
requirements.tc18: §12.4 ("The RC Server may support different power modes"), TC18.txt L2644

requirements.title: rcp_pwrmode_hotstart_required() is required for every wake path, network included
requirements.text: CORRECTED by REQ-PWRMODE-020's fix: this entry's own original text ("shall return false for RCP_PWRMODE_WAKE_VIA_NETWORK") baked in the exact divergence its own citation note already flagged as a known gap -- rcp_pwrmode_hotstart_required() now shall return true for both RCP_PWRMODE_WAKE_VIA_PIN and RCP_PWRMODE_WAKE_VIA_NETWORK, matching TC18 §12.4.1's own "proceed as before" text (a network wake runs the same handshake a pin wake does, skipping only the literal interface-re-enable sub-step, a hardware-level nuance this module's state machine does not represent specially).
requirements.tc18: §12.4.1 ("If the wake-up source was a TC14/TC10 wake-up request on the network this will also wake the RC Server, but it will directly check for the network availability and proceed as before."), TC18.txt L2680-2681

requirements.title: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_init() sets the initial handshake state
requirements.text: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_init() shall set hs->step to RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_NOT_STARTED, hs->wakeup_attempts to 0, and hs->wakeup_repeat_limit to repeat_limit.
requirements.tc18: §12.4.1 ("Hot-start-up procedure:"), TC18.txt L2671 -- the initial (not-yet-started) state of the procedure described in L2672-2678

requirements.title: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_iface_reenabled() implements handshake step (a)
requirements.text: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_iface_reenabled() shall, when hs->step == RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_NOT_STARTED, advance hs->step to RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_IFACE_REENABLED and return true; otherwise it shall leave hs unchanged and return false.
requirements.tc18: §12.4.1 ("...it will first enable the network interface, check if the network is available and if not initiate a WakeUp to be sent via the network."), TC18.txt L2672-2673

requirements.title: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_wakeup_attempt() implements handshake step (b)
requirements.text: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_wakeup_attempt() shall, when hs->step != RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_IFACE_REENABLED, leave hs unchanged and return false; otherwise it shall increment hs->wakeup_attempts, and if echoed is true advance hs->step to RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_ECHOED and return true, else if hs->wakeup_attempts has reached hs->wakeup_repeat_limit advance hs->step to RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_FAILED and return false, else leave hs->step unchanged and return true.
requirements.tc18: §12.4.1 ("...the RC Server will send via the responder stream which is configured for the original standby request a repetitive response to the sleep request with a WakeUp message and the WakeUp source. The message will be repeated until a valid AVTPDU from the sleep request Client is received."), TC18.txt L2674-2676

requirements.title: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_resume_queues() implements handshake step (c)
requirements.text: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_resume_queues() shall, when hs->step == RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_ECHOED, advance hs->step to RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_COMPLETE and return true; otherwise it shall leave hs unchanged and return false.
requirements.tc18: §12.4.1 ("After reception of valid message from the sleep request Client all used endpoints and response queues will be enabled."), TC18.txt L2677-2678

requirements.title: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_is_complete() reports handshake completion
requirements.text: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_is_complete() shall return true iff hs->step == RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_COMPLETE.
requirements.tc18: §12.4.1 ("After reception of valid message from the sleep request Client all used endpoints and response queues will be enabled."), TC18.txt L2677-2678 -- the completed end-state of the hot-start-up procedure

requirements.title: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_has_failed() reports handshake failure
requirements.text: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_has_failed() shall return true iff hs->step == RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_FAILED.
requirements.tc18: §12.4.1 ("Repetition time of the message can be configured inside the WakeUp EP."), TC18.txt L2676-2677 -- TC18 bounds the repetition by a configurable time rather than a configurable attempt count; c-RCP's wakeup_repeat_limit/has_failed() is this implementation's own finite-attempt realization of that bound, not itself named in the cited text

requirements.title: rcp_pwrmode_wake_from_sleep() classifies hot vs. cold wake starts
requirements.text: rcp_pwrmode_wake_from_sleep() shall fail with RCP_PWRMODE_ERR_INVALID_TRANSITION when *mode != RCP_PWRMODE_SLEEP; otherwise it shall set *mode to RCP_PWRMODE_NORMAL and report *out_start_kind as RCP_PWRMODE_START_HOT when !rcp_pwrmode_hotstart_required(path) or when handshake is non-NULL and rcp_pwrmode_handshake_is_complete(handshake), and as RCP_PWRMODE_START_COLD otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §12.4.1 ("There are two types of start-up: a cold start (after power-on or wake-up from sleep) and a hot start (=wake-up from StandBy)."), TC18.txt L2663-2664

requirements.title: rcp_pwrmode_check_entry() gates StandBy/Sleep entry requests
requirements.text: rcp_pwrmode_check_entry() shall return RCP_PWRMODE_ENTRY_REFUSED when gate is NULL or any of gate->wup_status_clear, gate->endpoint_idle, gate->response_queue_empty is false, and RCP_PWRMODE_ENTRY_OK otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §12.5 ("The RC Server will reject requests to enter sleep or standby mode and send an error message with error code = REQUEST_CANCELED, when: The wake-up event register (wup_status) is not cleared / At least one EP is not idle / In at least one responder queue there is a message pending for transmission."), TC18.txt L2703-2708

requirements.title: rcp_ep_wakeup_functional_cfg_init() zero-initializes a wakeup functional config
requirements.text: rcp_ep_wakeup_functional_cfg_init() shall zero-initialize cfg (including every sources[] entry) and initialize cfg->common via rcp_regmap_ep_functional_cfg_init().

requirements.title: rcp_ep_wakeup_functional_cfg_writable() delegates to the shared field-authorization logic
requirements.text: rcp_ep_wakeup_functional_cfg_writable() shall return rcp_lifecycle_field_writable(state, RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W, writer).

requirements.title: rcp_ep_wakeup_source_asserted() applies one source's own polarity
requirements.text: rcp_ep_wakeup_source_asserted() shall return true iff cfg.enabled is true and pin_level equals cfg.active_high.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.2 Table 40 (wake-up source pin configuration, IO_SRC[15:11]), TC18.txt L4533; reduced to a single active_high/active_low sense rather than Table 40's six-value IO_SRC encoding -- see the pre-existing gap REQ-WAKEUP-022

requirements.title: rcp_ep_wakeup_any_source_asserted() reports whether any configured source is asserted
requirements.text: rcp_ep_wakeup_any_source_asserted() shall return false when fcfg is NULL or when pin_levels is NULL with pin_level_count > 0, and otherwise return true iff rcp_ep_wakeup_source_asserted() is true for at least one of the first min(pin_level_count, RCP_EP_WAKEUP_MAX_SOURCES) source/pin_level pairs.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.1 ("the endpoint listens to configurable IO signals for activity... When the WakeUp endpoint detects activity during sleep mode it wakes up the RC Server"), TC18.txt L4484-4488; §13.7.2.2 Table 39 (ep1 - functional configuration), TC18.txt L4496-4515 (wup_nr_io_pins_max, io_scr1/2 entries) -- see the pre-existing gap REQ-WAKEUP-021 for the reduced register model

requirements.title: rcp_ep_wakeup_wup_status_init() clears the wup_status latch
requirements.text: rcp_ep_wakeup_wup_status_init() shall set s->latched to false.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.2 Table 39 (ep1 - functional configuration), TC18.txt L4496-4515 (wup_status, "Indication of wake-up source, writing '1' clears the flag. Each bit represents a wake-up source"), TC18.txt L4505-4507 -- modeled as a single latch rather than a 16-bit per-source bitfield, see the pre-existing gap REQ-WAKEUP-021

requirements.title: rcp_ep_wakeup_wup_status_latch() sets the wup_status latch
requirements.text: rcp_ep_wakeup_wup_status_latch() shall set s->latched to true.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.2 Table 39 (ep1 - functional configuration), TC18.txt L4496-4515 (wup_status register), TC18.txt L4505-4507 -- see the pre-existing gap REQ-WAKEUP-021

requirements.title: rcp_ep_wakeup_wup_status_clear() clears the wup_status latch
requirements.text: rcp_ep_wakeup_wup_status_clear() shall set s->latched to false.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.2 Table 39 (ep1 - functional configuration), TC18.txt L4496-4515 (wup_status, "writing '1' clears the flag"), TC18.txt L4505-4507 -- see the pre-existing gap REQ-WAKEUP-021

requirements.title: rcp_ep_wakeup_wup_status_is_clear() reports the wup_status latch's state
requirements.text: rcp_ep_wakeup_wup_status_is_clear() shall return !s->latched.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.2 Table 39 (ep1 - functional configuration), TC18.txt L4496-4515 (wup_status register), TC18.txt L4505-4507 -- see the pre-existing gap REQ-WAKEUP-021

requirements.title: rcp_ep_wakeup_strerror() returns a non-NULL message for every error code
requirements.text: rcp_ep_wakeup_strerror() shall return a non-NULL, non-empty message for each rcp_ep_wakeup_errc_t value, and a non-NULL message for any unrecognized value.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_wakeup_encode_sleepcmd_request() encodes a fixed-opcode SleepCMD request
requirements.text: rcp_ep_wakeup_encode_sleepcmd_request() shall encode an ACF_ABB message with op RCP_ACF_OP_NONE whose 1-byte payload is RCP_EP_WAKEUP_SLEEPCMD_OPCODE, padded to the next quadlet by rcp_acf_encode_abb() itself; the request carries no target-mode field and unconditionally means Sleep.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.3 Figure 23 (Endpoint sleep request), TC18.txt L4558-4563, directly confirmed against the rendered PDF page image: a 1-byte SleepCMD opcode followed by an undifferentiated padding region with no target-mode field; "SleepCMD is coded as 0xA5.", TC18.txt L4565; "bring the RC Server implementation to sleep mode" (never Standby), TC18.txt L4555 -- corrected 2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group E, superseding this entry's prior (incorrect) reading of a 2-byte, target_mode-selecting payload

requirements.title: rcp_ep_wakeup_decode_sleepcmd_request() validates and decodes a SleepCMD request
