requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.1 Figure 18 defines one generic configuration request — evt[2:0] = 111b, byte_msg_payload = a relative register start address within the addressed endpoint's EP_func section followed by configuration data — usable against EVERY endpoint type either through the RC Server (EP0) register map or directly by byte_bus_id. c-RCP implements this shape for all eleven endpoint types (twelve modules, since PWM_OUT and PWM_IN share src/ep_pwm.c): rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_reconfig()/rcp_ep_pwm_in_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_pwm.c), rcp_ep_gpio_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_gpio.c), rcp_ep_spi_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_spi.c), rcp_ep_i2c_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_i2c.c), rcp_ep_uart_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_uart.c), rcp_ep_lin_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_lin.c), rcp_ep_adc_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_adc.c), rcp_ep_iseled_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_iseled.c), rcp_ep_mdio_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_mdio.c), rcp_ep_wakeup_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_wakeup.c), and, as of 2026-08-12 (issue #201, REQ-CANEP-028), rcp_ep_can_apply_reconfig() (src/ep_can.c) -- CAN was the last of the eleven endpoint types still exposing no EP_func addressed-write path at all; this entry's own text was not updated when REQ-CANEP-028 closed that gap, a stale-precedent oversight caught and corrected 2026-08-13 (issue #334), matching this codebase's own established REQ-UART-032/REQ-CANEP-028 precedent for a requirement whose blocker was independently closed by later, differently-filed work. IMPLEMENTED. As with every other endpoint type's own module, routing a decoded evt[2:0]==111b request to this function rather than the endpoint's own normal read/write decoder is a caller's own responsibility (see e.g. rcp_ep_gpio_apply_masked_write()'s own doc comment for the identical division of responsibility) -- this requirement is about the primitive existing and being reachable via the generic §12.7.1 mechanism for every endpoint type, not about any one caller's own wiring, matching how the other ten endpoint types were already scored. CAN's own register block remains deliberately incomplete in one narrower respect tracked separately (REQ-CANEP-029's acceptance-filter address collision; the undecoded bit-timing registers, whose sub-field layout TC18 does not specify) -- neither blocks this requirement, which is about the addressed-write mechanism's own existence, not full register coverage.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints + Figure 18, TC18.txt L2464-2466, L2473-2479

requirements.title: Every endpoint must publish EP_LEN at EP_func offset 0x00 and ignore a write overrunning it
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.1 requires that every endpoint publish its EP_LEN parameter at EP_func relative start_address 0x00, and that any byte_msg_payload whose length plus start_address exceeds EP_LEN be ignored in its entirety. c-RCP satisfies this for all eleven endpoint types: RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_REG_EP_LEN and RCP_EP_PWM_IN_REG_EP_LEN both at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_pwm.h), RCP_EP_GPIO_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_gpio.h), RCP_EP_SPI_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_spi.h), RCP_EP_I2C_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_i2c.h), RCP_EP_UART_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_uart.h), RCP_EP_LIN_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_lin.h), RCP_EP_ADC_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_adc.h), RCP_EP_ISELED_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_iseled.h), RCP_EP_MDIO_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_mdio.h), RCP_EP_WAKEUP_REG_EP_LEN at 0x0000 (include/rcp/ep_wakeup.h), and, as of 2026-08-12 (issue #201, REQ-CANEP-028), can_ep_len at 0x0000 fixed to RCP_EP_CAN_EP_FUNC_LEN (include/rcp/ep_can.h) -- with the out-of-range write rejected via RCP_EP_CAN_RECONFIG_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE in rcp_ep_can_apply_reconfig(), the same "span would extend past EP_LEN" rejection pattern every other endpoint type's own apply_reconfig() already uses. This entry's own text was not updated when REQ-CANEP-028 closed CAN's gap, a stale-precedent oversight caught and corrected 2026-08-13 (issue #334), matching REQ-CFG-011's own identical correction (see that entry for the full precedent reasoning). IMPLEMENTED: the specification's one universal bounds check on configuration writes now exists at all eleven endpoint types.

requirements.title: rcp_config_manifest_free() releases every owned array and zeroes the manifest
requirements.text: rcp_config_manifest_free(m) shall free m's hw_pin_map, endpoints, and streams arrays and then zero *m in place, leaving it safe to reuse or discard.

requirements.title: A discovery request while the discovery stream is already claimed is answered with a stream-occupied error
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_discovery_claim_note_request() (discovery.h/discovery.c) now returns bool -- true when the discovery claim was open and granted, false when refused because it was already held by an unlapsed claimant (TC18 §12.3, Figure 16's own two "Discovery request received" transitions, applied uniformly regardless of requester identity: a different client or the current claimant re-requesting are both refused). A caller now has a real signal to act on instead of an unreportable silent decline. STILL OPEN: DISCOVERY_STREAM_OCCUPIED is a Figure-16-diagram-only label with no corresponding numbered code in TC18 §12.9.6 Table 30 (rcp_wire_error_t stops at RCP_ERROR_CHAIN_ERROR, 17) -- unlike LOCKED_CONFIG_ACCESS (which cleanly maps onto RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS, the only numbered code with a semantically matching name), no numbered code here has an obviously corresponding meaning, so this codebase does not invent one; which wire error code (if any) a caller should send for the false case remains a genuine, unresolved ambiguity (same class as REQ-ACF-012's RCP_ACF_MTV_UNCERTAIN).
requirements.tc18: §12.3, TC18.txt L2447-L2450 and L2481-L2483 (Figure 17, "RC Server lifecycle states", TC18.txt L2517) -- CORRECTED 2026-08-13, citation-drift fix (issue #341 lineage, found while investigating issue #338): the cached TC18.txt's own lifecycle-diagram is Figure 17 in the current RC5 baseline ("Figure 17 - RC Server lifecycle states", TC18.txt L2517), not "Figure 16" as this citation previously said -- Figure 16 in the current RC5 text is an unrelated diagram ("Cancellation of a single, specific request", TC18.txt L2158). Line numbers corrected to the real current location; the underlying technical claim is unchanged, re-verified directly against the fresh text before touching this citation.

requirements.title: per-stream sequence-number enforcement (rx_enforce_seq)
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-13 (issue #338, tc18-gap backlog PR B): TC18 §12.7.7 Table 24, relative address 0x000D bit 1 (rx_enforce_seq, 1 bit, R/W*), requires that a request only be filed for execution if the sequence number carried in its AVTPDU has increased relative to the previously accepted request on that stream. rcp_e2e_seq_evaluate() (e2e.h/e2e.c) was already a complete, directly-testable primitive; the previously-missing integration is now real: rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame()/_dispatch_frame_e2e() (mock.c) take a new sequence_num parameter (the caller-decoded AVTPDU Sequence_Nr, avtp.h's rcp_avtp_ntscf_header_t/rcp_avtp_tscf_header_t) and evaluate it exactly ONCE per frame, before any ACF member is processed -- deliberately NOT added to the lower-level per-member rcp_mock_server_dispatch()/_dispatch_e2e() entry points, since sequence_num is a property of the whole AVTPDU, not of any one member packed inside it (a per-member evaluation would spuriously reject a legitimate 2nd+ member of a multi-member frame as a replay against the 1st member's own just-advanced tracker state). A replayed/reordered sequence_num now rejects the WHOLE frame (every member comes back the new RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_SEQ_ERROR), using a new per-request-stream rcp_e2e_seq_tracker_t array (rcp_mock_server_t.seq_tracker[], mirroring request_stream_cfg[]'s own indexing). An unresolvable stream_id (rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_resolve_index() returning 0) skips the gate entirely, the same fail-toward-no-action disposition already established for the overflow-safestate broadcast (REQ-E2E-030).

requirements.title: sequence-error safe-state escalation (rx_seq_safestate_enable)
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-13 (issue #338, tc18-gap backlog PR B): TC18 §12.7.7 Table 24, relative address 0x000D bit 2 (rx_seq_safestate_enable, 1 bit, R/W*), requires that a detected sequence-number discontinuity (a Sequence_Nr that did not advance by exactly one increment) bring all endpoints bound to that request stream into their configured safe state. rcp_e2e_seq_evaluate()'s result.enter_safe_state field was already correct; the cross-endpoint broadcast half (rcp_mock_server_broadcast_safe_state(), issue #335, already proven for REQ-E2E-030/REQ-E2E-045) is now wired to it too, in the same once-per-frame gate REQ-E2E-028's own text describes -- checked regardless of the frame's own accept/reject outcome (a gap advanced by more than one is evidence of a problem even when ordering itself still held, so a still-accepted frame with a discontinuity broadcasts safe state without rejecting that frame's own members).

requirements.title: request-storage-overflow safe-state escalation (rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable)
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (issue #335, 2026-08-13): rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable's (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 24, relative address 0x000D bit 5, 1 bit, R/W*) full two-part rule is now wired end-to-end. Part 1 (single-endpoint, pre-existing): rcp_server_endpoint_admit() sets *out_error = RCP_ERROR_REQUEST_STORAGE_OVERFLOW on a request-store-full admission outcome (src/server.c), which mock.c's finish_admission() turns into a real Table 30 error response via rcp_acf_build_error_response(). Part 2 (stream-wide, closed this batch): rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_byte_bus_ids_for_stream() (regmap.h/regmap.c) is the missing cross-endpoint query over TC18 §12.7.8 Table 23's own EP_ID_config content model (the wire-defined "which endpoints are bound to which request stream" table -- it already existed with a full render/parse codec, REQ-RMAP-052, it simply had no caller-facing query over it); rcp_mock_server_broadcast_safe_state() (mock.h/mock.c) is the actuator, driven from dispatch_plain()'s own overflow check via rcp_e2e_overflow_should_enter_safe_state() and rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_resolve_index(). "Drive toward safe state" is, concretely, this library's own already-established watchdog-purge action (rcp_server_endpoint_watchdog_purge()/e2e.h's keep-only-the-safety-sequence rule) applied to every byte_bus_id EP_ID_config reports bound to the affected stream, not merely the one endpoint that overflowed. Proven end-to-end by test_conditional_dispatch.c's test_overflow_on_one_endpoint_broadcasts_safe_state_to_stream_siblings() (positive) and test_overflow_does_not_broadcast_without_an_ep_id_map() (negative control, confirms the broadcast is a genuine consequence of EP_ID_config content, not an unconditional side effect).
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24, TC18.txt L3252-L3256 -- CORRECTED 2026-08-13, citation-drift fix (issue #341 lineage, own follow-up self-check after PR #379's issue #335 batch left this citation untouched -- only status/text were updated there, not tc18). Table 24's real current location is TC18.txt L3217-L3293 ("Table 24: Request stream configuration"), not L2865-2882 as this citation previously said. Line numbers corrected to the real current location; the underlying technical claim is unchanged, re-verified directly against the fresh text before touching this citation.

requirements.title: GPIO request payload is exactly four bytes, mapped LSB-first for endpoints with fewer than 32 pins
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-12, issue #201 Phase 5e): rcp_ep_gpio_decode_write_request() and rcp_ep_gpio_decode_request() reject any GPIO request whose byte_msg_payload is not exactly RCP_EP_GPIO_PAYLOAD_LEN (4) octets with RCP_EP_GPIO_ERR_BAD_PAYLOAD_LEN; the new rcp_ep_gpio_wire_error() maps that local code to the numbered wire code TC18 13.7.4.1 answers with, RCP_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, for a caller building an Error Response frame (acf.h's rcp_acf_build_error_response()) -- closing the deviation this entry previously pinned (the wire code was never reachable from this path). The LSB-first bit-to-pin mapping for an endpoint supporting fewer than RCP_EP_GPIO_MAX_PINS (32) pins was already conformant by construction: this module's fixed bit-index n <-> pin IOn encoding (rcp_ep_gpio_pin_mask()/_pin_get()) never changes based on how many pins a real instance physically has, so pin 0 is always bit 0 regardless -- no code change was needed for that half, only test coverage confirming it explicitly.

requirements.title: GPIO trigger signal numbering (Table 40)
requirements.text: c-RCP implements the three GPIO trigger conditions (rcp_ep_gpio_trigger_fires() for change, rising and falling edges) and now also assigns them TC18 Table 40 (RC1)/Table 43 (RC5) trigger signal numbers via rcp_ep_gpio_trigger_signal_number(): signal 0 is the whole-endpoint 'GPIO EP request execution done' trigger (not modelled by this per-pin function) and, for each pin IOn, signal 3n+1/3n+2/3n+3 is ANY_CHANGE/RISING/FALLING, up to signal 96 for IO31 FALLING. A triggered request naming a Table 40/43 signal number can now be resolved against a (pin_index, trigger) pair by this library.

requirements.title: GPIO functional-config registers: base clock, divider and per-pin debounce (Table 41)
requirements.text: PARTIAL (updated 2026-08-13, tc18-gap backlog PR D, issue #336): rcp_ep_gpio_functional_cfg_t carries ep_status, clk_divider, and a 32-entry debounce[] array, wire-addressable via the real evt[2:0]=111b EP_func mechanism (TC18 Table 41). rcp_ep_gpio_debounce_state_t/rcp_ep_gpio_debounce_sample() (ep_gpio.h/ep_gpio.c) implement the filtering RULE those registers configure -- directly unit-tested (test_ep_gpio.c). DISPATCH-WIRING HALF CLOSED THIS BATCH: test_tc18_gaps_ep.c's own new gpio_dispatch_handler() (an rcp_mock_endpoint_handler_fn registered via the existing, unmodified rcp_mock_server_add_endpoint()) is a real caller that decodes a GPIO write request and calls rcp_ep_gpio_debounce_sample() on every one, proven end-to-end through mock.c's own real dispatch() path (test_gpio_dispatch_debounces_writes_before_reporting_settled_value(): three writes of the same raw value with n=3 settle -- and are reported via a subsequent read -- only on the third, checked after every single write, not just at the end). This is a test-fixture-level reference handler, not new public library API -- mock.c's own file header states it deliberately 'owns none of the per-endpoint wire semantics itself... a caller registers one handler per byte_bus_id', so building this INTO mock.c itself would have contradicted that stated architecture; a caller-supplied handler is exactly the documented mechanism. What remains genuinely open: gpio_base_clk (0x0004) is read-only and always renders 0 -- this module defines no real GPIO clock source, the same architecture-wide constant already established for REQ-ADC-033/every other endpoint type's own base_clk field -- so the periodic sampling CADENCE (gpio_base_clk/gpio_clk_divider-derived) that would drive repeated rcp_ep_gpio_debounce_sample() calls independently of requests remains a caller-owned timer this module never itself runs; this batch's own handler instead samples once per write, a reasonable stand-in but not the real periodic cadence TC18 describes.

requirements.title: GPIO response timing: immediate for a pure read, post-debounce otherwise
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-14): the genuine remaining gap the prior batch's own text found -- "mock.c's own dispatch model is entirely synchronous... actually WAITING the configured debounce time and THEN producing a response... would need a genuinely new mechanism this batch does not add" -- is now closed. New rcp_mock_server_stash_deferred_response()/_take_deferred_response() (mock.h): a caller-facing pair (not GPIO-specific -- mock.c continues to own none of the per-endpoint wire semantics itself, this section's own established file-header boundary) that gives a response a real place to wait once a caller has decided not to answer synchronously, until whatever condition it was genuinely waiting for is later met. Neither function tracks a timer, elapsed time, or an 'is it ready yet' concept of its own -- matching the same 'protocol library, not a scheduler' boundary every other caller-driven-clock primitive in this codebase already uses (e.g. rcp_mock_server_check_watchdog()'s own elapsed_since_last_kick_ms parameter); the caller decides when to stash and when to take. A handler (rcp_mock_endpoint_handler_fn) cannot call either function itself -- it has no srv of its own -- so both are meant to be called by whatever code drives dispatch() itself, alongside it, matching how test_tc18_gaps_ep.c's own new test_gpio_dispatch_deferred_write_response_is_retrievable_once_debounce_settles() uses them: the SAME three-write debounce sequence test_gpio_dispatch_debounces_writes_before_reporting_settled_value() already proved reachable, but on the settling (3rd) write, the TEST itself (not the handler) now stashes the response that write genuinely owes, and a later take_deferred_response() call retrieves it exactly once, carrying that write's own real transaction_num -- proving a genuine 'answer withheld now, delivered later' round trip through mock.c for the first time, not just a response permanently skipped. 2 mutations (the stash assignment itself, and the take-side clear-after-taking step), both caught cleanly. This closes REQ-GPIO-036's own remaining gap only -- REQ-GPIO-035's own separate, still-open concern (gpio_base_clk always renders 0, no real periodic sampling cadence) is untouched by this fix and stays partial on its own terms, the same 'no real clock source' architecture-wide disposition already accepted for REQ-ADC-033 and every other endpoint type's own base_clk field.

requirements.title: A write to a pin configured as input leaves that pin's value unchanged
requirements.text: rcp_ep_gpio_apply_masked_write() shall, for every evt, commit rcp_ep_gpio_apply_write()'s combined result to a bit position only when pins[i] has RCP_REGMAP_PIN_PROP_OUTPUT set, and shall leave that bit position's value from current unchanged when pins[i] does not, regardless of what request or the combinator's result specify for that position.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.3 ("A write request to an input pin is ignored for this input pin"), TC18.txt L4890

requirements.title: I2C functional-config registers beyond i2c_mode, and the Ultra-fast preset, are now modeled
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): c-RCP's rcp_ep_i2c_functional_cfg_t now carries i2c_clock_divider, i2c_trail (minimum trail time between two transactions in I2C clock cycles), and i2c_ep_status alongside i2c_mode (i2c_base_clk is not itself stored -- it has no setter and always renders 0, the same "no real clock source modelled" honesty ep_gpio.h's own gpio_base_clk already commits to); rcp_ep_i2c_mode_valid() now accepts Ultra-fast mode (value 4, 5 Mbit/s). rcp_ep_i2c_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig() implement the whole Table 46 block at corrected addresses: Table 46's own printed relative-address column collides i2c_ep_enable&clr (0x0002) with i2c_base_clk (also printed at 0x0002) and i2c_base_clk's second octet with i2c_ep_status (both printed at 0x0004) -- confirmed via direct visual inspection of the source PDF (physical page 99), not a text-extraction artifact. PWM_OUT's, GPIO's, and SPI's own common EP_func prefixes all place the same five conceptual fields (EP_LEN / a reserved-or-count octet / enable&clr / options / a 16-bit read-only base-clock register) at the identical address sequence 0x0000/0x0001/0x0002/0x0003/0x0004-0x0005, followed by a 16-bit ep_status at 0x0006-0x0007 -- that cross-table pattern is authoritative here too, so i2c_base_clk is placed at 0x0004-0x0005 (not the table's own printed 0x0002), pushing i2c_ep_status to 0x0006-0x0007, i2c_clock_divider to 0x0008, i2c_mode to 0x0009, and i2c_trail to 0x000A (RCP_EP_I2C_EP_FUNC_LEN = 0x000B, 11 octets total). Table 46 still numbers two distinct rows '3' (High-speed 1.7 and 3.4 Mbit/s), an ambiguity ep_i2c.h resolves conservatively in favour of the lower numbering -- this remains unresolved pending spec errata, unrelated to the fixes above.

requirements.title: I2C payload carries the address and the endpoint stays address-format agnostic
requirements.text: The I2C endpoint's request codec shall treat the byte_msg_payload as the complete I2C payload INCLUDING the target address and shall not interpret, validate or rewrite that address -- remaining transparent to whether the transfer uses a 7-bit or a 10-bit address, per TC18 13.7.7.3.

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_render_registers()/_encode_reconfig_request() implement the generic §12.7.1 configuration request for I2C
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): TC18 §12.7.1 Figure 18 defines one generic configuration request -- evt[2:0] = 111b, byte_msg_payload = a relative register start address within the addressed endpoint's EP_func section followed by configuration data -- usable against every endpoint type. rcp_ep_i2c_decode_transfer_request() already correctly rejected evt[2:0] = 111b as not a plain transfer (RCP_EP_I2C_ERR_BAD_EVT, via acf.h's rcp_acf_evt_row2_is_plain()), but no counterpart function implemented that path at all. rcp_ep_i2c_render_registers() serializes cfg's whole (corrected-address) Table 46 block; rcp_ep_i2c_encode_reconfig_request() encodes an ACF_ABB write request (op=WRITE, evt=111b) carrying a 16-bit big-endian start address followed by data, matching PWM_OUT's/GPIO's/SPI's own encode_reconfig_request() shape.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints + Figure 19 (renumbered from Figure 18 by the RC5 rebaseline), TC18.txt L2844-2860

requirements.title: rcp_ep_i2c_apply_reconfig()/_reconfig_strerror() apply the addressed configuration write and never return NULL for a status message
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): rcp_ep_i2c_apply_reconfig() decodes the address+data payload TC18 §12.7.1 defines and patches cfg's Table 46 register block at octet granularity, then adopts the whole block atomically -- a write whose start_address+length exceeds RCP_EP_I2C_EP_FUNC_LEN is rejected and cfg left entirely unchanged (RCP_EP_I2C_RECONFIG_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE), matching §12.7.1's own 'such a payload is to be ignored' rule; octets landing on a read-only register (EP_LEN, the reserved octet, or base_clk) are silently skipped while the rest of the span is still applied. rcp_ep_i2c_reconfig_strerror() never returns NULL, including for an unrecognized error code.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints, TC18.txt L2844-2860

requirements.title: A lifecycle-state change is refused with EPs_NOT_IDLE while any other endpoint is busy
requirements.text: PARTIAL: verified directly against the primary-source PDF's own Figure 16 image (not just the pre-existing text extraction, which renders this diagram too poorly to trust for a design decision) -- confirms the EPs_NOT_IDLE gate applies to exactly two transitions: the HW_UNCONFIGURED -> HW_CONFIGURED advance ("...& all other EPs are Idle -> send positive response") and either reset-to-HW_UNCONFIGURED transition ("...& other EPs are not Idle -> send error response EPs_NOT_IDLE"); the HW_CONFIGURED -> RCP_CONFIGURED advance's own label makes no mention of idleness and is correctly NOT gated. rcp_lifecycle_transition() now takes an all_other_eps_idle parameter and rejects with the new RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_EPS_NOT_IDLE for both gated transitions when false. Not fully IMPLEMENTED: TC18's own diagram names this outcome "EPs_NOT_IDLE" but that name maps to none of the seventeen numbered wire error codes errors.h models (§12.9.6's own table) -- a genuine TC18 inconsistency (the diagram-only name has no corresponding numbered code anywhere in the specification) this library cannot resolve by inventing a mapping, so RCP_LIFECYCLE_ERR_EPS_NOT_IDLE remains a local-only lifecycle error code, not yet wired to a wire response.
requirements.tc18: §12.3, TC18.txt L2492-L2495 and L2504-L2506 (Figure 17, "RC Server lifecycle states", TC18.txt L2517) -- CORRECTED 2026-08-13, citation-drift fix (issue #341 lineage, found while investigating issue #338): the cached TC18.txt's own lifecycle-diagram is Figure 17 in the current RC5 baseline ("Figure 17 - RC Server lifecycle states", TC18.txt L2517), not "Figure 16" as this citation previously said -- Figure 16 in the current RC5 text is an unrelated diagram ("Cancellation of a single, specific request", TC18.txt L2158). Line numbers corrected to the real current location; the underlying technical claim is unchanged, re-verified directly against the fresh text before touching this citation.

requirements.title: HW_config's own lock rule (RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC) also governs EP_GEN_CFG and QUEUE_CFG writes, per Figure 17
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (issue #338, 2026-08-13): re-investigated by rendering the actual PDF page (pdftoppm, page 51) rather than trusting text extraction alone, per this project's own established practice for this exact diagram. Confirmed unambiguously: Figure 17's own HW_CONFIGURED-box transition reads "Request on discovery stream or known stream/bb_id for configuration to HW_CONFIG or QUEUE_CFG or EP_GEN_CFG -> send error response LOCKED_CONFIG_ACCESS", explicitly contrasted against a separate, adjacent transition for "configuration to unlocked registers -> handle cfg and send positive response". This directly contradicts the generic R/W* access-level legend (§12.7.5, "write access prohibited if in lifecycle state RCP_configured") that Table 31 (ep_generic_cfg, §13.2) and Table 27 (response_queue_cfg, §12.7.9) both implicitly fall back to, since neither table's own prose carries an explicit table-specific override the way HW_config's own §12.7.6 does ("This configuration table can only be changed in the life-cycle state HW_unconfigured") -- a genuine TC18 prose/diagram contradiction, now catalogued as item 60 in TC18_spec_defects_report.md. Resolved in favor of the diagram (the more specific, deliberate statement on exactly this topic, consistent with HW_config's own already-implemented override) rather than the generic legend -- fail-closed, the safer failure mode for an access-control gate. This also resolves the catalog's own internal inconsistency: rcp_lifecycle_field_write_error()'s doc comment (lifecycle.h) already named "REQ-LIFECYCLE-023's HW_CONFIG/QUEUE_CFG/EP_GEN_CFG blocks" as belonging to RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC even before this fix -- src/regmap.c's actual write dispatch for ep_generic_cfg and response_queue_cfg had simply never been updated to match, using RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR (and, for response_queue_cfg, a mixed per-field W-star/W-plus split) instead -- a real, now-fixed conformance bug, not merely a citation error. response_queue_cfg's own STREAM_UID/flush_on_count/Flush_time fields retain their independent R/W-plus lock-bit check (TC18's own words, §12.7.8, "independently of the lifecycle state that governs W and W*") within the HW_UNCONFIGURED window HW_GENERIC still permits -- REQ-RMAP-055's own W-plus primitive is unchanged; only which lifecycle-state rule gates the table as a whole changed. REQ-RMAP-047's own scope (request_stream_cfg, Table 24 -- not named in Figure 17's lock list) is unaffected. Proven end-to-end by test_tc18_gaps_regmap.c's own new subtest 7pre in test_ep0_dispatcher_denies_unauthorized_writes_before_applying_or_bounds_checking() (writes to ep_generic_cfg/response_queue_cfg during HW_CONFIGURED, previously permitted, now correctly rejected with LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS); subtests 5/6/7 (already-existing RCP_CONFIGURED-state denials) updated to reflect the corrected reasoning without any change to their own assertions.
requirements.tc18: §12.3, TC18.txt L2485-L2488 (Figure 17, "RC Server lifecycle states", TC18.txt L2517; directly confirmed against the rendered PDF page image, not just text extraction)

requirements.title: A denied configuration write is answered with LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS (state-locked) or UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS (writer-denied)
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED, corrected a second time after a closer primary-source re-reading: this entry's text previously (a) cited RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS as the sole expected code, then (b) after checking only TC18 §13.7.1.2's prose, concluded the opposite -- that every denial maps to RCP_ERROR_UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS uniformly. Both were incomplete: checking Figure 17's own diagram (page 51) in addition to the prose reveals TC18 actually specifies two distinct cases. Figure 17's HW_CONFIGURED-box transition -- "Request on discovery stream or known stream/bb_id for configuration to HW_CONFIG or QUEUE_CFG or EP_GEN_CFG -> send error response LOCKED_CONFIG_ACCESS" -- covers an otherwise-authorized request denied purely because the target block is state-locked (every RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC denial, and a FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR denial once RCP_CONFIGURED); LOCKED_CONFIG_ACCESS does not literally match any of the seventeen numbered wire error codes' own strings, but is unambiguously RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS (4), the only numbered code with a semantically matching name (the same prose-vs-table naming variance already documented for POCI_FAILURE). §13.7.1.2's own prose -- "Writing to a write prohibited register (e.g. lock bit for map set) creates a response with err=1 and an error code UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS" -- is the separate, narrower case: a writer/frame-specific denial on top of an otherwise-permitting state. rcp_lifecycle_field_write_error() now distinguishes these (comparing the real writer's verdict against a maximally-privileged writer's verdict for the same state/kind, to isolate which case applies) rather than collapsing them to one code. Citation corrected 2026-08-13 (no-status-field audit pass): this entry's own citation previously named "Figure 16's own diagram (page 42)", verified against a PDF revision with a 2026-07-14 footer date (matching the pre-extracted TC18.txt reference file). The currently authoritative PDF (OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf, footer date 2026-07-31) has since gained additional front matter/content, shifting this same diagram -- content and wording otherwise unchanged, including the LOCKED_CONFIG_ACCESS transition text quoted above -- to page 51 and renumbering it Figure 17. TC18.txt's own line citations (L2110-L2113, L4039-L4041) remain valid for that file's own pagination and are unaffected by this correction.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2, TC18.txt L4039-L4041; Figure 17 in the current 2026-07-31-footer PDF revision, page 51 of its own image (shown as Figure 16 on page 42 in the earlier 2026-07-14-footer revision that TC18.txt itself was extracted from, TC18.txt L2110-L2113; diagram content and LOCKED_CONFIG_ACCESS transition text are identical between the two revisions)

requirements.title: Requests on an unknown stream/byte_bus_id are ignored in HW_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: PARTIAL: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-14 directly against TC18.txt's own current §12.3.1.2/§12.3.1.3 prose (not just Figure 17's diagram, this requirement's prior verification pass) before touching this text -- §12.3.1.3's own RCP_CONFIGURED paragraph reads: "all write access to configuration spaces is locked and only write access to the EP's functional configurations is allowed via their dedicated stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations or via root client access EP0" -- this defines what IS allowed (an EP's own dedicated association, or root client) but, like Figure 17's own box, still specifies no disposition for a request that matches NEITHER case. The new rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_is_valid_association() primitive built for REQ-LIFECYCLE-031 (issue #341 lineage, same session) does not change this finding: that primitive answers 'is this stream_id/byte_bus_id combination currently configured at all', not 'what happens to a request that fails to match one during RCP_CONFIGURED's own broader per-EP dispatch' -- the latter is what remains genuine spec silence. Inventing an ignore/reject disposition TC18 itself never specifies would risk introducing non-conformant behavior, not fixing a gap -- the same standing conclusion as before, now re-confirmed against the prose directly rather than only the diagram. Tracked as an open architecture question, same underlying "no wire-level concept of a valid stream_id/byte_bus_id association" limitation as REQ-LIFECYCLE-034 -- though as of REQ-LIFECYCLE-031's own fix, that limitation is now only genuinely open for THIS specific question (RCP_CONFIGURED's own unmatched-request disposition), not for the concept itself, which now exists and is available to whichever future spec revision or product decision needs it.
requirements.tc18: §12.3, TC18.txt L2476-L2480 (Figure 17, "RC Server lifecycle states", TC18.txt L2517) -- CORRECTED 2026-08-13, citation-drift fix (issue #341 lineage, found while investigating issue #338): the cached TC18.txt's own lifecycle-diagram is Figure 17 in the current RC5 baseline ("Figure 17 - RC Server lifecycle states", TC18.txt L2517), not "Figure 16" as this citation previously said -- Figure 16 in the current RC5 text is an unrelated diagram ("Cancellation of a single, specific request", TC18.txt L2158). Line numbers corrected to the real current location; the underlying technical claim is unchanged, re-verified directly against the fresh text before touching this citation.

requirements.title: In HW_UNCONFIGURED only the discovery claimant's stream may configure the server
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: primary-source re-verification found the enforcement point this entry originally named was wrong -- rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() is a frame-admission filter (subtype/msg-type/byte_bus_id only), not where TC18's own write-authorization rules live in this codebase (that is rcp_lifecycle_field_writable(), the same layering REQ-LIFECYCLE-027/030/036 already established). The real gap was RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC's HW_UNCONFIGURED branch admitting any writer unconditionally, with no authorization concept at all. Fixed: HW_GENERIC is now writable in HW_UNCONFIGURED only when writer.via_discovery_stream is set, matching TC18 §12.3.1.1's "All configurations must be run via the stream which was used for discovery." Deriving via_discovery_stream from a real frame's stream_id against rcp_discovery_claim_is_claimant() (src/discovery.c) is caller composition, per discovery.h's own documented architecture -- the same division of responsibility REQ-LIFECYCLE-027's via_non_unicast_frame member already established for this library.

requirements.title: Write requests are accepted only from unicast frames
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.3.1.1, §12.3.1.2 and §12.3.1.3 each state (once per lifecycle state) that a write request is accepted only when carried in a unicast frame. rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t gained a via_non_unicast_frame member (l2.h's new rcp_l2_mac_is_unicast() -- REQ-L2-011 -- is the primitive an integrator uses to classify a real frame's destination MAC into it), and rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() now ANDs !writer.via_non_unicast_frame into every kind/state that would otherwise be writable, uniformly across HW_GENERIC, FUNCTIONAL_W and FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR. rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() gained a matching via_unicast parameter so its one real derivation path plumbs the same classification through. rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() deliberately still takes no destination-MAC input: TC18's rule is scoped to write requests specifically, not general frame admission, so gating happens only at the field_writable() layer where the write path already lives, not at should_accept()'s frame-admission layer.

requirements.title: HW_CONFIGURED drops TSCF-headed AVTPDUs regardless of time-sync support
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.3.1.2 (whose own printed heading confusingly repeats "HW_UNCONFIGURED" -- verified against the primary-source PDF directly to rule out an extraction artifact; the section's actual content is unambiguously about HW_CONFIGURED, distinct from the correctly-labeled §12.3.1.1 immediately preceding it) requires TSCF-headed AVTPDUs to be dropped in HW_CONFIGURED without further response, unconditionally. rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() now drops a TSCF-headed frame in HW_CONFIGURED regardless of time_sync_supported, the same unconditional rule already applied to HW_UNCONFIGURED.

requirements.title: HW_CONFIGURED drops ACF_GBB-format requests without response
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (resolved differently than originally scoped): this entry's own remaining exposure -- a conditional (ACF_GBB) request literally addressed to EP0 in HW_CONFIGURED, the one case REQ-LIFECYCLE-032's byte_bus_id restriction did not already cover -- turned out to directly conflict with TC18 §12.7's own text once REQ-LIFECYCLE-033 was scoped: §12.7 requires EP0-addressed non-STANDARD requests to be answered with REQUEST_REJECTED, not silently dropped as this entry's own §12.3.1.2 citation demands. Resolved by reading §12.3.1.2's "requests in ACF_GBB format[are dropped]" as the general, non-EP0-scoped rule (still correctly enforced -- any non-EP0 byte_bus_id is dropped by REQ-LIFECYCLE-032's own restriction, unconditionally of acf_msg_type) and §12.7's REQUEST_REJECTED rule as the more specific, EP0-scoped override that governs for exactly this residual case. rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() now returns RCP_LIFECYCLE_REJECT (not RCP_LIFECYCLE_DROP) for a non-ABB message addressed to EP0 in HW_CONFIGURED -- see REQ-LIFECYCLE-033's own entry for the implementation detail, and that function's own header doc comment for the full reconciliation between the two TC18 sections.

requirements.title: In HW_CONFIGURED, EP0 write access to another endpoint's configuration requires the root client or the discovery stream
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.3.1.2 permits cross-endpoint write access via EP0 in HW_CONFIGURED only for a configured root client or via the discovery stream. rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() now gates RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W's HW_CONFIGURED branch on `authorized || writer.via_discovery_stream`, where authorized is the same via_root_client_ep0 || via_owning_stream formula already used for RCP_CONFIGURED, and via_discovery_stream is a new rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t member (REQ-LIFECYCLE-036 closed the same gate for FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR in the same change, since both requirements reduce to the identical HW_CONFIGURED authorization condition).

requirements.title: A lifecycle-state write is accepted only from the discovery stream, the root client, or (with no root client) any valid stream
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-14 (issue #341 lineage): the missing classification this requirement's own former text named -- "a distinction this library cannot yet express (no wire-level concept of 'a valid stream_id/byte_bus_id combination' independent of a specific endpoint's own owning stream)" -- now exists. New rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_is_valid_association() (regmap.h/.c) is a direct membership query over TC18 §12.7.8 Table 23's own EP_ID_config table: true iff SOME row names the exact (request_stream_index, byte_bus_id) pair, regardless of which ep_id owns it -- the "regardless of which endpoint owns it" distinction is exactly what separates it from rcp_regmap_ep_client_t's own single-endpoint-scoped via_owning_stream. rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() now derives a new rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t member, via_valid_stream_association, from it -- bakes TC18's own "If a root client is configured only the root client's stream_id/byte_bus_id is accepted" narrowing directly into the member itself (map->svr_root_client_index == RCP_REGMAP_NO_ROOT_CLIENT AND a valid association), the same pattern via_root_client_ep0 already used for its own root-client-index check, so the member is always false by construction when a root client IS configured and can never wrongly widen access. rcp_lifecycle_transition() now ORs writer.via_valid_stream_association into its authorization check for both the HW_CONFIGURED -> RCP_CONFIGURED advance and the HW_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset -- the two transitions TC18 §12.3.1.2's identical wording governs -- but deliberately NOT into the RCP_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset, which §12.7.4's own narrower text (REQ-LIFECYCLE-037) restricts to via_root_client_ep0 alone; a dedicated test (test_lifecycle.c) pins that this new member does not widen that specific reset. Mutation-tested: the OR-clause, the membership scan, and the "no root client configured" guard were each independently removed/weakened and confirmed to fail the new tests, then restored.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2, TC18.txt L2562-L2565 and L2574-L2577 -- CORRECTED 2026-08-13, citation-drift fix (issue #341 lineage, found while investigating issue #338). Line numbers corrected to the real current location in the refreshed RC5 TC18.txt; the underlying technical claim is unchanged, re-verified directly against the fresh text before touching this citation.

requirements.title: In HW_CONFIGURED, non-configuration requests to endpoints other than EP0 are dropped
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP has no wire-level encode/decode pair for a functional-configuration read/write request at all, for any endpoint type -- regmap.h's own file header documents this as deliberately deferred ("wiring them to an actual byte_message_info read/write exchange is later phases' job"), confirmed by grepping the whole codebase for any regmap encode/decode pair and finding none outside discovery.c's own read-only discovery-response encoder. Every wire request this library can currently decode for a non-EP0 endpoint is therefore, by construction, operational -- so rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() now restricts HW_CONFIGURED to RCP_LIFECYCLE_DISCOVERY_BYTE_BUS_ID (EP0) only, the honestly-achievable form of TC18 §12.3.1.2's "requests to EPs other than EP0 that are not config requests will be ignored and dropped without response" given this library's real current wire-format scope. Migrating this restriction into rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() required moving test_mock.c's and test_conditional_dispatch.c's own dispatch fixtures from HW_CONFIGURED to RCP_CONFIGURED (both files' fixtures dispatch to non-EP0 endpoints as their normal, unremarkable test setup, not gap-specific behavior).

requirements.title: Non-STANDARD requests to EP0 before full configuration must be answered with REQUEST_REJECTED, not dropped
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: primary-source re-verification found the RCP_SCHED_KIND_* input this entry's own text said was needed is unnecessary machinery -- STANDARD-vs-conditional is already fully determined by the acf_msg_type parameter rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() already receives (ACF_ABB is this codebase's wire encoding for STANDARD requests; ACF_GBB is the encoding for every conditional request kind -- compound/compound-wait/triggered/chained/timed/cancel -- unconditionally, per request_compound.h and siblings' own mtv-repurposing scheme). Fixed: rcp_lifecycle_should_accept()'s bool return widened to a three-way rcp_lifecycle_accept_t (ACCEPT/DROP/REJECT); a non-ABB message type addressed to EP0 (RCP_LIFECYCLE_DISCOVERY_BYTE_BUS_ID) while HW_UNCONFIGURED, or while HW_CONFIGURED (this library's own architecture makes TC18's "no valid stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations have been defined" condition permanently true throughout HW_CONFIGURED, since no wire-level regmap read/write exists yet to ever establish one), now returns REJECT instead of the prior silent DROP. rcp_mock_server_dispatch() answers a REJECT with RCP_ERROR_REQUEST_REJECTED (wire code 11) via the same rcp_acf_build_error_response() convention find_slot()'s own EP_NOT_FOUND path already used, and returns the pre-existing RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_REJECTED result. This also resolves REQ-LIFECYCLE-029's own residual (see that entry) by treating §12.7's EP0-scoped REJECT as the more specific rule overriding §12.3.1.2's general ACF_GBB-drop rule for exactly this case.
requirements.tc18: §12.7 Configuration, TC18.txt L2827-2830

requirements.title: A direct-to-EP configuration request without a valid stream_id/byte_bus_id association must be dropped
requirements.text: PARTIAL: re-verified TC18.txt L2458-2459's exact wording directly against the primary-source PDF: "Configuration requests directly to EPs are only allowed In RCP_CONFIGURED or in HW_CONFIGURED with valid stream_id/byte_bus_id configuration. If the condition is not fulfilled, the request is dropped." Two distinct cases, read precisely: (a) in RCP_CONFIGURED, direct-to-EP configuration requests are allowed unconditionally by this sentence -- no per-request stream_id/byte_bus_id validity check is required here at all, so this requirement's own RCP_CONFIGURED half was mis-scoped in its original text; (b) in HW_CONFIGURED, a valid association is required. REQ-LIFECYCLE-032's already-merged fix (HW_CONFIGURED admits only byte_bus_id == EP0) satisfies (b) conservatively -- more strictly than §12.7 literally asks for (a properly-associated non-EP0 request would also now be dropped, not just an unassociated one), but this library has no wire-level regmap encode/decode for a functional-configuration request at all yet (regmap.h's own file header defers this), so no such properly-associated non-EP0 traffic can exist in this codebase's current scope regardless -- the over-restriction has no practical effect today and is the safe, conservative choice pending that missing capability. Genuinely open only for the theoretical future case once wire-level configuration requests exist; not an active gap given current scope.
requirements.tc18: §12.7 Configuration, TC18.txt L2833-L2834 -- CORRECTED 2026-08-13, citation-drift fix (issue #341 lineage, found while investigating issue #338). Line numbers corrected to the real current location in the refreshed RC5 TC18.txt; the underlying technical claim is unchanged, re-verified directly against the fresh text before touching this citation.

requirements.title: In HW_UNCONFIGURED only the claimed discovery stream may configure the server
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: the same underlying gap as REQ-LIFECYCLE-026 (this entry's own "claimed discovery stream" framing and that entry's "discovery claimant's stream" framing describe one code path, RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC's HW_UNCONFIGURED writability), closed by the same fix -- see REQ-LIFECYCLE-026's own text for the full correction (the enforcement point is rcp_lifecycle_field_writable(), not rcp_lifecycle_should_accept() as originally assumed here too). rcp_discovery_claim_note_request()/rcp_discovery_claim_is_claimant() (src/discovery.c) remain pure primitives a caller composes into writer.via_discovery_stream, per discovery.h's own documented architecture -- unchanged by this fix, and correctly so.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.2 Configuration in HW_UNCONFIGURED state, TC18.txt L2868-2870

requirements.title: HW_CONFIGURED configuration access is restricted to the discovery stream or a known stream_id/byte_bus_id pair
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.3 permits configuration access in HW_CONFIGURED only (a) via a discovery request on the discovery stream, or (b) via a KNOWN stream_id/byte_bus_id combination addressed directly to the endpoint. rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() now gates both RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W and RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR's HW_CONFIGURED branches on `authorized || writer.via_discovery_stream` -- via_owning_stream (already-modeled) is (b)'s "known stream_id/byte_bus_id pair addressed directly to the endpoint", and the new via_discovery_stream member is (a). rcp_lifecycle_should_accept()'s own byte_bus_id acceptance is unaffected -- this requirement's substance is about write authorization, which is field_writable()'s layer, matching REQ-LIFECYCLE-030's identical HW_CONFIGURED condition (both closed in the same change).
requirements.tc18: §12.7.3 Configuration in HW_CONFIGURED state, TC18.txt L2872-2874

requirements.title: Once RCP_CONFIGURED, a discovery request may no longer change configuration although it is still answered
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: primary-source re-verification found this entry had actually conflated two different things -- rcp_lifecycle_field_writable()'s FUNCTIONAL_W RCP_CONFIGURED branch already correctly excluded via_discovery_stream before this fix (authorized there is via_root_client_ep0 || via_owning_stream only), so field WRITES were never actually leaking discovery-stream authority into RCP_CONFIGURED. The real, confirmed gap was in rcp_lifecycle_transition()'s own RCP_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset path: it shared one `authorized` (via_discovery_stream || via_root_client_ep0) computation with the HW_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset, so a bare discovery-stream writer could still demote a fully RCP_CONFIGURED server -- itself a configuration change TC18 §12.7.4's "Changes in configuration via a discovery request are no longer allowed" forbids. Fixed: the RCP_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset now requires writer.via_root_client_ep0 specifically (the HW_CONFIGURED -> HW_UNCONFIGURED reset keeps the wider rule, since §12.7.3 still permits the discovery stream while HW_CONFIGURED). rcp_discovery_claim_note_config_write()/rcp_discovery_claim_release() (src/discovery.c) remain pure claim-bookkeeping primitives that deliberately do not consult lifecycle state, per discovery.h's own documented architecture -- the claim primitive still refreshes for the claimant regardless of state, but that no longer translates into actual write or transition authority once RCP_CONFIGURED, since both real gates (field_writable() and transition()) now independently close that door.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.4 Configuration in RCP_CONFIGURED state, TC18.txt L2876-2879

requirements.title: RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT's own third plausibility bullet -- every configured request stream has at least one endpoint using it
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-12, issue #201 Phase 5e): TC18 §12.3.1.2's RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT plausibility check names three bullets for the HW_CONFIGURED -> RCP_CONFIGURED transition: (1) "Each EP used has at least one stream_id/byte_bus_id association" -- REQ-LIFECYCLE-005/007; (2) "For each configured stream at least one stream_id/byte_bus_id is configured" -- the mirror-image completeness check, that no request stream is left configured with zero endpoints actually using it; (3) "Each response stream configured is assigned to at least one request stream" -- REQ-LIFECYCLE-006. Bullet 2 previously had no counterpart in rcp_lifecycle_check_rcp_cfg(): rcp_lifecycle_request_stream_plausibility_t carried only `configured` and `has_response_stream`, with no field representing whether any endpoint actually referenced that specific stream, so a request stream marked `configured = true` with zero endpoints bound to it -- an orphaned, unused stream slot -- passed the check exactly as if it were legitimately in use. Fixed by adding a new `request_stream_index` field to rcp_lifecycle_endpoint_plausibility_t (placed as the struct's own last field so existing positional-initializer call sites keep compiling, matching this codebase's established backward-compatibility convention) and a new bullet-2 scan in rcp_lifecycle_check_rcp_cfg() that, for each configured request stream, requires at least one endpoint with `ep_used && has_stream_assoc && request_stream_index == i`. Mutation-testing during this fix caught a genuine correctness gap in the first draft: the bullet-2 scan did not check `ep_used`, so a stale/unused endpoint slot (skipped by bullet 1's own loop, its `has_stream_assoc`/`request_stream_index` never validated by anything) could incorrectly "cover" an otherwise-orphaned stream if it happened to carry leftover `has_stream_assoc = true` and a matching index; the `ep_used` guard was added and a dedicated test (`test_rcp_cfg_inconsistent_an_unused_endpoint_does_not_cover_a_stream`) added to discriminate it. 5 tests (1 rewritten gap-pinning test, 4 new), 3/3 systematic mutations caught cleanly after the fix.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("Only if the configuration so far is plausible the state will be advanced. Plausibility check contains a check that: ... For each configured stream at least one stream_id/byte_bus_id is configured ... If not plausible the request will be rejected and an error response sent with RCP_CFG_INCONSITENT"), TC18.txt L2566-2572

requirements.title: PWM_OUT trigger events are derived from the skew-delayed signal and fire at 0% duty
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-13 (issue #338, tc18-gap backlog PR A): c-RCP enumerates the three TC18 Table 42/45 PWM_OUT trigger events (rcp_ep_pwm_out_trigger_t: DONE, CYCLE_START, MID_PULSE) and carries the pwmo_skew register. The two governing rules previously not implemented are now closed by a new primitive, rcp_ep_pwm_out_trigger_events_at_tick() (ep_pwm.h/.c), composed alongside the pre-existing pure selector rcp_ep_pwm_out_trigger_fires(): (1) TC18 §13.7.5.1's own break-before-make provision -- "for trigger signal generation the delayed signal is used" -- trigger timing is now derived relative to the pwmo_skew-delayed edge, not the undelayed source edge; (2) Table 45's own event-2 row -- "in the middle of the active pulse (even in case duty cycle is 0%)" -- MID_PULSE now fires unconditionally at active_duration/2 ticks past the delayed cycle start, including active_duration == 0, where it naturally coincides with CYCLE_START rather than being suppressed. Table 45's own event 0 ("PWM request exec done") is not a per-cycle timing event and stays the pre-existing one-shot, caller-driven signal via rcp_ep_pwm_out_trigger_fires()/RCP_EP_PWM_OUT_EVENT_DONE.

requirements.title: PWM_OUT duty-cycle limits cap the requested active time
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-12, issue #201 Phase 5e): rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() now takes duty_cycle_min/duty_cycle_max parameters (the endpoint's own pwmo_duty_cycle_min/pwmo_duty_cycle_max register values) and clamps the resulting active_duration into [duty_cycle_min, duty_cycle_max] after evt's own write semantics have already been applied, per TC18 Table 43's own wording ("requests with lower values will be capped to this limit" / "requests with higher values will be capped to this limit") -- capped, not rejected and not applied verbatim. period is unaffected, since Table 43 names only "PWM active" (the active-phase duration). Real signature change to a function with real callers: updated every call site (12 in tests/test_ep_pwm.c with no-op [0, 0xFFFF] limits that don't affect their own existing assertions, 5 in tests/test_tc18_gaps_ep.c). Split the pre-existing combined REQ-PWM-055/REQ-PWM-056 gap-pinning test into two -- REQ-PWM-055 (trigger-signal generation from the skew-delayed output, mid-pulse firing at 0% duty) remains a genuine, still-open deviation pin, since it needs a real timing/signal-generation model this protocol-codec library does not have. Mutation-tested 3 ways: bypassing capping entirely (caught), the min-boundary comparison reversed to the wrong direction (caught heavily), and the min-boundary's own < vs <= operator (a provably equivalent mutant -- assigning duty_cycle_min to a value already equal to duty_cycle_min is a no-op, so no test of the output can discriminate the two operators there).

requirements.title: PWM_OUT request semantics: stop on period 0, output-off on active 0, phase shift, readback check
requirements.text: PARTIAL (2 of TC18 13.7.5.3's own 4 PWM_OUT request rules): rcp_ep_pwm_out_generation_state() now classifies the endpoint's own signal-generation state purely from its {period, active_duration} pair -- period == 0 stops generation; active_duration == 0 with period != 0 keeps the endpoint running with the output disabled while trigger signals still fire; otherwise ordinary running generation. rcp_ep_pwm_out_apply_write() itself is unaffected -- both fields remain opaque 16-bit setpoints stored verbatim, this is a separate, additive classifier a caller applies to the result. The other 2 rules remain genuinely out of scope, not routine: a trigger-configuration request's first two payload octets carrying a PHASE SHIFT instead of a period depends on the conditional-request layer's own request-kind classification (request_compound.h/_triggered.h/_chained.h), which this endpoint's decode path has no connection to today, and the TC18 spec-defects report's own items 11-12 document a live, currently-unresolved request_type code collision in exactly that harmonization effort -- "which request even counts as a trigger configuration" is itself an open spec question; and checking that the output pin actually toggles needs real physical IO readback this protocol-codec library has never modelled for any endpoint type.

requirements.title: PWM_IN functional-config register block (Table 48)
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (FIXED 2026-08-11, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I; behavioral gap closed 2026-08-14, issue #428): c-RCP's rcp_ep_pwm_in_functional_cfg_t models every TC18 Table 48 PWM_IN register -- pwmi_polarity, pwmi_err_on_max_period, pwmi_continuous_mode (packed into a new flags octet at 0x0009, RCP_EP_PWM_IN_FLAG_* masks), pwmi_max_period (0x000A-0x000B), pwmi_base_clk (0x0004-0x0005, read-only), pwmi_clk_divider (0x0008), and pwmi_ep_status (0x0006-0x0007) -- reachable via the same generic evt[2:0]=111b TC18 §12.7.1 register-block mechanism every other endpoint type now has: rcp_ep_pwm_in_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig()/_reconfig_strerror()/_encode_reconfig_request(). This endpoint type had been silently omitted from every prior batch's own 'N of 11 endpoint types' accounting (REQ-CFG-011/REQ-CFG-012's own text counted the pwm.c module as fully done once PWM_OUT's own fix landed, without separately checking PWM_IN); see REQ-CFG-011's own corrected text. `trigger` remains a non-wire, module-own field; the measurement-timeout sentinel RCP_EP_PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL is unrelated to the register block. The new rcp_ep_pwm_in_max_period_outcome() (issue #428) is the pure classifier this bit's behavioral meaning needed: given a measured period, max_period, and the err_on_max_period bit, it returns Table 48's own outcome -- bit=0 invalidates the measurement and waits for a new active phase; bit=1 stops the measurement and, only if the caller-supplied EP_RESP_ON_ERR (EP_config) is enabled, signals an error -- closing the last purely-storage gap this entry used to pin. Also corrects this entry's own stale 'Table 45' citation (PWM_OUT's own 'pwmo trigger outputs' table) to the real 'Table 48' (pwmi functional configuration).

requirements.title: PWM_IN read-request decode validates evt[2:0]
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (FIXED 2026-08-11, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): rcp_ep_pwm_in_decode_read_request() shall reject a frame whose evt[2:0] is not one of the plain-request values rcp_acf_evt_row2_is_plain() accepts, returning RCP_EP_PWM_IN_ERR_BAD_EVT -- matching the check every other endpoint type in this Table 33 grouping (ADC/I2C/LIN/CAN/UART/ISELED/MDIO) already performs. Before this fix, this endpoint type never checked evt[2:0] at all: a real evt=111b configuration-write request from a conforming peer would have been silently misinterpreted as an ordinary read request rather than being rejected or routed to rcp_ep_pwm_in_apply_reconfig() -- a live conformance bug, distinct from (and worse than) every prior Group I register-block finding, which found only an unreachable path, never a misinterpreted one.

requirements.title: A cold start restores the configured lifecycle state, not always HW_UNCONFIGURED
requirements.text: power.h's rcp_pwrmode_cold_start_lifecycle_target() takes a required recovered_state parameter -- the caller's own already-recovered fact (this module owns no NVM access or default-configuration table of its own, the same convention as network_available) -- and returns it unchanged when it is one of lifecycle.h's three valid states, so a server that reached RCP_CONFIGURED before a power cycle no longer silently loses it; RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED remains the fail-safe default for a genuinely unconfigured device or a corrupt/unrecognized recovered_state.

requirements.title: Configuration data and wake sources survive StandBy
requirements.text: power.h owns no register-map or wake-source storage of its own (regmap.c/ep_wakeup.c do) -- the guarantee this library actually provides, and the only one it architecturally can, is that rcp_pwrmode_transition() correctly and always classifies Normal<->StandBy RCP_PWRMODE_START_HOT, now stated explicitly as a retention obligation on RCP_PWRMODE_START_HOT's own doc comment: a caller withholding re-init on HOT (per that documented contract) never has a reason to touch either structure, so both survive by construction, not merely by omission.

requirements.title: Hot start checks network availability before sending a WakeUp
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_iface_reenabled() now takes a network_available bool (this codebase's established "caller supplies already-classified inputs" convention -- this module reads no hardware itself, e.g. BEACON detection). A false network_available leaves hs at RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_NOT_STARTED (a cheap, uncounted "not yet" a caller polls again, not a failure) and does not advance the handshake, so rcp_pwrmode_handshake_wakeup_attempt() -- which requires RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_IFACE_REENABLED -- cannot be driven, and its own wakeup_repeat_limit budget is never touched, until the network is actually available. rcp_powerstate_manager_handshake_begin() (powerstate.c, the client-side convenience wrapper) threads the same network_available parameter through to its own caller.

requirements.title: The wake response is sent on the responder stream configured for the original sleep/standby request
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: rcp_powerstate_manager_handshake_begin() (powerstate.c) now takes a required resp_stream_id parameter (this codebase's established "caller supplies already-classified inputs" convention -- this module owns no register-map instance and no transport of its own, so it cannot itself resolve which response stream regmap.h's request_stream_cfg/response_queue_cfg pairing designates; the caller, which does have that access, resolves and supplies it). Recorded per-addr alongside the handshake itself; a new rcp_powerstate_manager_wake_response_stream_id() getter returns it so a caller transmits rcp_powerstate_manager_encode_wakeup_probe()'s own output (and the eventual wake notification) on the correct stream rather than assuming addr's own request stream, which TC18 does not guarantee are the same stream.

requirements.title: WakeUp repetition stops on any valid AVTPDU from the sleep-request client
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (documentation/citation correction, no logic change needed): re-verification found rcp_pwrmode_handshake_wakeup_attempt()'s own `echoed` bool was already sufficiently generic -- it is a plain caller-supplied bool, not itself hardwired to rcp_ep_wakeup_is_wakeup_echo(). powerstate.c's rcp_powerstate_manager_apply_wakeup_echo() is the ONE caller that narrows it to a literal WakeUp echo, but that function's own scope was always meant to be a specific convenience wrapper, not the sole way to satisfy step (b) -- a caller recognizing some other valid, already-demultiplexed frame from the sleep-request client may call rcp_pwrmode_handshake_wakeup_attempt() directly with echoed=true for that case instead, matching TC18 §12.4.1's actual "a valid AVTPDU from the sleep request Client" termination condition exactly. Both functions' own doc comments now state this explicitly. The repeat-limit framing this entry's own text already asked for was already correct and unchanged: wakeup_repeat_limit/RCP_PWRMODE_HANDSHAKE_FAILED are this implementation's own added safety bound, not spec-derived -- TC18 itself defines no limit.

requirements.title: Completing the wake handshake re-enables every used endpoint and response queue
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_pwrmode_handshake_resume_queues() (power.h) deliberately advances only a state enum -- power.h's own file header states it never touches server.h at all, matching this codebase's established "pure primitive, caller composes" layering (lifecycle.h/discovery.h use the identical pattern). The composition this requirement actually needs now lives at mock.h's new rcp_mock_server_pwrmode_resume(srv, hs): calls resume_queues(hs) first, then (iff it succeeds) calls rcp_server_endpoint_set_enable() on every registered endpoint, closing TC18 §12.4.1's "all used endpoints... will be enabled" for this test double. Still not modeled anywhere in this codebase: response-queue objects (rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t is inert, no STREAM_UID/queue_size/storage -- see test_response_queue_has_no_identity_size_or_storage()) and heartbeat-stream re-emission (see test_flush_triggers_and_heartbeat_are_absent()) -- both separate, already-tracked architecture gaps this fix cannot close, so "response queue"/heartbeat resumption remains genuinely unimplemented. STALE-TEXT CORRECTED, CLOSED 2026-08-14 (tc18-gap post-backlog audit): this entry's own text above referenced test_response_queue_has_no_identity_size_or_storage() and test_flush_triggers_and_heartbeat_are_absent() as its evidence for 'response queue... not modeled' -- neither test exists in this codebase anymore (grep-confirmed), both superseded by real work: response_queue_cfg[] storage (REQ-RMAP-034/059-061, mock.c) and heartbeat-stream re-emission (REQ-RMAP-065/SRV-017, rcp_mock_server_check_response_queue_heartbeat()) both now exist. rcp_mock_server_pwrmode_resume()'s own doc comment (mock.h) is corrected to match. The remaining question -- does TC18 §12.4.1's 'response queues will be [re-]enabled' clause need its own wiring beyond the endpoint-enable half rcp_mock_server_pwrmode_resume() already performs -- resolves to no: neither rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t nor rcp_mock_server_check_response_queue_heartbeat() carries any independent 'enabled/disabled' state of its own (unlike an endpoint's own ep_enable) for sleep to have disabled in the first place, so there is nothing left for wake to reverse -- the clause is vacuously satisfied by this codebase's own stateless response-queue design. (Whether heartbeat emission itself should be SUPPRESSED while asleep is a distinct question this entry's own §12.4.1 citation does not ask -- that citation is specifically about the wake handshake's own re-enable obligation, not about sleep-side gating -- and is left open as its own, separately-scoped concern if TC18 elsewhere requires it.)

requirements.title: A network wake runs the same hot-start handshake a pin wake does, not a bypass
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: rcp_pwrmode_hotstart_required() (REQ-PWRMODE-005) now returns true unconditionally, so rcp_pwrmode_wake_from_sleep() classifies RCP_PWRMODE_WAKE_VIA_NETWORK by the same handshake-completion rule RCP_PWRMODE_WAKE_VIA_PIN already used, matching TC18 §12.4.1's own "proceed as before" text -- a network-woken server now runs the WakeUp-repetition exchange (steps b/c) and is no longer classified hot before the sleeping client has actually been told it is awake. power.h's own state machine still requires a step-(a) rcp_pwrmode_handshake_iface_reenabled() call before step (b) can run for either path, unchanged -- the spec's own nuance (a network wake's network-availability check is trivially satisfied, since the wake arrived via the network in the first place) does not need separate modeling here: no literal hardware action is implied by that call for either path, only a state-machine precondition. A second call site, powerstate.c's rcp_powerstate_manager_wake_via_network() (the legacy client-side convenience wrapper's own "always hot for network" contract), now synthesizes and immediately completes a handshake locally to preserve that documented contract against power.h's corrected primitive -- see that function's own doc comment.

requirements.title: StandBy is entered only in response to an RCP request, never from a network signal
requirements.text: power.h's rcp_pwrmode_commit_network_sleep() is the sole entry point a caller integrating a real TC14/TC10 network signal uses, and it has no target-mode parameter at all -- unlike rcp_pwrmode_commit_entry(), which the SleepCMD (RCP-request) path uses. The only power mode a network trigger can ever produce is RCP_PWRMODE_SLEEP, making the StandBy exclusivity impossible to violate by construction rather than merely true by omission (there being no network path modelled at all, the prior state).

requirements.title: Sleep can also be initiated by a valid network TC14/TC10 sleep request
requirements.text: power.h's rcp_pwrmode_commit_network_sleep(mode, gate, response_sent, out_start_kind) delegates to the same rcp_pwrmode_commit_entry() a normal (RCP-request) sleep entry uses, target fixed to RCP_PWRMODE_SLEEP -- 'the same conditions apply as for a normal sleep request' (TC18's own text). TC14/TC10 sleep signaling is PHY/MAC-level out-of-band control, not an RCP/ACF wire message this library's decode layer could ever parse; matching rcp_pwrmode_handshake_iface_reenabled()'s own network_available convention, a caller supplies 'a valid TC14/TC10 sleep request was received' as an already-classified fact simply by calling this function, with no frame/byte-buffer parameter to give since none exists for this library to inspect.

requirements.title: A sleep/standby request from an authorized client applies to the entire RC Server
requirements.text: c-RCP gates SleepCMD admission on client authorization via ep_wakeup.h's rcp_ep_wakeup_sleepcmd_writable() (true iff writer.via_root_client_ep0, mirroring rcp_lifecycle_transition()'s own RCP_CONFIGURED-state root-client rule) before power.h's rcp_pwrmode_check_entry()/rcp_pwrmode_commit_entry() is ever consulted. Those two functions operate on a single rcp_pwrmode_t, this module's existing whole-server mode representation, not a per-endpoint one -- a real server-side composition points *mode at its own one server-wide variable, satisfying TC18's 'entire RC Server implementation' wording by construction. rcp_powerstate_manager_t's own per-addr mode tracking (unchanged) is this library's CLIENT-side bookkeeping of multiple distinct remote peers, not a per-endpoint model of one server's own state.

requirements.title: A wake-source event during sleep-request processing aborts the sleep entry
requirements.text: power.h's rcp_pwrmode_commit_entry() re-validates a freshly re-sampled rcp_pwrmode_entry_gate_t (via rcp_pwrmode_check_entry() internally) immediately before the mode actually changes -- a caller that admitted the request against a gate sampled at arrival time and re-samples it again just before committing sees any wake-source event that occurred in between, refuses the entry (RCP_PWRMODE_ERR_ENTRY_REFUSED), and leaves the mode unchanged, closing the lost-wakeup race a single up-front rcp_pwrmode_check_entry() call would leave open.

requirements.title: The sleep/standby refusal conditions are evaluated server-wide, across every EP and every responder queue
requirements.text: power.h's rcp_pwrmode_entry_gate_t.endpoint_idle/.response_queue_empty are documented as server-wide aggregates -- true iff EVERY endpoint/responder queue on the RC Server is idle/empty, not just the endpoint the request arrived on -- matching TC18 §12.5's 'AT LEAST ONE EP is not idle' / 'AT LEAST ONE responder queue' refusal conditions. Both fields were always caller-supplied opaque bools with no code-level scope restriction; the pre-fix reading of their doc comments (worded around a single wake-up endpoint) was the actual gap, not rcp_pwrmode_check_entry()'s own logic, which already ANDs whatever the caller supplies.

requirements.title: The mode change happens only after the sleep/standby response has been transmitted
requirements.text: power.h's rcp_pwrmode_commit_entry() takes a required response_sent bool and refuses the entry (RCP_PWRMODE_ERR_ENTRY_REFUSED, mode left unchanged) unless it is true, mirroring rcp_pwrmode_handshake_iface_reenabled()'s own network_available convention -- this library does no I/O of its own and cannot observe transmission completion directly, so response_sent is the caller's own proof that the sleep/standby response has actually been transmitted before the mode transition it gates is permitted to run.

requirements.title: A refused network sleep request suppresses the TC14/TC10 LPS confirmation
requirements.text: power.h's rcp_pwrmode_commit_network_sleep() has no PHY-signalling surface of its own (this library never touches hardware, the same scoping precedent as network_available), so its RCP_PWRMODE_OK vs. RCP_PWRMODE_ERR_ENTRY_REFUSED return value IS the confirmation signal: a caller integrating a real TC14/TC10 PHY asserts LPS only on RCP_PWRMODE_OK, never on RCP_PWRMODE_ERR_ENTRY_REFUSED, honouring 'the network PHY shall not signal a TC14/TC10 LPS as confirmation' when the go-to-sleep conditions are not fulfilled.

requirements.title: Sleep-request processing order: stop admitting requests, drain, then acknowledge
requirements.text: server.h's rcp_server_endpoint_t gains an admission_suspended flag (default false, additive) and rcp_server_endpoint_set_admission_suspended() setter; rcp_server_endpoint_admit() checks it first, before inspecting the arriving frame at all, and returns the new RCP_SERVER_ADMIT_SUSPENDED outcome -- neither queued nor executed -- implementing TC18 13.7.2.3 step 1 ("stop entering incoming requests into endpoint queues") ahead of step 3's preconditions (rcp_pwrmode_check_entry()/rcp_pwrmode_commit_entry(), REQ-PWRMODE-024/026), which a caller already evaluates during the same drain.

requirements.title: The lifecycle state is exposed as the svr_lifecycle_state register-map entry
requirements.text: PARTIAL: the lifecycle state must be exposed as a register-map entry (TC18 §12.3.1.1, §12.3.1.2, §12.4.1). rcp_regmap_general_t now carries a svr_lifecycle_state field (content modeling only), kept in sync with the authoritative rcp_lifecycle_state_t by rcp_mock_server_transition() -- the one caller today composing rcp_lifecycle_transition() with a regmap.h general block -- on every transition attempt, success or failure. What remains open: REQ-RMAP-024 (the general Table 20 register map's own wire-reachability gap) is now CLOSED, but that closure deliberately does not reach this field -- svr_lifecycle_state has no genuine TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 address at all (confirmed directly against the primary source), so rcp_regmap_general_render() never serializes it. Its real home is TC18 §13.7.1.2 Table 33 (the RC Server's own EP_FUNC_config block, a separate register space), still unimplemented (REQ-RMAP-067). A remote client therefore still cannot read this server's readiness or drive a transition by writing it over the wire -- only in-process consumers of the field can.

requirements.title: The RC Server general register map's full Table 20 extent is now reachable on the wire, not just the first 14 octets
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: c-RCP now exposes the RC Server general register map's full TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 extent (RCP_REGMAP_GENERAL_LEN, 0x0000..0x003F) over ACF_ABB via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response()/_decode_read_response() (include/rcp/regmap.h, src/regmap.c) -- the same read mechanism rcp_discovery_encode_response() already used for its own narrower, still-unchanged 14-octet identity slice (RCP_DISCOVERY_GENERAL_SLICE_LEN), generalized to serve every field at its own TC18-documented address; a read_size shorter than the full extent still works, carrying only a prefix (matching every other register-block decoder's own partial-population convention). Two struct fields, svr_lifecycle_state and svr_root_client_index, have no genuine Table 20 address (confirmed directly against the primary source: Table 20's own address sequence has no room for either) and are deliberately excluded from this render/decode pair, not force-mapped onto an invented address -- their real home is TC18 §13.7.1.2 Table 33 (the RC Server's own EP_FUNC_config block, a separate register space reached via §12.7.1's own pointer-addressed mechanism), still unimplemented (REQ-RMAP-023, REQ-RMAP-067). Write access is also now dispatched: rcp_regmap_general_decode_write_request() recognizes any ACF_ABB WRITE addressed to EP0 and reports RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS every time, via lifecycle.h's already-proven RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_READ_ONLY primitive (REQ-RMAP-025). EP0 is now a genuinely addressable, read/write-dispatched register space for its Table 20 extent, closing this requirement's own scope.
requirements.tc18: §12.7 Configuration, TC18.txt L2452-2453

requirements.title: Every register in the RC Server static part is read-only to a remote client
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 marks every register of the RC Server general (static) part with access type R — a remote write to any of them must not take effect. rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() (src/lifecycle.c) models this as its own explicit kind, RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_READ_ONLY: unconditionally unwritable in every lifecycle state, by every writer (proven for a maximally-privileged writer too, not just an unprivileged one), and rcp_lifecycle_field_write_error() correctly reports RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS for it (never RCP_ERROR_UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS, since no writer condition is ever consulted). A real wire write path now exists and consults it: rcp_regmap_general_decode_write_request() (regmap.h/regmap.c) recognizes any ACF_ABB WRITE addressed to EP0 targeting the general register map and reports RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS every time, reusing (not duplicating) this same primitive -- closing the live-enforcement gap this requirement previously left open. rcp_mock_server_regmap() itself still hands back a directly mutable in-process pointer, a deliberate, separate design choice for that test double's own convenience API, not a remaining conformance gap: no code path routes a real wire write through it.

requirements.title: svr_req_stream_max (0x000E) is the wrong width and svr_responder_streams_max (0x000F) is missing
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 defines svr_req_stream_max as an 8-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x000E (maximum number of request streams usable to access this RC Server) and svr_responder_streams_max as an 8-bit read-only register at 0x000F (maximum number of supported responder queues for response and acknowledge traffic). rcp_regmap_general_t declares both at the correct width: svr_req_stream_max (uint8_t, renamed from this field's own former name svr_max_request_streams to match TC18's own register name) and the previously-missing svr_responder_streams_max (uint8_t). A value neither register's own 8-bit width could hold on the wire can no longer be constructed in the first place, and both are now wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response() at their own TC18-cited addresses.

requirements.title: The two memory-capacity registers svr_responder_mem_size (0x0010) and svr_req_mem_size (0x0012) are missing
