requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 defines two distinct 16-bit read-only capacity registers, both counted in 32-bit words: svr_responder_mem_size at absolute address 0x0010 (maximum responder-queue memory) and svr_req_mem_size at 0x0012 (maximum memory for EP request queues). rcp_regmap_general_t models both distinctly, replacing the former undifferentiated 32-bit svr_memory_capacity field that conflated them into one unaddressed field with no unit, and both are now wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response() at their own TC18-cited addresses.

requirements.title: svr_sequencers_max (0x0014) is 16-bit and its 0-means-unsupported encoding is unenforced
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 defines svr_sequencers_max as an 8-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x0014 whose value 0 means sequencer operation is not supported and whose values 1..n give the number of available sequencer state registers. rcp_regmap_general_t declares svr_sequencers_max at the correct 8-bit width (renamed from this field's own former name svr_max_sequencers), and mock.c's rcp_mock_server_set_sequencer_count() keeps it synced with the actual rcp_sequencer_table_t.count it allocates -- request_sequencer.h's own rcp_sequencer_table_unsupported() (table->count == 0) already implements the "0 means unsupported" rule this register describes, so once synced, the register correctly reflects that same rule by construction, and the address (0x0014) is now wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response().

requirements.title: svr_configuration_lock (0x0015) is entirely missing, so R/W+ writes are never lock-gated
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 defines svr_configuration_lock as an 8-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x0015 whose value 0x00 permits write access to "R/W+" type parameters and whose every other value causes such write access to be rejected. rcp_regmap_general_t declares this field (content modeling), zero-initializing to 0x00 (the correct unlocked default), and it is now wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response(). This requirement's own scope is the register's existence, default, and wire-reachability, all now satisfied. What remains open, tracked separately: rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() (src/lifecycle.c) still grants or denies RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR writes purely from lifecycle state and writer context, with no lock input, so a device that has latched its configuration still cannot have that latch actually enforced -- deliberately deferred to REQ-RMAP-055 (issue #200 Group 3), this codebase's own already-identified "shared plumbing, implement once" home for the W+ lockable-access-type primitive Table 23's EP_ID_config rows and Table 24's queue registers also need identically, rather than building a redundant, table-specific check here ahead of that shared work.

requirements.title: svr_implemented_options (0x0016) is now 8-bit, five independent bits, matching Table 20 exactly (formerly an invented 32-bit, six-bit, three-pair design)
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 defines svr_implemented_options as an 8-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x0016 with one independent bit per optional feature: a = compound & wait requests, b = trigger requests, c = chained requests, d = time synch and timed requests, e = enhanced request cancellation (bits f/g/h reserved). rcp_regmap_general_t declares this field at its correct 8-bit width, with RCP_REGMAP_OPT_COMPOUND_WAIT/_TRIGGER/_CHAINED/_TIME_SYNC/_ENH_CANCEL (include/rcp/regmap.h) at bit values 0x01/0x02/0x04/0x08/0x10 -- five independent bits, verified directly against the primary-source PDF (OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC.pdf, Table 20, page 51). This replaces a prior 32-bit field carrying six bits of this project's own invention, grouped into three all-or-nothing pairs and enforced by rcp_regmap_options_group_consistent() (both removed outright; see REQ-RMAP-004..008's own retirement text for the primary-source finding that invalidated their shared citation). This also closed a real, previously-unadvertised capability gap: c-RCP has always implemented both trigger requests (src/request_triggered.c) and chained requests (src/request_chained.c) in full, but the prior design had no bit for either -- a conforming client had no way to learn c-RCP supports them. All three real consumers use the new bits: rcp_timed_feature_enabled() (src/request_timed.c, checks RCP_REGMAP_OPT_TIME_SYNC), the CLI's capabilities_json() "features" array (src/cli.c, RCP_CLI_IMPLEMENTED_OPTIONS macro), and the config manifest parser's "svr_implemented_options" array (src/config.c, OPTION_BIT_NAMES table, now including "trigger"/"chained" names). This address (0x0016) is now wire-reachable too (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response().
requirements.tc18: §12.7.5 Table 20, TC18.txt L2554-2560 -- primary-source-verified against OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC.pdf Table 20, page 51, and §12.9.1.1, page 64 (this milestone)

requirements.title: The reserved octet at 0x0017 is now explicitly modeled and reads 0x00
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 reserves the 8-bit register at absolute address 0x0017 and requires it to read 0x00. rcp_regmap_general_t declares an explicit reserved_0x17 field for this octet, zero-initializing for free via the existing memset in rcp_regmap_general_init(); no setter exists anywhere in this codebase to construct a nonzero value. This documents the octet as deliberately reserved (not merely forgotten), and this address (0x0017) is now genuinely wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed): rcp_regmap_general_render() writes 0x00 there for real, dispatched via rcp_regmap_general_encode_read_response(), not merely produced by a generic zero-filled buffer beyond a truncated slice.

requirements.title: svr_io_pin_count (0x0018) is now explicitly modeled, so the HW_config table has a declared extent
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 defines svr_io_pin_count as a 16-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x0018 giving the number of assignable I/O pins, and §12.7.6 makes it the authoritative source for how many IO-pin entries the HW_config table (Table 21) contains. rcp_regmap_general_t declares this field, and it is wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response(). CLOSED 2026-08-13 (issue #338, tc18-gap backlog PR A): the register's own text previously flagged "nothing in this codebase yet allocates or bounds a real HW_config table against this count", citing issue #200 items REQ-RMAP-040 through REQ-RMAP-045 -- that citation was stale (all six are themselves now implemented, closed in an earlier batch). The real remaining gap was narrower and already correctly identified by REQ-RMAP-034's own text: svr_io_pin_count was never cross-checked against the actual hw_pin_map table's own length. rcp_mock_server_set_hw_pin_map() (mock.c) now syncs srv->regmap.svr_io_pin_count to len on every call, including shrinking back down on a smaller replacement, not just a one-time high-water mark.

requirements.title: svr_hw_cfg_ptr (0x001A) is now correctly shaped, a bare 16-bit pointer with no spurious capacity
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 defines svr_hw_cfg_ptr as a 16-bit read-only pointer register at absolute address 0x001A, giving the address of the HW_config register map of §12.7.6. rcp_regmap_general_t declares this field as svr_hw_cfg_ptr, a bare uint16_t matching TC18's own width exactly -- replacing the former rcp_regmap_table_ref_t representation, whose offset member was a 32-bit value expressed in this implementation's own "register words" rather than a 16-bit register-map address, and which carried an extra capacity member that TC18 does not define for this table (HW_config's extent is svr_io_pin_count at 0x0018, REQ-RMAP-032). This address (0x001A) is now wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response(). RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (found stale while scoping the next RMAP batch after issue #308): this entry's own prior text claimed "no real HW_config table storage anywhere yet for this pointer to meaningfully address... currently always reads 0", citing issue #200's original REQ-RMAP-040 through -045 scope as still-open. That scope closed across issues #301/#306/#308 -- rcp_mock_server_t's own rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_entry_t table is real storage, and rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request()/_encode_read_response() route both directions through svr_hw_cfg_ptr's own extent by this exact field, with authorization (issue #308). Text was simply never revisited after the pointed-to table it names was built. No code change; documentation-only correction.

requirements.title: The request/response stream config pointer and capacity registers are now correctly sized and separately addressed
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 defines four separate registers for the stream-configuration sub-tables — svr_request_stream_cfg_capacity (8 bit, 0x001C), svr_response_stream_cfg_capacity (8 bit, 0x001D), svr_request_stream_cfg_ptr (16 bit, 0x001E) and svr_response_stream_cfg_ptr (16 bit, 0x0020). rcp_regmap_general_t declares these as four correctly-sized scalar fields. This address range (0x001C-0x0021) is wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response(). svr_request_stream_cfg_ptr/svr_response_stream_cfg_ptr are the exact fields request-stream-cfg's and response-queue-config's own dispatcher routing blocks address (issue #306/#308), confirmed directly in src/regmap.c's dispatcher routing conditions. CLOSED 2026-08-13 (issue #338, tc18-gap backlog PR A): the previously-open capacity cross-check is now real. rcp_mock_server_set_request_stream_cfg() syncs srv->regmap.svr_request_stream_cfg_capacity to count on every call; the new rcp_mock_server_set_response_queue_cfg() (mock.c, mirroring set_request_stream_cfg()'s own shape -- response_queue_cfg[] previously had no backing storage in rcp_mock_server_t at all) syncs srv->regmap.svr_response_stream_cfg_capacity to count. Both shrink back down on a smaller replacement, not just a one-time high-water mark.

requirements.title: The reserved 16-bit register at 0x0022 is now explicitly modeled and preserved as reserved
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 reserves the 16-bit read-only register at absolute address 0x0022. rcp_regmap_general_t declares an explicit reserved_0x22 field for this span, zero-initializing for free via the existing memset in rcp_regmap_general_init(); no setter exists anywhere in this codebase to construct a nonzero value. This documents the span as deliberately reserved (not merely forgotten), matching the reserved_0x17 precedent (REQ-RMAP-031), and this address (0x0022) is now genuinely wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024, closed): rcp_regmap_general_render() writes 0x00 there for real, dispatched via rcp_regmap_general_encode_read_response(), not merely produced by a generic zero-filled buffer beyond a truncated slice.

requirements.title: svr_ep_generic_cfg_ptr/_capacity are now correctly sized, addressed, and unit-correct
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 defines svr_ep_generic_cfg_ptr as a 16-bit read-only pointer at absolute address 0x0024 to the generic endpoint register map (§13.2), and svr_ep_generic_cfg_capacity as a 16-bit read-only register at 0x0026 giving the LENGTH OF THE EP CONFIG REGISTER SECTION IN BYTES (re-verified directly against the primary-source PDF, Table 20 page 52). rcp_regmap_general_t declares both as correctly-sized, correctly-UNITED scalar fields. This address range (0x0024-0x0027) is wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response(). CAPACITY HALF CLOSED 2026-08-13 (issue #338, tc18-gap backlog PR A): svr_ep_generic_cfg_capacity was never cross-checked against the real endpoint table's own size. rcp_mock_server_add_endpoint()/_remove_endpoint() (mock.c) now sync srv->regmap.svr_ep_generic_cfg_capacity to endpoint_count * 12 (the same per-entry byte stride src/regmap.c's own EP0 dispatcher already uses for ep_generic_cfg_len) on every registration/removal. STILL PARTIAL: this codebase has no real EP_config table storage anywhere yet for svr_ep_generic_cfg_ptr itself to meaningfully address (a materially bigger, separate feature -- building the whole per-endpoint generic-config register section -- not this narrower capacity-cross-check gap); the pointer field is wire-readable but currently always reads 0. CLOSED 2026-08-14 (tc18-gap backlog PR I, issue #334): this entry's own prior text was STALE -- it claimed "no real EP_config table storage anywhere yet... a materially bigger, separate feature", but rcp_mock_endpoint_slot_t (src/mock.c) already carries its own rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_t as of every rcp_mock_server_add_endpoint() call; the storage has existed per-endpoint-slot all along, just sparse (indexed by registration slot) rather than the contiguous array rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request()/_encode_read_response()'s own ep_generic_cfg/ep_generic_cfg_count parameters expect. New rcp_mock_server_ep_generic_cfg_view() (mock.h/mock.c) gathers a snapshot into a caller-supplied scratch array (the same "ask first, then size a buffer" idiom rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_byte_bus_ids_for_stream() already establishes); new rcp_mock_server_apply_ep_generic_cfg() scatters a possibly-mutated array back into the same live slots, rejecting a mismatched count outright rather than risk misattributing rows. Neither function invents a second, parallel wire codec -- the existing, already-tested rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_apply_reconfig()/_render() do the actual mutation, mutating the gathered array in place exactly as they already do for every other pointed-to table. Proven via a genuine gather -> real-dispatcher-write -> scatter -> re-gather round trip through rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() (ep_tx_buffer_size, relative 0x0008, R/W*), plus two dedicated tests using a genuine hole in the slot array (register 3, remove the middle one without re-adding) to prove the in_use skip in both the gather and scatter loops is real, not merely coincidentally correct for a hole-free setup -- both skips were mutation-tested and caught cleanly, along with the mismatched-count rejection. Same bar as REQ-RMAP-040's own established closure: a proven wire codec via the dispatcher, not that mock.c's own live per-request dispatch loop calls it.

requirements.title: svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_ptr/_capacity are now correctly sized and separately addressed
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20 defines svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_ptr as a 16-bit read-only pointer at absolute address 0x0028 to the EP-to-byte_bus_id mapping table, and svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_capacity as an 8-bit read-only register at 0x002A giving that table's maximum entry count (re-verified directly against the primary-source PDF, Table 20 page 52). rcp_regmap_general_t declares both as correctly-sized scalar fields. This address range (0x0028-0x002A) is wire-reachable (REQ-RMAP-024) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response(). svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_ptr is the exact field EP_ID_config's own dispatcher routing block addresses (issue #301 batch 2/#308), confirmed directly in src/regmap.c's dispatcher routing conditions. CLOSED 2026-08-13 (issue #338, tc18-gap backlog PR A): the previously-open capacity cross-check is now real. rcp_mock_server_set_ep_id_map() (mock.c) now syncs srv->regmap.svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_capacity to count on every call, shrinking back down on a smaller replacement, not just a one-time high-water mark.

requirements.title: svr_ep_functional_cfg_ptr/svr_sequencer_state_ptr are now correctly sized and separately addressed
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-14, re-verification against the current tree found this requirement's own text stale): svr_ep_functional_cfg_ptr and svr_sequencer_state_ptr are both correctly sized and separately addressed (this requirement's own title claim, unchanged and re-confirmed) -- rcp_regmap_general_t declares both as bare 16-bit pointer scalars with no spurious capacity member. The prior text's own remaining-gap note ("no real EP_FUNC_config or Sequencer_config table storage anywhere yet for either pointer to meaningfully address") no longer describes the current codebase for the Sequencer_config half: REQ-SEQ-013/REQ-SEQ-014 (issue #334/#335, 2026-08-13, landed AFTER this requirement's text was last written) built real storage (rcp_sequencer_table_t.state[]/owner[]), a real wire codec (rcp_regmap_sequencer_table_render()/_apply_reconfig(), TC18 12.7.10 Table 28's 2-octet-per-sequencer Seq_state/Request_stream_index stride), and full EP0 dispatcher routing (rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request()/_encode_read_response(), with REQ-SEQ-013's own ownership-aware per-octet write authorization) -- re-verified directly against src/regmap.c and its own dedicated dispatcher-level tests (tests/test_tc18_gaps_regmap.c: test_sequencer_table_render_interleaves_state_and_owner, test_sequencer_table_apply_reconfig_patches_addressed_octets_only, and 5 more covering ownership-aware write authorization) before trusting this closure, not merely inferred from the sibling requirements' own status. svr_sequencer_state_ptr's own value stays caller-set (0 unless a caller assigns it), the same established convention every other Table 20 pointer field in this codebase already uses (REQ-RMAP-033/034/037's own already-implemented status accepts the identical convention) -- not a gap specific to this field. The EP_FUNC_config half (svr_ep_functional_cfg_ptr's own target, TC18 13.7.1.2 Table 33/36's RC-Server-specific block) remains genuinely unaddressable, but that is REQ-RMAP-067's own separately-tracked, already-documented spec self-contradiction (a real, confirmed address collision in Table 36 itself, plus 13.7.1.1's own prose directly contradicting Table 36 listing EP_FUNC-common-header fields for the RC Server at all) -- not a new finding, and not this requirement's own responsibility to re-solve; REQ-RMAP-067 stays partial for that reason on its own terms. No code changed for this closure -- .fusa-reqs.json text and status corrected only, matching REQ-PWRMODE-019's own prior precedent for a text-only stale-status correction.
