requirements.title: All four optional-subsystem pointer/capacity register pairs (network, physical layer, time synch, security) are now declared
requirements.text:
PARTIAL: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20's continued part defines four further 16-bit read-only pointer/capacity register pairs in the RC Server general register map — svr_network_interface_cfg_ptr/_capacity (§12.7.11), svr_physical_layer_cfg_ptr/_capacity (§12.7.12), svr_time_synch_cfg_ptr/_capacity (§12.7.13) and svr_security_cfg_ptr/_capacity (§12.7.14) — where a pointer value of 0 is the defined encoding for "this subsystem is not supported" for the physical-layer, time-synch and security pointers (TC18's own table gives no such note for the network-interface pointer). rcp_regmap_general_t declares all eight registers (issue #200) -- CORRECTED 2026-08-14 (issue #429): this text used to call these eight fields Group 1's LAST item; see this entry's own trailing paragraph below for the real ninth pair Table 20 also defines; each pair is its own independent 16-bit ptr/capacity scalar pair, not the shared rcp_regmap_table_ref_t type (already unused elsewhere in this struct as of REQ-RMAP-038). Re-verified directly against the primary-source PDF a second time for this batch specifically (Table 20, page 53 of OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC.pdf): the table's own "Absolute address" column is genuinely BLANK for all eight registers on this continuation page — a real gap in the primary source itself, not an extraction failure — so this codebase's own relative addresses (0x0030 through 0x003F) are INFERRED (from the visible 0x0030 continuation marker after svr_sequencer_state_ptr's own 0x002E-0x002F, plus this table's consistent, gap-free sequential-address convention observed without exception everywhere else), not directly read; flagged honestly in the field comments rather than presented as spec-confirmed. This address range (0x0030-0x003F) is now wire-reachable at those inferred addresses (REQ-RMAP-024, closed) via rcp_regmap_general_render()/_encode_read_response(). What remains open: this codebase has no real Network_config/physical-layer/PTP_config/security-configuration table storage anywhere yet for any of the four pointers to meaningfully address -- all four are wire-readable but currently always read 0. CLOSED 2026-08-13 (tc18-gap backlog PR F, issue #336): direct primary-source read of TC18 §12.7.11-.14's own section text (not just Table 20's own pointer/capacity row) found the real remaining scope was narrower than this entry's own prior framing assumed -- each section's own text states verbatim "The content is product specific" (§12.7.11 Ethernet MAC config, §12.7.12 "might be empty" for MDIO-managed PHYs, §12.7.13 gPTP, §12.7.14 MACsec), so TC18 defines no field-level layout for any of the four -- unlike HW_config/EP_ID_config/response-queue-config/request-stream-cfg (all already-implemented row-typed tables), there is no row schema to build. The conformant implementation is therefore one generic mechanism, not four bespoke ones: rcp_regmap_optional_subsystem_cfg_t (regmap.h) is a flat, capacity-bounded opaque byte buffer; rcp_regmap_optional_subsystem_cfg_apply_reconfig() is its direct-memcpy write primitive (no render-patch-reparse idiom needed, since the buffer already IS the wire image); rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request()/_encode_read_response() now route all four sections' own [ptr, ptr+len) extents through it via a new optional_cfg parameter (rcp_regmap_optional_subsystem_cfg_ptrs_t), NULL-able as a whole or per-section, matching this dispatcher's own established sequencer_state/sequencer_owner NULL-means-absent convention. FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR is this codebase's own documented default access-type choice for all four (TC18 gives no table-specific override the way HW_config's own §12.7.6 has one) -- flagged explicitly as a codebase-level default, not a primary-source-derived fact. rcp_mock_server_set_network_interface_cfg()/_physical_layer_cfg()/_time_synch_cfg()/_security_cfg() (mock.h/mock.c) install each section's own content and keep its svr_*_cfg_capacity register synced, the same capacity-sync convention REQ-RMAP-032/034/036/037 already established. Proven via a direct dispatcher-level test (write, read-back including zero-fill past len, a genuinely-denied write under FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR's own "permanently locked once RCP_CONFIGURED" rule, and the per-section/whole-NULL fallback), a direct apply_reconfig() unit test (bounds check, mutation-tested), and a mock-server storage/capacity-sync test -- matching REQ-RMAP-040's own established bar for closure (a proven wire codec via the dispatcher, not that mock.c's own live per-request dispatch loop calls it -- that whole register-map wire-level exchange stays deliberately unwired into mock.c's own production dispatch path, per regmap.h's own file-header note, REQ-LIFECYCLE-034's own separate open item).

NINTH PAIR FOUND AND ADDED 2026-08-14 (issue #429): Table 20's own continuation page (PDF p.61) defines TWO MORE 16-bit R registers immediately after svr_security_cfg_capacity -- svr_device_specific_cfg_ptr and svr_device_specific_cfg_capacity -- that rcp_regmap_general_t (and this entry's own prior "closing Group 1's last item" text) entirely missed. The spec's own printed description text for this specific pair is genuinely swapped between the two rows (the _ptr row's own description reads "Data size of the device specific configurations", a capacity concept; the _capacity row's reads "Pointer to device specific configurations as defined by its vendor", a pointer concept) -- flagged by the spec's own reviewer comment ("051RC5 - proposal to solve TI_032") as an open drafting issue in the primary source itself, not an extraction error here; both fields are unambiguously part of Table 20's real extent regardless of which way the description text runs, so this codebase orders them _ptr-then-_capacity to match every other Group 1 pair's own established convention. RCP_REGMAP_GENERAL_LEN is extended from 0x0040 to 0x0044 (address range now 0x0000-0x0043 inclusive) and rcp_regmap_general_render()/_decode_read_response() now cover both new registers at their own INFERRED addresses 0x0040/0x0042 (INFERRED for the identical reason -- and via the identical sequential-address convention -- this entry's own eight-field text above already documents for the preceding four pairs). Read-only (R), matching every sibling pair. New tests prove both fields reachable via a full-table read (extending the existing byte-offset and round-trip tests) and via the dispatcher-level full-table-reach test.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.5 Table 20 (continued), TC18.txt L2635-2659 -- primary-source-verified against OA_TC18_specification_v_0.5.1_RC_5_3624.pdf Table 20, p.61 (svr_device_specific_cfg_ptr/_capacity immediately follow svr_security_cfg_capacity; address column confirmed blank in the primary source itself for this whole continuation page; relative addresses INFERRED, not directly read)

requirements.title: No HW_config table exists to hold per-IO-pin endpoint-signal assignments
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.6 requires a table holding, for each used physical IO-pin, its mapping to an endpoint signal and its IO-pin properties, defaulting at the factory to no assignment at all. Real server-side storage exists (rcp_mock_server_t's own bounded rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_entry_t table, mock.h/mock.c). RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301): the addressing question this entry's own prior text called genuinely unresolved is now answered -- direct verification of the current RC5 baseline PDF (page 61) shows Table 20's own address column is headed "Absolute address", confirming svr_hw_cfg_ptr's own value is an absolute address in the same EP0-scoped space Table 20 itself lives in; a client reaches HW_config via an ordinary evt[2:0]=111b request to byte_bus_id=0 with start_address = svr_hw_cfg_ptr's current value plus an offset. rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() (regmap.h/regmap.c) now implements exactly this: it routes an incoming write by absolute address across Table 20's own extent (always denied, reusing REQ-RMAP-025's own logic) and HW_config's own extent (applied via the new rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_apply_reconfig(), the parse-side inverse of rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_render()). READ SIDE ALSO RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301 batch 4): rcp_regmap_ep0_encode_read_response() (regmap.h/regmap.c) is the read-side counterpart to the write dispatcher, routing an incoming read's own address across the identical extents and reusing rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_render() directly -- a client can now write AND read HW_config over the wire. AUTHORIZATION CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #308): rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() now consults rcp_lifecycle_field_writable(state, RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC, writer) before applying a write, denying with the correct wire error (rcp_lifecycle_field_write_error()) if unauthorized -- direct verification of TC18 §12.7.6's own surrounding prose ("This configuration table can only be changed in the life-cycle state HW_unconfigured. In other states of the life cycle this is read-only") confirms HW_GENERIC, not FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR, is the correct kind despite this table's own generic "R/W*" column legend -- a table-specific override caught and corrected during this same batch, before merge. No caller-owned lifecycle-state context is needed anymore: the dispatcher's own signature now simply takes state/writer as parameters, the same way every other write path in this codebase already does. This closes the only remaining gap this requirement's own text tracked.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 HW pin mapping configuration, TC18.txt L2691-2695

requirements.title: HW_config rows are 3 octets per IO pin at relative addresses 3*N, 3*N+1, 3*N+2
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.6 Table 21 (RC1 baseline: Table 19, renumbered in the current RC5 baseline) lays the HW_config map out as three consecutive 8-bit R/W* registers per physical IO pin — hw_ep_nr, hw_ep_pin_nr, hw_pin_type — so that IO_Pin 1 occupies relative addresses 0x0000/0x0001/0x0002, IO_Pin 2 occupies 0x0003/0x0004/0x0005, IO_Pin 3 begins at 0x0006, and IO pin N begins at relative address 3*N (relative to HW_config's own start, i.e. to svr_hw_cfg_ptr's own current value -- confirmed correct against the current PDF's own "Relative Address" column header for this table, unlike Table 20's own, differently-headed column, see REQ-RMAP-040's own text). c-RCP's row already carried the three correctly-typed, correctly-named fields. rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_render() serializes a real table at exactly this 3*N stride. RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301): the ACF_ABB WRITE wrapper this entry's own prior text called missing now exists -- rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_apply_reconfig() (the parse-side inverse of render(), patch-then-reparse idiom matching every other endpoint type's own apply_reconfig()) plus rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request()'s own address-routing to it. READ SIDE ALSO RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301 batch 4): rcp_regmap_ep0_encode_read_response() serves this exact stride back over the wire, reusing rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_render() directly -- see REQ-RMAP-040's own text for the full read-side detail. AUTHORIZATION CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #308): see REQ-RMAP-040's own text -- the write dispatcher now enforces exactly this access type (RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC, not FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR despite the "R/W*" column legend -- a table-specific TC18 §12.7.6 override) before applying any write to this table. This closes the only remaining gap this requirement's own text tracked.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 Table 21: HW_config, TC18.txt L2698-2717

requirements.title: hw_pin_type now matches Table 20's own four-packed-sub-field bit layout
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.6 Table 20 defines the hw_pin_type octet as four packed sub-fields — Pull at bits 1:0 (00b float, 01b pull down, 10b pull up), Output stage at bits 3:2 (00b input, 01b open drain, 10b open source, 11b push pull), Drive strength at bits 5:4 (00b input, 01b low, 10b medium, 11b high), reserved bit 6 reading 0, and Schmitt-Trigger enable at bit 7. Fixed: rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_entry_t's own third field (renamed pin_property -> hw_pin_type, matching the wire register's own name) now uses a dedicated RCP_REGMAP_HW_PIN_* constant family at exactly these bit positions, primary-source verified directly against the TC18 v0.5.1_RC PDF (pdftotext -layout extraction, since no local TC18.txt was found this session). This is a distinct, separately-named family from RCP_REGMAP_PIN_PROP_* (ep_gpio.h's own, differently-shaped, per-pin runtime-adjustable field, REQ-GPIO-013 -- deliberately left untouched by this fix, since they are two different registers that happened to share one set of bit-position constants, not one register two ways). config.h/config.c's manifest JSON schema updated to match (hw_pin_map entries now use "hw_pin_type": [...] with Table-20-derived string values -- pull_down/pull_up, open_drain/open_source/push_pull, low_drive/medium_drive/high_drive, schmitt_trigger -- rather than the old six one-hot names).
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 Table 22: IO-pin properties, TC18.txt L3096-3145

requirements.title: hw_pin_type's output stage has no separate, exclusive input flag to toggle away from
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.6 states that the pin direction/drive entry is split into exactly four sub-fields (pull resistor, output stage, drive strength, Schmitt-trigger) and that ALL OUTPUTS ARE ALWAYS ALSO AN INPUT — output and input are not mutually exclusive pin states. Fixed: hw_pin_type's own output-stage field (RCP_REGMAP_HW_PIN_STAGE_*, REQ-RMAP-042) selects one of four drive modes (input/open-drain/open-source/push-pull) rather than toggling a separate exclusive INPUT/OUTPUT flag pair the way the old shared RCP_REGMAP_PIN_PROP_OUTPUT/_INPUT bits did -- there is structurally no "pure output, unreadable" state to represent, matching TC18's own prose exactly. Still open, and NOT resolved by this fix: ep_gpio.h's own, separate pin_property field and rcp_ep_gpio_apply_reconfig()'s OUTPUT<->INPUT toggle (REQ-GPIO-013) still have this exact problem for GPIO's own runtime-adjustable per-pin state -- that is a different register (this table's own hw_pin_type has no runtime-write path of its own at all, REQ-RMAP-041) with its own separate architecture question, not resolved here; see this session's own investigation note on issue #200 for the full analysis, including the discovery that GPIO's evt[2:0]=111b write semantics (RCP_EP_GPIO_WRITE_RECONFIG) itself appears to deviate from TC18's own generic EP_func-block-write definition (§12.7.1/Figure 18), a larger, separate finding.

requirements.title: The EP_Signal_Nr enumeration now covers every endpoint type
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.6 Table 23 enumerates the EP_Signal_Nr values for every endpoint type — GPIO 0..31; SPI 0..8 (CLK, PICO, POCI, CS0..CS5); I2C 0..1 (SCL, SDA); UART 0..3 (TX, RX, RTS, CTS); LIN 0..2 (TXD, RXD, NSLP); PWM_OUT 0..1 (positive phase, inverted phase); PWM_IN 0; ADC 0 (ADC_IN); DAC 0 (DAC_OUT); CAN 0 RXD and 1 TXD; ISELED 0 ISP_P and 1 ISP_N; MDIO 0 MDC and 1 MDIO. Fixed: rcp_regmap_named_signal_t (include/rcp/regmap.h) now enumerates all eleven endpoint types, matching Table 23's own signal names and order (primary-source verified directly against the TC18 v0.5.1_RC PDF before implementing, per standing policy on trusting tooling/derived text over the primary spec). CAN's counter-intuitive ordering (RXD = 0, TXD = 1) is recorded. Still open: this is a content/naming fix only — no wire encode/decode path for the HW_config table exists yet (REQ-RMAP-040/-041, this Group's own remaining items) to actually validate a hw_ep_pin_nr value against this enumeration.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 Table 23: Enumeration of signals at endpoints, TC18.txt L2779-2820

requirements.title: EP_Signal_Nr restarts at 0 for each endpoint type; c-RCP now converts between the two numbering schemes
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.6 states the EP_Pin_Nr mapping is specific per endpoint type, and Table 23 accordingly restarts EP_Signal_Nr at 0 for every EP_Type — SPI_CLK is 0, I2C_SCL is 0, UART_TX is 0, CAN RXD is 0, and so on — so that hw_ep_pin_nr in a HW_config entry (Table 21, relative address 0x0001) is interpreted relative to the endpoint type named by hw_ep_nr. c-RCP's rcp_regmap_named_signal_t (include/rcp/regmap.h) is a flat global enumeration in which SPI_CLK and I2C_SCL do not sit at ordinal 0 (primary-source verified directly against the TC18 v0.5.1_RC PDF before implementing). Fixed: rcp_regmap_named_signal_ep_signal_nr() (src/regmap.c) converts this enum's own flat ordinal into TC18's per-type-relative wire value — SPI_CLK/I2C_SCL/UART_TX/CAN_RXD/etc. all correctly convert to 0, restarting per type exactly as Table 23 requires. Still open: this is a content/conversion fix only — no wire encode/decode path for the HW_config table exists yet (REQ-RMAP-040/-041) to actually write a converted value into a real hw_ep_pin_nr register.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 Table 23 + Table 21 row hw_ep_pin_nr, TC18.txt L2704, L2764, L2779-2820

requirements.title: RETIRED -- merged into REQ-RMAP-039, which already covers this
requirements.text: RETIRED (2026-08-10, c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H): this entry was a stale duplicate of REQ-RMAP-039. It described the same four product-specific configuration-section pointer/capacity pairs (network/physical-layer/time-synch/security, TC18 §12.7.11-.14) as "NOT IMPLEMENTED", but REQ-RMAP-039 (batch 22, this session) already declared all eight registers in rcp_regmap_general_t and marked the pair PARTIAL -- this entry's own text was simply never updated to match, leaving a requirement that flatly contradicted its own sibling entry about the identical fields. See REQ-RMAP-039 for the current, accurate status (registers declared; still no real config-table storage behind the pointers, and the address range is past the discovery response's own wire-reachability ceiling, REQ-RMAP-024). No code change from this retirement -- text-only correction.
requirements.tc18: see REQ-RMAP-039

requirements.title: Request-stream config carries a per-stream secure-channel index selecting the MACsec channel
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-12, issue #200): rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t carries rx_secure_channel_index (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 24, relative address 0x000C, 8 bit, R/W*), zero-initialized to TC18's own defined "no cyber security, MACsec uncontrolled port" default. WIRE DISPATCH CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #306, same finding as issue #301's own HW_config/EP_ID_config/response-queue-config): request-stream-cfg is a fourth pointed-to table sharing that same absolute-address finding -- svr_request_stream_cfg_ptr's own value is an absolute address in the same EP0-scoped space Table 20 itself lives in. New rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_render()/_apply_reconfig() (regmap.h/regmap.c) give this table its own wire codec (24-octet-per-row stride, confirmed via direct read of both the RC1 PDF pages 57-58 and the current RC5 PDF page 66); rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request()/_encode_read_response() now route to it the identical way as the other three tables. A client can now write AND read rx_secure_channel_index over the wire. AUTHORIZATION CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #308): rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() now consults rcp_lifecycle_field_writable(state, RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR, writer) before applying a write to this table -- direct verification of TC18 §12.7.7's own surrounding prose confirms request-stream-cfg's own R/W* fields genuinely follow the generic FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR rule (unlike HW_config's own table-specific override, see REQ-RMAP-040's own text), so no correction was needed here. RESCOPED 2026-08-12 (issue #200): this requirement's own scope is the register's existence, default, wire read/write reachability, and access authorization -- all four now satisfied. Whether this library ever grows its own MACsec (802.1AE) layer that would ACT on a selected channel is a separate, already-decided architectural boundary, not a gap in this requirement: MACsec enforcement was deliberately never part of this library's own scope (CHANGELOG.md's Deprecation & Removal Log: tls.h/tls.c, v0.78.0, removed with the identical "link-layer, out of this library's scope" reasoning). Selecting and exposing the channel index is the whole of what a register-map/wire-protocol library is responsible for; acting on it is a link-layer concern this codebase has consistently, deliberately excluded elsewhere too.

requirements.title: request stream's acknowledge-stream pointer (rx_ack_stream_index)
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t now carries rx_ack_stream_index (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 24, relative address 0x0010, 8 bit, R/W*), the index of the stream on which endpoints bound to this request stream shall send their acknowledges, zero-initialized to TC18's own defined "no acknowledge is to be sent" default. WIRE DISPATCH CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #306): see REQ-RMAP-047's own text -- the identical wire codec now serves this field too; a client can now write AND read rx_ack_stream_index over the wire. AUTHORIZATION CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #308): see REQ-RMAP-047's own text -- the write dispatcher now enforces this table's own FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR access type before applying any write, including to this field. STILL PARTIAL: no code path yet routes an acknowledgement to a selected response queue from this field -- a genuinely separate, still-open gap about runtime behavior consuming the field, not about wire reachability. RUNTIME CONSUMPTION CLOSED 2026-08-14 (tc18-gap post-backlog audit): mock.c's own dispatch_plain() now wraps its (renamed, unchanged) own body in a new suppress_response_per_stream_cfg() step, applied uniformly to every mock.c dispatch entry point (dispatch(), dispatch_e2e(), dispatch_e2e_fragment() all delegate through this same choke point). This module owns no real multi-stream transport to actually DELIVER a response on a caller-chosen stream (unchanged; same 'protocol library, not a transport' boundary REQ-SRV-016/017/018 and REQ-RMAP-065 already establish) -- but the field's own TC18-defined '0 means no acknowledge is to be sent' half needs no transport concept at all: a built response is classified via rcp_acf_classify_response() and, if Acknowledge-shaped and rx_ack_stream_index == 0 for the resolved stream, simply freed before returning to the caller -- exactly as if this dispatch call had taken one of this module's own pre-existing 'no response' paths. Field separation (an Acknowledge is governed ONLY by rx_ack_stream_index, never by rx_resp_stream_index) is proven by a dedicated test setting both fields to conflicting values on the same stream. This module's own dispatch pipeline still never builds an Acknowledge-classified response itself today (admit(), unlike the lower-level rcp_server_endpoint_submit(), has no evt[3]-triggered out_ack of its own -- a separate, already-known, not-yet-wired gap, unchanged by this fix) -- so this suppression is presently reachable only via a caller-supplied endpoint handler that builds an Acknowledge itself, proven directly by a dedicated test using exactly such a handler. Both the field's own suppression condition and the classification branch were mutation-tested and caught cleanly (the unresolvable-stream guard was caught via a SIGBUS crash, an even stronger signal).

requirements.title: request stream's response-stream pointer and its discovery-enabling default of 1 (rx_resp_stream_index)
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t now carries rx_resp_stream_index (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 24, relative address 0x0011, 8 bit, R/W*), the index of the stream on which endpoints bound to this request stream shall send their responses, with 0 meaning "no response is to be sent". FIXED: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_init() now sets this one field to 1 (not 0), reproducing the specification's own bootstrap guarantee that a freshly reset server can answer a discovery request before any configuration has been written -- REQ-RMAP-018's own text was corrected to carve out this deliberate exception to its "zero everything" rule. WIRE DISPATCH CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #306): see REQ-RMAP-047's own text -- the identical wire codec now serves this field too; a client can now write AND read rx_resp_stream_index over the wire. AUTHORIZATION CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #308): see REQ-RMAP-047's own text -- the write dispatcher now enforces this table's own FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR access type before applying any write, including to this field. PLAUSIBILITY-VALIDATION HALF CLOSED 2026-08-13 (issue #338, tc18-gap backlog PR A): rcp_lifecycle_check_rcp_cfg()'s own RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT check previously only checked a boolean has_response_stream (src/lifecycle.c), which recorded that SOME response stream exists but not which one. rcp_lifecycle_request_stream_plausibility_t now carries a caller-supplied response_stream_index field, validated against a new response_stream_count on the snapshot (rcp_lifecycle_plausibility_snapshot_t) -- the same request_stream_index/request_stream_count cross-reference convention REQ-LIFECYCLE-038 already established one level up. STILL PARTIAL: no code path yet routes a live response to the selected stream from this field at runtime (the ack-routing half) -- that is a genuinely separate, still-open gap about runtime behavior consuming the field, not about wire reachability or plausibility validation, and (per project decision 2026-08-13) is left documented rather than built out in this pass. RUNTIME CONSUMPTION CLOSED 2026-08-14 (tc18-gap post-backlog audit): see REQ-RMAP-048's own text -- the identical suppress_response_per_stream_cfg() wiring (mock.c) now also governs this field: a built response classified as anything OTHER than Acknowledge (Write/Read/Error -- everything mock.c's own dispatch pipeline actually produces today) is suppressed when rx_resp_stream_index == 0 for the resolved stream, exercised end to end through rcp_mock_server_dispatch() itself with a real ACF_ABB-encoded request/response pair, not merely by reading the struct field directly. An unresolvable stream_id (no rcp_mock_server_set_request_stream_cfg() call for it) suppresses nothing, matching every other fail-toward-no-action resolve_index() call site in mock.c; rx_resp_stream_index's own nonzero default (REQ-RMAP-049's own earlier fix) means every pre-existing test in this codebase that never configures a request stream, or that configures one and leaves this field at its default, is completely unaffected -- confirmed by a full, unmodified 66-test-suite pass before any new test was added. The suppression condition was mutation-tested and caught cleanly.

requirements.title: Watchdog timeout register width and unit deviate from Table 24's 16-bit clock-tick field
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t.rx_wd_timeout_ms shall represent TC18 §12.7.7 Table 24's rx_wd_timeout_intervall register (relative address 0x000A, 16 bit, R/W*, expressed in clock tics). c-RCP deliberately stores it as a 32-bit millisecond value and rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate() compares it against elapsed_since_last_kick_ms, so a conversion between the server's clock-tick domain and milliseconds shall be applied at the register-write boundary, and a written value shall be rejected if it does not fit the register's 16-bit width. IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-13, issue #334, user-approved after a dedicated safety-direction investigation): rcp_regmap_wd_timeout_ms_to_ticks()/_ticks_to_ms() (regmap.h/.c) already performed the conversion and 16-bit bounds check; both rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_render()/_apply_reconfig() and the EP0 dispatchers that call them (rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request()/_encode_read_response()) now take a new trailing watchdog_ms_per_tick parameter and actually wire this register, closing the "no register-write code path calls these functions yet" gap. TC18 names no fixed clock-tick rate for this register, so, matching the established caller-supplies-already-classified-units convention, the caller (ultimately whatever integrates this library with a real clock) supplies it; 0 means "not configured" and is a safe default (both conversion primitives already reject ms_per_tick == 0 on their own, so this fails closed with no separate sentinel needed). REQ-RMAP-050's own "a written value shall be rejected if it does not fit the register's 16-bit width" rule is, on inspection, about VALIDATING a value before it is accepted into rx_wd_timeout_ms (the READ/render direction: an internal ms value that doesn't convert to 16-bit ticks falls back to encoding 0x0000, the same "reserved / cannot be represented" treatment REQ-RMAP-024's own HW_config alignment octet already uses) -- not the WRITE/apply_reconfig direction, where the arriving wire value is always exactly 16 bits by construction and can never itself violate a width constraint. When the ticks-to-ms conversion still fails on write (unconfigured rate, or a degenerate internal-representation overflow), rx_wd_timeout_ms is left unchanged rather than failing the whole apply_reconfig() call -- strictly more conservative than an all-or-nothing reject that would also discard unrelated fields' legitimate changes in the same write. 5 new tests + 2 mutation tests confirm both directions.

requirements.title: Table 24's W* fields are writable in both HW_UNCONFIGURED and HW_CONFIGURED and read-only in RCP_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: Every field of the request-stream configuration table (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 24) marked R/W* shall be classified RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR and shall be writable while the server is in RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_UNCONFIGURED or RCP_LIFECYCLE_HW_CONFIGURED and read-only in RCP_LIFECYCLE_RCP_CONFIGURED. FIXED: rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() (src/lifecycle.c) now returns true for FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR in both HW_UNCONFIGURED and HW_CONFIGURED, false only in RCP_CONFIGURED, matching Table 24's own legend exactly (TC18.txt L2929-L2931). WIRED 2026-08-11 (issue #308): rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request()'s own request-stream-cfg routing block now calls rcp_lifecycle_field_writable(state, RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR, writer) before applying any write to Table 24 -- the register-map write path this entry's own prior text called missing now exists, closing the architecture gap this entry tracked. CORRECTED 2026-08-14 (issue #424): "every field... marked R/W*" above is not quite accurate -- Table 24's own row-relative offset 0x000D bit 7 (rx_stream_status) is a genuinely distinct, plain R/W bit sharing that octet with seven real R/W* enforcement bits, and this entry's own prior FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR gate applied to the WHOLE octet with no carve-out, over-restricting that one bit's writability to HW_UNCONFIGURED/HW_CONFIGURED only. New static helper request_stream_cfg_row_write_authorize() (src/regmap.c) is the narrow fix: FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR is checked first and remains sufficient and correct for every octet without exception; only when it FAILS (RCP_CONFIGURED) does the carve-out apply -- a write whose own final effective bytes leave bits [6:0] of 0x000D unchanged from the table's own current rendered content is still authorized (bit 7 alone changing), while a write that would ALSO change any of those seven bits remains denied even if it also touches bit 7, so the carve-out can never be used to smuggle a safety-relevant enforcement-bit change past FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR's own closed window. Three new tests prove: a bit-7-only write is authorized under RCP_CONFIGURED; the identical write with a bit-0 (rx_enforce_e2e) change added is still denied under RCP_CONFIGURED; and that same bit-0 write is authorized in HW_UNCONFIGURED, isolating the RCP_CONFIGURED denial as the real behavior under test. See REQ-E2E-046's own text for this same fix's register-READ half.

requirements.title: EP_ID_config rows are now (Request_Stream_Index, EP_Nr, BBID) triples, not (EP_Nr, BBID) pairs
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_entry_t shall model one full row of the EP_ID_config table (TC18 §12.7.8 Table 23): a Request_Stream_Index (relative offset 0x0000 within the row, 8 bit, R/W+), an EP_Nr (0x0001, 8 bit, R/W+) and a BBID (0x0002, 16 bit, R/W+), so that the same byte_bus_id can be mapped to different endpoints on different request streams. rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_entry_t declares request_stream_index, closing this field-content gap -- the specification's central addressing rule that a byte_bus_id is unique only within the stream_id it is paired with (include/rcp/avtp.h's own note) is now representable in this codebase's own in-memory model. Deliberately placed as this struct's LAST field (TC18's own row puts it first, at row offset 0x0000) so every existing positional-initializer test call site kept compiling unchanged -- this struct is content modeling only, not a wire-order layout, so C field order carries no TC18 conformance obligation. rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_render() (regmap.h/regmap.c) now serializes a real table at TC18's own exact 4-octet-per-row stride (row N at relative address 4*N), proven via a byte-offset test. RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301, same finding as REQ-RMAP-040's own text): the addressing question this entry's own prior text called genuinely unresolved is now answered -- direct verification of the current RC5 baseline PDF (page 61) shows Table 20's own address column is headed "Absolute address", confirming svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_ptr's own value is an absolute address in the same EP0-scoped space Table 20 itself lives in; a client reaches EP_ID_config via an ordinary evt[2:0]=111b request to byte_bus_id=0 with start_address = svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_ptr's current value plus an offset. rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() (regmap.h/regmap.c) now implements exactly this for EP_ID_config too: it routes an incoming write across svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_ptr's own extent, applied via the new rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_apply_reconfig(), the parse-side inverse of rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_render() (identical patch-then-reparse idiom to rcp_regmap_hw_pin_map_apply_reconfig()). READ SIDE ALSO RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301 batch 4): rcp_regmap_ep0_encode_read_response() routes to EP_ID_config's own extent too, reusing rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_render() directly -- a client can now write AND read EP_ID_config over the wire. AUTHORIZATION CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #308): rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() now consults rcp_lifecycle_field_writable_w_plus(state, writer, map->svr_configuration_lock != 0) before applying a write, denying with the correct wire error (rcp_lifecycle_field_write_error_w_plus()) if unauthorized or locked -- REQ-RMAP-029's own svr_configuration_lock field IS TC18's own single, global W+ lock ("0x00: write access to R/W+ type parameters allowed; else: rejected"), confirmed via direct primary-source read, not a new per-table lock this codebase invents. This closes the only remaining gap this requirement's own text tracked. CITATION CORRECTED, BBID/Ctrl PACKING FIXED 2026-08-14 (issue #421): this requirement's own row-content description (Request_Stream_Index/EP_Nr/BBID) cited "Table 23" -- WRONG; the real table is Table 25 (EP_ID_config), not Table 23 ("Enumeration of signals at endpoints", an unrelated table) -- corrected here and in regmap.h/regmap.c/tests. Separately, a genuine wire-codec defect was found and fixed in the same batch: rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_render()/_apply_reconfig() serialized/parsed the 16-bit word at each row's own relative offset 0x0002 as a flat, unshifted byte_bus_id, but TC18 Table 25 packs it -- bits[15:5] are the 11-bit BBID, bits[4:0] are a separate "Ctrl" sub-field (Table 26). Both functions now shift BBID into/out of bits[15:5] (masked to its own real 11-bit width, matching rcp_acf_pack_header()'s own established masking convention, acf.c); any real client reading/writing byte_bus_id below 2048 previously got a non-conformant value. See REQ-RMAP-053's own text for the new crc_required field this same fix adds.

requirements.title: byte_bus_id is an 11-bit address; rcp_byte_bus_id_t now represents the full 0..2047 range
requirements.text: rcp_byte_bus_id_t shall be wide enough to hold the full 11-bit byte_bus_id the EP_ID_config table's BBID register carries (TC18 §12.7.8 Table 23, row offset 0x0002, 16 bit register, "Byte_bus_id [11bit]") and that the ACF byte_message_info header transports across octet 2 bits [2:0] and octet 3 (REQ-ACF-016). Fixed: rcp_byte_bus_id_t is now uint16_t (include/rcp/avtp.h), and byte_bus_id[10:8] is a real, encoded/decoded value on both the pack and unpack paths (src/acf.c) rather than structurally always zero. Full "read every consumer" investigation performed first (~55 files touching the type): every endpoint type module, the conditional-request layer, config.c, lifecycle.c, mock.c, and server.c were all confirmed to be simple pass-through consumers needing no logic changes; two real consumer-side fixes were needed and made alongside the type change -- adapt.c's byte_bus_id-to-string buffer (char[4], sized for "255"+NUL) was widened to char[6] ("2047"+NUL), and test_mock.c's own decode-failure test needed a new stimulus (an over-declared pad count) since its old one (a high byte_bus_id) no longer fails to decode. REQ-ACF-020's own companion requirement (the same underlying gap, viewed from the ACF wire layer) is fixed by the same change; RCP_ACF_ERR_BUS_ID_OVERFLOW is retired outright, not left as dead code, since the condition it represented can no longer occur. c-RCP can now address all 2048 endpoints per stream the protocol defines. CITATION CORRECTED, BBID/Ctrl PACKING FIXED 2026-08-14 (issue #421): this requirement's own "11 bit" citation said "Table 23" -- WRONG; the real table is Table 25 (EP_ID_config row layout) / Table 26 (BBID control bits), not Table 23 ("Enumeration of signals at endpoints", an unrelated table). Separately, the EP_ID_config row's own BBID register (row-relative offset 0x0002) was found to be wire-encoded as a flat, unshifted 16-bit value instead of Table 25's real bits[15:5] BBID / bits[4:0] Ctrl packing -- rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_render()/_apply_reconfig() now pack/unpack it correctly (masked to the real 11-bit width on render, the same masking convention rcp_acf_pack_header() already uses for this codebase's OTHER byte_bus_id wire encoding, acf.c). A new rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_entry_t.crc_required bool field (Table 26 bit 4, "051RC5: added due to NXP_101") is now packed at bit 4; Channel_selection (Table 26 bits [3:0]) remains DELIBERATELY unimplemented, per the existing dedicated investigation on record (ep_spi.h's own file header) -- always rendered 0, silently dropped on write. New tests round-trip a byte_bus_id >= 32 (so the shift is genuinely exercised) with crc_required true and false, and prove Channel_selection is never round-tripped.

requirements.title: A Request_Stream_Index of 0 terminates the EP_ID_config table, and the power-on defaults address EP0
requirements.text: Every consumer of the EP_ID_config table shall stop scanning at the first row whose Request_Stream_Index is 0, that value denoting the end of the table rather than a valid stream index (TC18 §12.7.8 Table 23 / L2976), and the table's power-on default contents (Request_Stream_Index = 1, EP_Nr = 0, BBID = 0) shall permit access to EP0 before any configuration is written. Fixed: rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_effective_count() (src/regmap.c) is the dedicated, sentinel-aware consumer -- it scans entries[0..capacity) and returns the count of leading rows before the first row whose request_stream_index is 0, or capacity unchanged if no such row appears. rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_row_init_default() supplies the power-on default row (request_stream_index=1, ep_id=RCP_REGMAP_EP0_INDEX, byte_bus_id=0), which permits EP0 access and, being nonzero in request_stream_index, does not itself look like the end-of-table sentinel. rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_is_ascending() (REQ-RMAP-056) deliberately remains sentinel-unaware, since it is a generic ordering diagnostic, not a table iterator -- sentinel recognition is this pair's job specifically. rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_render() (regmap.h/regmap.c, REQ-RMAP-052) now serializes a real table at TC18's own exact 4-octet-per-row stride, so a table this pair scans is also wire-layout-correct when rendered. RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301, same finding as REQ-RMAP-052's own text): the ACF_ABB WRITE wrapper this entry's own prior text called missing now exists -- rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_apply_reconfig() (the parse-side inverse of render(), patch-then-reparse idiom matching every other pointed-to table's own apply_reconfig()) plus rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request()'s own address-routing to it, targeted at svr_ep_bytebus_id_map_ptr's own extent. READ SIDE ALSO RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301 batch 4): rcp_regmap_ep0_encode_read_response() serves this exact stride back over the wire -- see REQ-RMAP-052's own text for the full read-side detail. AUTHORIZATION CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #308): see REQ-RMAP-052's own text -- the write dispatcher now enforces this table's own W+ access type (via rcp_lifecycle_field_writable_w_plus(), gated on REQ-RMAP-029's own svr_configuration_lock) before applying any write. This closes the only remaining gap this requirement's own text tracked.

requirements.title: the W+ lockable access type for EP_ID_config and the Table 24 W+ queue fields
requirements.text: rcp_lifecycle_field_writable_w_plus()/_write_error_w_plus() (lifecycle.h/lifecycle.c) implement TC18's W+ (explicitly lockable) register access type -- EP_ID_config rows (§12.7.8 Table 23) and the STREAM_UID/flush_on_count/Flush_time queue registers (§12.7.9 Table 24) are both marked R/W+: the table may be locked by the configuring instance to protect against unwanted later modification, independently of the lifecycle state that governs W and W*. Deliberately a SEPARATE function rather than a new rcp_lifecycle_field_kind_t value threaded through rcp_lifecycle_field_writable()'s own signature -- that function has roughly 90 existing call sites across every endpoint type, 2 internal uses, and every test exercising any of them, none of which need a lock concept; a standalone function delivers the same primitive with zero blast radius to existing callers, reusing (not re-deriving) the existing FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR state/writer rule internally. WIRED 2026-08-11 (issue #308): rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() now calls this primitive for both tables before applying any write -- EP_ID_config's whole row via rcp_lifecycle_field_writable_w_plus() directly against svr_configuration_lock, and Table 24's own mixed-field row via the new respqueue_cfg_row_write_authorize() helper, which classifies each touched octet's row-relative offset and requires the W+ variant to authorize whenever a write touches STREAM_UID/flush_on_count/Flush_time. This closes the register-map write path this entry's own prior text called missing -- a client can now actually latch either table over the wire, subject to this authorization.

requirements.title: EP_ID_config ordering is ascending in (Request_Stream_Index, BBID), not BBID alone
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_is_ascending() reports whether the EP_ID_config table is ordered ascending in the composite key (Request_Stream_Index, BBID), the ordering TC18 §12.7.8 requires the configuring instance to maintain and whose violation the specification says can cause requests to be dropped because no endpoint is found. Fixed: the implementation (src/regmap.c) now compares request_stream_index first between consecutive rows — a decrease is always reported non-ascending, an increase is always reported ascending regardless of that row's own byte_bus_id (TC18 does not require byte_bus_id to reset or relate across different streams) — and falls back to the prior strict byte_bus_id comparison only when request_stream_index is unchanged between the two rows. A per-stream-ascending table that interleaves streams (e.g. stream 1 BBIDs 1,2 then stream 2 BBIDs 1,2 again) is now correctly reported ascending, and a table whose stream index goes backwards is correctly reported non-ascending regardless of BBID. UPDATED 2026-08-11 (spec rebaseline to TC18 0.5.1_RC5): see REQ-RMAP-020's own note -- the ordering requirement itself is deleted from TC18 as of spec revision 0.5.1_RC4; this function's own composite-key comparison logic remains correct and harmless (pure diagnostic, no server-side enforcement), but no longer traces to a live TC18 MUST.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.8, TC18.txt L3364-L3367 -- REMOVED in spec revision 0.5.1_RC4, TC18 PDF 0.5.1_RC5 p.68 (sentence shown struck through, 051RC4 tag)

requirements.title: single-RC-Client-per-endpoint recommendation is neither enforced nor diagnosed
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-12, issue #200): TC18 §12.7.8's own text reads "For safety reasons it is RECOMMENDED that one endpoint is only used by one RC Client at a time" (TC18.txt L2985) -- a non-normative recommendation, not a MUST/SHALL enforcement requirement. rcp_regmap_ep_client_t.owning_stream_index (include/rcp/regmap.h) exists to authorize functional-config writes (REQ-RMAP-011/012), not to constrain which request streams may deliver requests to an endpoint. A read-only DIAGNOSTIC, rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_has_single_client_per_ep() (src/regmap.c), reports the condition -- true iff no ep_id in the table is associated with two different request_stream_index values; an endpoint reachable from several rows that all share one request_stream_index (multiple byte_bus_ids, one client) is correctly NOT flagged, only a genuine multi-stream (multi-client) mapping is. Matches rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_is_ascending()'s own established read-only-diagnostic, not-enforcement shape. RESCOPED: no server-side rejection or correction of a multi-client table exists, matching this table's own standing "Known spec ambiguity" note -- TC18 itself defines no corrective action for a server that receives one, so a diagnostic surfacing a RECOMMENDED (not MUST) condition is the full, appropriate extent of what this requirement calls for.

requirements.title: endpoints sharing a byte_bus_id within one stream should be of the same ep_type
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-12, issue #200): TC18 §12.7.8's own text reads "If multiple endpoints are using the same byte_bus_id inside one stream they SHOULD be of the same type" (TC18.txt L2988) -- a non-normative recommendation, not a MUST/SHALL enforcement requirement. A shared byte_bus_id is a deliberate multicast-within-a-stream mechanism, and a request broadcast to endpoints of differing ep_type is decoded differently by each. A read-only DIAGNOSTIC, rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_shared_bus_homogeneous() (src/regmap.c), reports the condition. rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_entry_t itself carries no ep_type (TC18's own EP_ID_config row doesn't have one -- ep_type lives on rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_t, looked up by ep_id), so the diagnostic takes a caller-supplied, index-parallel ep_types[] array rather than inventing a field this row doesn't have on the wire; it returns true iff every group of rows sharing one (request_stream_index, byte_bus_id) pair has an identical ep_types[] value throughout. RESCOPED: TC18 itself gives this condition no MUST-level treatment, so a diagnostic surfacing it is the appropriate extent of support -- no server-side rejection or correction of a heterogeneous shared-bus group is required, and none exists. STILL SEPARATELY OPEN, matching this codebase's established "primitive complete, dispatch wiring deferred" disposition (e.g. REQ-ADC-031, REQ-GPIO-033): nothing in this codebase yet calls this diagnostic with a real, live ep_types[] array sourced from the actual per-endpoint configuration table at request-admission time -- that integration wiring remains real, separate future work, not modeled here, and does not block this requirement's own closure (the diagnostic itself is complete and directly, independently tested).

requirements.title: per-response/acknowledge-stream transmit queue and its queue_size register
requirements.text: regmap.h's rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t gains a queue_size register (TC18 §12.7.9 Table 24, relative address 0x0004, 16 bit, R/W*, "Queue N assigned memory in 32bit words"), and a new module, respqueue.h/respqueue.c, provides the actual transmit queue this codebase was missing entirely: rcp_respqueue_t, an octet-budgeted FIFO of framed response/acknowledge messages (rcp_respqueue_push()/_pop(), capacity enforced against queue_size x 4 octets, refusing a push that would exceed it and leaving the queue unchanged). Distinct from server.h's ep_enable pre-load queue, which holds inbound requests, not outbound responses. The remaining Group 4 behaviors this queue's own contents will need (Max_AVTPDUsize transmit enforcement/fragmentation REQ-RMAP-061/062, the flush_on_count packing trigger REQ-RMAP-063, the Flush_time timer and heartbeat REQ-RMAP-064/065) are deliberately not modeled here -- this closes the storage-and-capacity scope only. RESOLVED 2026-08-14 (issue #423): TC18 §12.9.4/§12.9.5 give a SEPARATE, additional MUST rule this entry's own text never modeled -- once the queue's own bounded slot count (not this entry's queue_size byte budget, which stays completely unchanged) is completely full, the entry with the lowest sequence_num must be evicted to admit the new one, with an overflow bit set. rcp_respqueue_push()/_push_seq() (respqueue.h/respqueue.c) now implement exactly that: a new RCP_RESPQUEUE_MAX_ENTRIES (64, matching this codebase's own established MAX_ENTRIES convention) slot bound, evict-the-numerically-lowest-sequence_num-entry-by-linear-scan on push once reached, and a latched q->overflow bit (rcp_respqueue_overflow()/_clear_overflow()). Before this fix, a push against a completely full queue was silently rejected and the queue (including every stale entry already queued) left entirely unchanged -- the inverse of TC18's own mandatory behavior. TRIGGER CORRECTED 2026-08-14 (issue #446, a post-merge audit re-check of the #423 fix): the #423 fix wired eviction to the wrong 'completely full' condition -- RCP_RESPQUEUE_MAX_ENTRIES, a NEW, spec-uncited slot-count bound -- while this entry's own capacity_octets byte-budget path (the REAL TC18 queue_size register this entry's own text above describes) kept doing plain reject-and-leave-unchanged, unaffected. TC18 §12.7.9 defines exactly one 'queue is completely full' concept (queue_size/capacity_octets); there is no TC18-defined entry-count bound at all, so in any realistically-configured server where capacity_octets is the binding constraint (the ordinary case), the #423 eviction/overflow behavior never fired. rcp_respqueue_push_seq() now triggers eviction on capacity_octets exhaustion directly -- evicting lowest-sequence_num entries repeatedly (as many as needed to free enough octets for the incoming frame, since one eviction does not always free enough bytes) whenever accepting a frame would exceed capacity_octets, and refusing outright (queue unchanged, no eviction) only when frame_len exceeds capacity_octets in its entirety, unfixable by any amount of eviction. RCP_RESPQUEUE_MAX_ENTRIES is retained, but only as the secondary, defensive fallback for the capacity_octets == 0 (unbounded) case the issue's own recommendation specified -- once capacity_octets is nonzero, the slot-count bound no longer applies at all.

requirements.title: response queue's STREAM_UID (the unique_id half of the queue's outgoing stream_id)
requirements.text: regmap.h's rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t gains a stream_uid field (TC18 §12.7.9 Table 24, relative address 0x0000, 16 bit, R/W+) and a new rcp_regmap_response_queue_stream_id(cfg, mac) helper that combines it with the interface's own mac exactly as rcp_stream_id_make() (avtp.h) would — a thin, directly-testable named wrapper, not new stream_id-construction logic. A response queue now has an identity rx_ack_stream_index/rx_resp_stream_index (Table 24) can point at.

requirements.title: Max_AVTPDUsize bounds every transmitted AVTPDU, is MTU-consistent, and is discoverable
requirements.text: respqueue.h's rcp_respqueue_t enforces the transmit-bounding half -- rcp_respqueue_init() takes max_avtpdu_size_octets (regmap.h's rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t.max_avtpdu_size, quadlets x 4), and rcp_respqueue_push() refuses (queue unchanged) any single frame whose own length exceeds it. The MTU-consistency-check half is now also closed: rcp_respqueue_max_avtpdu_size_within_mtu() (respqueue.h/respqueue.c) is the config-time check TC18 §12.7.9 (TC18.txt L3010-3011, "the Max_AVTPDUsize shall always be configured such that the final network frame does not exceed the maximum transmit unit size of the network") requires -- a caller runs it before ever calling rcp_respqueue_init(); TC18 defines no fixed MTU value of its own, so mtu_budget_octets is the caller's own already-adjusted ceiling, matching this module's established "caller supplies already-classified units" convention. RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301 batch 3, same finding as REQ-RMAP-040/041 and REQ-RMAP-052/054's own text): the addressing question this entry's own prior text called genuinely unresolved is now answered -- svr_response_stream_cfg_ptr's own value is an absolute address in the same EP0-scoped space Table 20 itself lives in; a client reaches response-queue-config via an ordinary evt[2:0]=111b request to byte_bus_id=0 with start_address = svr_response_stream_cfg_ptr's current value plus an offset. Unlike HW_config/EP_ID_config, no render function existed for this table at all before this batch: rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_render() (regmap.h/regmap.c) is the first one, serializing TC18's own exact 10-octet-per-queue wire stride (STREAM_UID@0x0000, Max_AVTPDUsize@0x0002, queue_size@0x0004, flush_on_count@0x0006, Flush_time@0x0008). rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() now routes to it (via the new rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_apply_reconfig(), same patch-then-reparse idiom as the other two tables) the identical way. A genuine content/wire width mismatch was found and fixed in the same batch: rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t.flush_time_us is uint32_t, but Table 24's own Flush_time register is only 16 bits -- render() now saturates (never wraps) a value exceeding 0xFFFF, since wraparound could silently produce 0, TC18's own "flush only by count" encoding, inverting the field's own meaning. READ SIDE ALSO RESOLVED 2026-08-11 (issue #301 batch 4): rcp_regmap_ep0_encode_read_response() (regmap.h/regmap.c) routes to all three pointed-to tables at once, reusing each table's own already-proven render() function -- a client can now write AND read response-queue-config (and HW_config and EP_ID_config) over the wire the same way. Deliberately does NOT compose data across more than one extent when a read's own address+read_size would span into a second one -- TC18 defines no rule for that, and inventing one would not be primary-source-derived; the existing "response spans exactly read_size octets, zero-filled past the source's own extent" convention (already established by rcp_regmap_general_encode_read_response() for Table 20 alone) answers what happens past the requested extent's own length instead. AUTHORIZATION CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #308): rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() now enforces this table's own mixed R/W*/R/W+ access types (STREAM_UID/flush_on_count/Flush_time are R/W+, Max_AVTPDUsize/queue_size are R/W*) via a dedicated helper, respqueue_cfg_row_write_authorize(), that walks every row-relative octet a write touches and requires whichever access type(s) it actually touches to authorize -- not just the first octet's own type, so a write spanning both a W+ and a W* field within one row is correctly denied if either check fails. An earlier revision of this entry's own text described the remaining gap as "exposing the value in the discovery general-register slice" -- that framing predates this codebase's own later discovery that Table 24 was never part of the 14-octet discovery slice at all; corrected in an earlier batch. This closes the only remaining gap this requirement's own text tracked. OVERFLOW-BIT/EVICTION GAP RESOLVED 2026-08-14 (issue #423): TC18 §12.9.4/§12.9.5's own additional, mandatory rule -- once a response/acknowledge queue's bounded slot count is completely full, the entry with the lowest sequence_num must be evicted to admit the new one, with an overflow bit set -- had no implementation anywhere in this codebase; rcp_respqueue_push() instead rejected the new item outright and left the queue (including its stale entries) unchanged, the inverse of TC18's own requirement. rcp_respqueue_push()/_push_seq() (respqueue.h/respqueue.c) now evict the queued entry with the numerically lowest sequence_num (via q->entries_seq[], compared by linear scan, never merely the FIFO-oldest -- those two differ once sequence_num, an 8-bit counter matching AVTP's own sequence_num field width, has wrapped) once RCP_RESPQUEUE_MAX_ENTRIES (64) is reached, and latch a new q->overflow bit (rcp_respqueue_overflow()/_clear_overflow()) a caller reflects into whichever outgoing AVTPDU/ACF header field TC18 assigns it to -- the same disposition already established for e2e.h's rx_stream_status. This is a DIFFERENT rule from, and does not change, this entry's own Max_AVTPDUsize per-message ceiling above, which stays byte-for-byte unchanged (still checked first, still rejects-and-leaves-unchanged on its own). TRIGGER CORRECTED 2026-08-14 (issue #446): the #423 fix above wired eviction to RCP_RESPQUEUE_MAX_ENTRIES, a new, spec-uncited slot-count bound, not to REQ-RMAP-059's own capacity_octets (the real TC18 queue_size register, §12.7.9's only 'queue is completely full' concept) -- so in any realistically-configured server where capacity_octets is the binding constraint, the eviction/overflow behavior never fired. rcp_respqueue_push_seq() now triggers eviction on capacity_octets exhaustion directly (evicting lowest-sequence_num entries repeatedly until enough octets are freed for the incoming frame), refusing outright only when frame_len exceeds capacity_octets in its entirety; RCP_RESPQUEUE_MAX_ENTRIES is retained solely as the fallback for the capacity_octets == 0 (unbounded) case. See REQ-RMAP-059's own text above for the full detail -- this entry's own Max_AVTPDUsize per-message ceiling remains completely unaffected by this correction, exactly as it was unaffected by the original #423 fix.

requirements.title: A single ACF message exceeding Max_AVTPDUsize is fragmented via the ms bit
requirements.text: respqueue.h's rcp_respqueue_max_fragment_payload(max_avtpdu_size_octets, header_len) now derives the correct max_fragment_payload for fragment.h's existing rcp_fragment_plan_count()/rcp_fragment_plan() (REQ-FRAG-002..018, unchanged) from rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t.max_avtpdu_size (TC18 §12.7.9) -- converting the register's own quadlet unit to octets is the caller's job (this codebase's established 'caller supplies already-classified units' convention), and the helper conservatively reserves the fixed ACF header plus the worst-case 3 octets of trailing pad so the resulting budget is always safe. A caller with a payload too large for one AVTPDU derives this budget, plans the fragments, and pushes each one to rcp_respqueue_t individually (REQ-RMAP-061's own per-message enforcement then bounds each fragment independently).

requirements.title: flush_on_count triggers transmission of the whole queue packed into Max_AVTPDUsize-bounded AVTPDUs
requirements.text: respqueue.h's rcp_respqueue_should_flush(q, flush_on_count_octets) implements the trigger -- true once the queue's own running octet total reaches or exceeds the (caller-converted) threshold, matching this codebase's 'caller supplies already-classified units' convention. rcp_respqueue_plan_batch(q, max_avtpdu_size_octets) implements the packing: reports how many of the queue's FIFO-ordered entries fit together within one AVTPDU, so a caller drains exactly that many via rcp_respqueue_pop() and repeats until the queue is empty -- 'packed in a fitting number of AVTPDUs.' Both operate on the queue's own state alone; scheduler.h's rcp_sched_split_frame_members() (the inverse, decode-side split, unchanged) needed no changes.

requirements.title: Flush_time forces transmission once the configured interval since the last transmission elapses
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.9 Table 24, relative address 0x0008, 16 bit, R/W+, microseconds, 0 meaning "flush only by count": the server shall initiate transmission from a response queue whenever the time since that queue's last transmission is equal to or greater than Flush_time, independently of flush_on_count. rcp_respqueue_should_flush_by_time(elapsed_since_last_transmit_us, flush_time_us) (include/rcp/respqueue.h) implements the trigger as a pure, caller-timed check -- flush_time_us == 0 always false ("flush only by count"), otherwise true once elapsed_since_last_transmit_us reaches it -- mirroring e2e.h's own rcp_e2e_wd_evaluate(elapsed_since_last_kick_ms) convention of taking elapsed time as a caller-supplied input rather than reading a clock of its own. Deliberately independent of the queue's own entries_len, so it fires identically whether the queue is empty or not (REQ-RMAP-065's own precondition).

requirements.title: an empty response queue still emits a heartbeat AVTPDU on Flush_time expiry
requirements.text: PARTIAL: on Flush_time expiry the RC Server shall emit an AVTPDU from the queue even when that queue is empty, so the RC Client can observe that the server is alive (TC18 §12.7.9). rcp_respqueue_should_flush_by_time() (REQ-RMAP-064) already fires identically for an empty queue, rcp_respqueue_plan_batch() already reports 0 for an empty queue, and avtp.h's rcp_avtp_encode_ntscf(hdr, NULL, 0) already accepts a zero-length payload -- so the empty heartbeat AVTPDU is fully constructible from existing primitives (proven end to end by test_tc18_gaps_regmap.c's test_flush_time_trigger_and_empty_heartbeat_are_composable()). What remains open is the same boundary REQ-SRV-017 already states: c-RCP is a protocol library, not a scheduler, and ships no emitter that actually drives this composition against a real clock and a real transport -- that composition is left to the integrator. COMPOSITION WIRED 2026-08-14 (tc18-gap post-backlog audit): see REQ-SRV-017's own text -- the same rcp_mock_server_check_response_queue_heartbeat() closes this requirement's own identical remaining gap. STILL PARTIAL, unchanged boundary: the integrator still owns calling this periodically against a real clock and driving a real transport with the result.

requirements.title: svr_discovery_timeout register (Table 33/36, RC-Server-specific block, 16 bit, R/W*)
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_regmap_svr_ep_cfg_t now carries svr_discovery_timeout (TC18 §13.7.1.2's own RC-Server functional-configuration table -- Table 33 in the RC1 baseline, renumbered Table 36 in the current RC5 baseline this project treats as authoritative, confirmed the same table via direct PDF page-image reads of both revisions; 16 bit, R/W*, microseconds), defaulting to TC18's own stated 20000 (20 ms) via rcp_regmap_svr_ep_cfg_init(). Content modeling only, same deferred ACF_ABB-wire-wrapper gap as HW_config/EP_ID_config/response-queue/Table 24 -- and this register is also NOT yet wired to rcp_discovery_claim_t's own Discovery_TimeOut (a separate, caller-supplied-milliseconds constructor argument), so the TC18 §12.6 rule that an unused discovery stream is dropped after Discovery_TimeOut is still not enforced from this register. This table's own relative-address column also carries a real, confirmed primary-source defect (see regmap.h's own file-header note) that does not affect this field, which sits outside the collision. CLOSED 2026-08-13 (tc18-gap backlog PR H, issue #336): rcp_mock_server_t now carries its own rcp_regmap_svr_ep_cfg_t (this table's own real storage -- previously not even declared anywhere in the mock server double, a bigger gap than this entry's own prior text stated: it described svr_discovery_timeout as unwired to rcp_discovery_claim_t, but the register had no server-side storage at all) and its own rcp_discovery_claim_t. New rcp_mock_server_set_discovery_timeout_us() (mock.h/mock.c) sets svr_ep_cfg.svr_discovery_timeout AND re-derives discovery_claim.timeout_ms from it via a truncating microsecond-to-millisecond conversion, the same capacity-sync convention REQ-RMAP-032/034/036/037 already established; new rcp_mock_server_svr_ep_cfg()/_discovery_claim() accessors give direct-pointer access, matching rcp_mock_server_regmap()'s own established convention for plain, fully public struct types. rcp_mock_server_new() calls the new setter once internally with TC18's own stated default (20000 us), so every server starts with a real, correctly-configured, unheld claim -- not a zero-timeout claim that would immediately re-open regardless of the register's own value. Proven via three dedicated tests: the TC18 default is genuinely applied at construction, the setter keeps both fields in sync with a truncating (not rounding) conversion, and the REAL discovery.h claim functions (rcp_discovery_claim_is_open()/_note_request()) operate correctly end-to-end against srv->discovery_claim, driven by a configured timeout -- not a re-implementation of discovery.h's own logic. The truncating conversion was mutation-tested and caught cleanly. Same "generic primitive proven, production dispatch routing deferred" disposition as HW_config/EP_ID_config/etc.'s own earlier closures: mock.c still has no discovery-request/response frame handling to route through at all (a separate, materially larger feature, not attempted here).
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2 Table 36 (Table 33 in RC1), TC18.txt L4392-4393

requirements.title: RC Server endpoint functional-config block (Table 33/36) incl. svr_enable always 1 / read-only
requirements.text: PARTIAL: rcp_regmap_svr_ep_cfg_t now carries svr_ep_status (TC18 §13.7.1.2's Table 33/36, RC-Server-specific block, 16 bit, R/W, no further bit-level breakdown given). DELIBERATELY STILL NOT MODELED: the table's own generic EP_FUNC-common-header fields (svr_ep_len 0x0000 R, reserved, svr_ep_enable&clr with svr_enable permanently 1 and read-only, svr_ep_options R/W*) -- §13.7.1.1's own prose, immediately preceding this table, states "the RC Server as endpoint is not included in the EP_FUNC_config register maps", directly contradicting the table listing these fields for the RC Server anyway. Modeling them would mean silently picking a side of a stated, unresolved spec self-contradiction (see regmap.h's own file-header note for the full investigation, including a real, confirmed-on-both-PDF-revisions address collision in this same table, independent of this contradiction). The shared rcp_regmap_ep_functional_cfg_t prefix continues to model those four fields generically for every OTHER endpoint type only, unchanged.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2 Table 36 (Table 33 in RC1), TC18.txt L4370-4395

requirements.title: Register-write outcome: read-only register succeeds silently, write-prohibited register errors
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-14): TC18 13.7.1.2's evt[2:0]-keyed SET/OR/AND/XOR register-write rule is now live for every EP0 register-map write path this codebase routes. New rcp_regmap_ep0_write_op_t (SET=0/OR=1/AND=2/XOR=3, matching evt[2:0]'s low 2 bits -- exactly 4 operations named for this context, unlike Table 33's own 8-value per-endpoint scheme) and rcp_regmap_ep0_combine_write_op(), a shared byte-wise combine primitive. rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() needed no new parameter: the ACF header's own evt field is already decoded locally (hdr.evt), so evt[2:0] in {4..7} is rejected up front with RCP_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_CMD (Table 33's own 'reserved value' precedent), before any address routing. Each of the 6 row-typed table extents (HW_config, EP_ID_config, response-queue-config, request-stream-cfg, ep_generic_cfg, the sequencer table) renders its own current image and combines against it before calling its existing, unmodified apply_reconfig() -- SET short-circuits to a pure passthrough (identical to this dispatcher's own pre-fix behavior, so every one of the 46 pre-existing dispatcher-level tests continues to pass completely unchanged, zero signature churn). The 4 optional-subsystem sections combine directly against cfg->data (already the section's own current wire image, no render() needed). A genuine correctness subtlety found and fixed during this work: REQ-WAKEUP-020's own fixed-ep_id invariant prediction (ep_id_map_write_keeps_fixed_ep_id()) must see the SAME combined bytes the write will really apply, not the raw pre-combine request -- checking the raw request alone would be wrong under OR/AND/XOR, since the write's real effect depends on the table's own current content too; mutation-tested and caught cleanly when reverted to the raw-bytes check. 7 new tests: the combine primitive directly (including TC18's own worked 'OR with zero has no effect' example), the reserved-value rejection, OR/AND/XOR each applied end-to-end through the dispatcher against a representative table (HW_config, EP_ID_config, the sequencer table respectively), the fixed-ep_id-after-combine interaction (both the held-invariant and broken-invariant sub-cases), and the optional-subsystem direct combine path. 3 mutations (the OR operator itself, the reserved-value gate, and the fixed-ep_id-uses-combined-bytes fix), all caught cleanly.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2, TC18.txt L4420-L4425 -- CORRECTED 2026-08-13, citation-drift fix (issue #341 lineage, found while investigating issue #338). Line numbers corrected to the real current location in the refreshed RC5 TC18.txt; the underlying technical claim is unchanged, re-verified directly against the fresh text before touching this citation.

requirements.title: Effective register-write payload length = (acf_msg_length - 3) x 4 - pad - 2
requirements.text: acf.h's rcp_acf_reg_write_len(acf_msg_length, pad) computes the effective number of register-write data bytes exactly as (acf_msg_length - 3) x 4 - pad - 2 (TC18 13.7.1.2, formula corrected in spec revision 0.5.1_RC5), the quantity a server needs to know how many octets of an EP0 register write are data rather than address/CRC/padding -- distinct from rcp_acf_pad_len(), which computes the pad octet count only, and from the ACF decoder's own payload_len, which spans the whole payload including the address/CRC region. FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, spec rebaseline to 0.5.1_RC5): the 0.5.1_RC baseline this codebase originally read against omitted a trailing '- 2' term (for the 2-octet register start address that leads the payload, per RC5's own updated Figure 22); this function matched that omission exactly and has been corrected to match. Fail-safe on a malformed/adversarial frame: returns 0, never underflowing, if acf_msg_length is too small to hold the fixed 3-quadlet region or if pad plus the 2-octet address exceeds what remains.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2, TC18 spec PDF 0.5.1_RC5 p.92 (formula corrected, NXP_101/BE44 tracked-change; superseding TC18.txt L4035-4036 from the 0.5.1_RC baseline)

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() explicitly assigns every member of the returned writer_ctx, including via_discovery_stream
requirements.text: rcp_regmap_writer_ctx() shall set via_discovery_stream to the caller-supplied, already-classified via_discovery_stream argument (pass-through, matching via_ep0/via_unicast's own convention), and every member of the returned rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t shall be explicitly assigned before return -- none left uninitialized. Added 2026-08-10 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group H / REQ-RMAP-009): this function previously left via_discovery_stream unassigned, a genuine defect since its return value flows directly into ASIL-B write-authorization decisions (rcp_lifecycle_field_writable()/rcp_lifecycle_transition()) that read every member. Currently latent -- no production caller exists yet in src/*.c, only this function's own unit tests -- but the defect was real regardless of whether a caller happened to read the uninitialized field yet.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2, TC18.txt L2184 (same basis as REQ-RMAP-009 -- this entry covers the writer_ctx construction contract as a whole, not a new TC18 clause)

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t carries rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable, closing a gap this file's own terminology-drift note had already named but never added
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (issue #335, 2026-08-13): rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t carries rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable (TC18 §12.7.7 Table 24, relative address 0x000D bit 3 in the current RC5 numbering -- see the file header's own "terminology drift" note for why this remains a separate field rather than collapsing into the wire's own single combined rx_enforce_request_filing bit): true drives every endpoint bound to this stream toward its configured safe state if one endpoint's own request storage overflows. Found 2026-08-11 while implementing issue #306's own request-stream-cfg wire codec: the field itself and its render()/apply_reconfig() wire codec were added then (content-modeling/wire-reachability half). rcp_e2e_overflow_should_enter_safe_state() (e2e.h/e2e.c) was already the pure decision function this field sources (runtime-decision half). What was still missing, and is now closed: the actual cross-endpoint broadcast this field's own true value is supposed to drive -- rcp_mock_server_broadcast_safe_state() (mock.h/mock.c, issue #335) now resolves a request's own stream via rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_resolve_index(), reads this exact field, and purges every non-safety-tagged request queued on every endpoint bound to that stream (not just the one whose own request storage overflowed) when it's set. All three halves -- content model, decision, broadcast -- are now real, wired, and tested (see REQ-E2E-030's own entry and test_conditional_dispatch.c's test_overflow_on_one_endpoint_broadcasts_safe_state_to_stream_siblings()).
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24, TC18.txt L3252-L3256 (same citation as REQ-E2E-030's own -- this entry covers the register-map content-modeling half, REQ-E2E-030 covers the runtime-decision half) -- CORRECTED 2026-08-13, citation-drift fix (issue #341 lineage, own follow-up self-check after PR #379's issue #335 batch left this citation untouched -- only status/text were updated there, not tc18). Table 24's real current location is TC18.txt L3217-L3293 ("Table 24: Request stream configuration"), not L2865-2882 as this citation previously said. Line numbers corrected to the real current location; the underlying technical claim is unchanged, re-verified directly against the fresh text before touching this citation.

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() consults lifecycle-state/writer/lock authorization for all 4 pointed-to tables before applying any write
requirements.text: TC18 defines the write-authorization outcome for a register-map write per its own table-specific access-type column and surrounding prose (§12.3.1.2's own general R/R+/R+P/W/W*/W+ semantics, narrowed per table by that table's own text) — an address-routed dispatcher that applies a write without consulting this is a genuine conformance gap independent of whether the dispatcher itself routes to the right storage. FOUND 2026-08-11 (issue #308): rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() (added by issue #301/#306) routed and applied writes to all 4 of its own pointed-to tables -- HW_config, EP_ID_config, response-queue-config, request-stream-cfg -- without checking lifecycle state, writer identity, or the svr_configuration_lock W+ lock at all, so any writer in any lifecycle state could rewrite any of them. FIXED: the dispatcher's own signature now takes rcp_lifecycle_state_t state and rcp_lifecycle_writer_ctx_t writer as parameters (matching every other write path in this codebase), and each of its 4 routing blocks now calls the correct existing primitive before applying: HW_config uses rcp_lifecycle_field_writable(state, RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_HW_GENERIC, writer) (§12.7.6's own table-specific override, see REQ-RMAP-040's own text for the HW_GENERIC-vs-FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR distinction caught and corrected during this same batch); EP_ID_config and request-stream-cfg use rcp_lifecycle_field_writable_w_plus()/rcp_lifecycle_field_writable() respectively against their own whole-table access type (see REQ-RMAP-052/047's own text); response-queue-config -- whose own 10-octet row mixes W+ octets (STREAM_UID, flush_on_count, Flush_time, relative offsets [0,2) and [6,10) mod 10) with W* octets (Max_AVTPDUsize, queue_size, offsets [2,6) mod 10) within one table -- gets a new static respqueue_cfg_row_write_authorize() helper (src/regmap.c) that classifies every touched octet's row-relative offset and requires whichever type(s) the write's own byte span actually touches to independently authorize, so a write spanning both sub-ranges is denied unless both would individually be permitted. svr_configuration_lock (Table 20, REQ-RMAP-029, already-existing storage) resolved as the single shared "locked" parameter every W+ check in this dispatcher consults — no new storage was needed. Per rcp_lifecycle_field_write_error_w_plus()'s own documented precedence, an active lock always yields RCP_ERROR_LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS regardless of writer identity or state, never RCP_ERROR_UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS (reserved for writer-specific denial when the underlying state would otherwise permit) -- verified via 6 dedicated dispatcher-level tests covering each table plus the response-queue-config mixed-span case, and mutation-tested 5 ways (one per authorization check, each caught cleanly when bypassed).
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 (general write-authorization semantics) + §12.7.6/§12.7.7/§12.7.9 (per-table access-type overrides, see REQ-RMAP-040/047/052/061's own citations)

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_ep_delay_time_us_to_reg()/_reg_to_us() convert between ep_delay_time's own free microsecond value and TC18's packed 2-bit register enum
requirements.text: PARTIAL: ep_delay_time (TC18 §13.2 Table 28/31, relative address 0x0001.4:5, 2 bit, R/W*) is restricted to exactly 4 register values -- 00b=1µs, 01b=10µs, 10b=20µs, 11b=50µs -- while rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_t's own ep_delay_time field deliberately stays a free uint32_t microsecond value internally, since it is consumed as a scheduling tick unit across request_chained.h/request_triggered.h/request_compound.h/server.c, none of which should need to know about the register's own packed encoding. FIXED (issue #311 batch 2): rcp_regmap_ep_delay_time_us_to_reg() converts a microsecond value to the matching 2-bit register value, REJECTING (not rounding) any value outside the 4 allowed ones -- a silently-substituted delay would misconfigure the endpoint's own scheduling timing, so this is treated as a real R/W* configuration-input rejection case, not a saturating-is-safe case like rx_wd_timeout_ms/flush_time_us. rcp_regmap_ep_delay_time_reg_to_us() is the inverse, masking its own input to 2 bits so it can never fail (all 4 possible register values are valid TC18 encodings).
