CROSS-CHECK FINDING: TC18's own separate prose (request_compound/_triggered/_chained's own field descriptions, 4 occurrences, both RC1 and RC5 revisions) instead reads "[1µs, 20µs, 20µs, 50µs]" -- a duplicated 20µs where the table's own 10µs belongs, almost certainly a copy-paste typo in TC18's own text propagated identically across all 4 sites; Table 28/31's own definitive, typed register table is treated as authoritative here, not the repeated prose. READ SIDE CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #311 batch 3): rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_render() (REQ-RMAP-078) calls rcp_regmap_ep_delay_time_us_to_reg(), falling back to register value 0 (1µs) if the internal value is not exactly one of the 4 allowed ones -- expected behavior for any not-yet-configured endpoint, not an error case, since this field's own zero-init default (0µs) is itself not a valid register value. WRITE SIDE CLOSED 2026-08-12 (issue #311 batch 4): rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_apply_reconfig() (REQ-RMAP-079) calls rcp_regmap_ep_delay_time_reg_to_us() to decode an incoming write's own octet 0x0001 bits 4:5 -- this direction can never fail (all 4 register values are valid), so no fallback is needed on the write side (unlike render()'s own read-side fallback). Per-field range-overlap tracked, not derived through a lossy whole-buffer reparse. DISPATCHER ROUTING CLOSED 2026-08-12 (issue #311 batch 5): see REQ-RMAP-073's own text for the shared dispatcher wiring (REQ-RMAP-080). This closes the last gap this requirement's own text tracked.
requirements.tc18: §13.2 Table 28/31, TC18.txt L3555-3559 (RC5 baseline; identical on RC1)

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_ep_req_storage_size_words_to_octets()/_octets_to_words() convert between ep_req_storage_size's own octet count and TC18's 32-bit-word register unit; the field itself widened to uint32_t
requirements.text: PARTIAL: ep_req_storage_size (TC18 §13.2 Table 28/31, relative address 0x0002, 16 bit, R/W*) is expressed in 32-bit words on the wire, octets internally. FIXED (issue #311 batch 2): rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_t's own ep_req_storage_size field is widened from uint16_t to uint32_t -- the register's own maximum representable value, 65535 words, is 262140 octets, which does not fit a 16-bit octet count, a real correctness gap independent of any wire codec (this widening has zero consumers to break, per a direct grep of the whole codebase before making the change). rcp_regmap_ep_req_storage_size_words_to_octets() (read side) is always exact and cannot fail. rcp_regmap_ep_req_storage_size_octets_to_words() (write side) rejects an octet count that is not an exact multiple of 4 (no lossy rounding of a configuration input) or whose word count would not fit the register's own 16-bit width. READ SIDE CLOSED 2026-08-11 (issue #311 batch 3): rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_render() (REQ-RMAP-078) calls rcp_regmap_ep_req_storage_size_octets_to_words(), clamping down to the nearest representable word count (never rounding up) if the internal value is not an exact multiple of 4 or exceeds the register's own 16-bit width -- the same "never grant more than configured" bias already established for this table's own ep_delay_time. WRITE SIDE CLOSED 2026-08-12 (issue #311 batch 4): rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_apply_reconfig() (REQ-RMAP-079) calls rcp_regmap_ep_req_storage_size_words_to_octets() to decode an incoming write's own octet 0x0002-0x0003 -- this direction can never fail (always exact), so no clamp is needed on the write side (unlike render()'s own read-side clamp). Per-field range-overlap tracked. DISPATCHER ROUTING CLOSED 2026-08-12 (issue #311 batch 5): see REQ-RMAP-073's own text for the shared dispatcher wiring (REQ-RMAP-080). This closes the last gap this requirement's own text tracked.
requirements.tc18: §13.2 Table 28/31, TC18.txt L3562 (RC5 baseline; identical on RC1)

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_render() serializes ep_generic_cfg's own 12-octet-per-endpoint wire stride, the READ side of issue #311's own wire-codec batch
requirements.text: PARTIAL: TC18 §13.2 Table 28/31 lays ep_generic_cfg out as a 12-octet row per endpoint (ep_type at relative 12*N onward). FIXED (issue #311 batch 3): rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_render() serializes entries[0..count) at exactly this stride -- ep_type (0x0000, direct octet), ep_used/ep_delay_time packed into 0x0001 (bit 0 and bits 4:5 respectively, reserved bits 1:3/6:7 left 0), ep_req_storage_size (0x0002-0x0003, via rcp_regmap_ep_req_storage_size_octets_to_words(), REQ-RMAP-077, clamping down on overflow/non-multiple-of-4 rather than wrapping), ep_description (0x0004-0x0007, direct), ep_tx_buffer_size/ep_rx_buffer_size (0x0008-0x000B, direct -- both already store their own wire-native word unit, REQ-RMAP-074/075). ep_delay_time uses rcp_regmap_ep_delay_time_us_to_reg() (REQ-RMAP-076), falling back to register value 0 (1µs) if the internal microsecond value is not exactly one of TC18's 4 allowed ones -- NOT a rare case: rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_init()'s own zero-init default (0µs) is itself not a valid register value, so every not-yet-configured endpoint hits this fallback until explicitly set. Matches every sibling render() function's own established non-fallible convention (HW_config/EP_ID_config/response-queue-config/request-stream-cfg all render() unconditionally); this is a defensive best-effort fallback, not an error signal, consistent with the "never grant more than configured" bias already established for the saturating fields in sibling tables. WRITE SIDE CLOSED 2026-08-12 (issue #311 batch 4, REQ-RMAP-079): rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_apply_reconfig() is the write-side counterpart, using PER-FIELD range-overlap tracking (not the whole-buffer render/patch/reparse idiom every sibling apply_reconfig() uses, which would be unsafe here given this function's own lossy fallback/clamp -- see REQ-RMAP-079's own text) and correctly no-op'ing (not erroring) a write touching the read-only ep_type octet, per TC18 §13.7.1.2. DISPATCHER ROUTING CLOSED 2026-08-12 (issue #311 batch 5, REQ-RMAP-080): rcp_regmap_ep0_encode_read_response() routes svr_ep_generic_cfg_ptr's own extent to this function directly, reusing it exactly as every sibling extent already does. This closes the last gap this requirement's own text tracked.
requirements.tc18: §13.2 Table 28/31, TC18.txt L3534-3582 (RC5 baseline; identical on RC1)

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_apply_reconfig() is the WRITE side of ep_generic_cfg's wire codec, per-field range-overlap tracked (not the whole-buffer idiom every sibling apply_reconfig() uses) and correctly no-op's a write touching the read-only ep_type octet
requirements.text: PARTIAL: TC18 §13.2 Table 28/31's ep_generic_cfg row is mostly R/W* except ep_type (relative 0x0000), which is plain R -- the first read-only field mixed into an otherwise fully-writable row anywhere in this codebase's wire-codec family. FIXED (issue #311 batch 4): rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_apply_reconfig() applies an incoming write's own byte span to entries[0..count). TWO design decisions, both primary-source-grounded, documented in the function's own doc comment (regmap.h) and posted to issue #311 as a scoping comment before implementation: (1) ep_type is NEVER updated regardless of whether the write's own span covers it -- TC18 §13.7.1.2 (TC18.txt L4039-4040, identical RC1/RC5) states in general terms "Writing data to read only registers has no effect and request is confirmed normally", so a write touching only ep_type returns RCP_REGMAP_EP_GENERIC_CFG_RECONFIG_OK, not an error (this directly confirms REQ-RMAP-068's own long-standing "UNCONFIRMED HYPOTHESIS" for this specific case -- see that entry's own updated text). (2) this function does NOT use the render()-then-patch-then-reparse-the-whole-buffer idiom every sibling apply_reconfig() (HW_config/EP_ID_config/response-queue-config/request-stream-cfg) uses -- that idiom is safe for them only because their own render() is a lossless round-trip; rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_render() (REQ-RMAP-078) is NOT lossless (its own defensive ep_delay_time fallback and ep_req_storage_size clamp), so reparsing a whole rendered-then-patched row would silently "launder" any already-invalid field through its own fallback/clamp even for a row/field the write never touched -- a real corruption with no basis in the actual write. Instead, each of the 5 writable fields (ep_used+ep_delay_time packed at 0x0001, ep_req_storage_size at 0x0002-0x0003, ep_description at 0x0004-0x0007, ep_tx_buffer_size at 0x0008-0x0009, ep_rx_buffer_size at 0x000A-0x000B) is updated ONLY if the write's own byte span FULLY covers that field's own octet range -- a write only partially covering a multi-octet field leaves that field entirely unchanged, the same "do not silently corrupt what wasn't fully specified" principle extended from the render()-lossiness problem to ordinary partial-field writes. Tested with a dedicated case proving an already-invalid ep_delay_time in an UNTOUCHED row survives a write to a different row unchanged (the motivating correctness scenario), plus the ep_type no-op-confirmed-normally case, plus a partial-field-write case. DISPATCHER ROUTING CLOSED 2026-08-12 (issue #311 batch 5, REQ-RMAP-080): rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() routes svr_ep_generic_cfg_ptr's own extent to this function directly, with FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR authorization on the row as a whole checked first (ep_type's own read-only handling stays entirely inside this function, independent of that row-level authorization). This closes the last gap this requirement's own text tracked -- issue #311 is now fully closed, all 5 batches complete.
requirements.tc18: §13.2 Table 28/31 + §13.7.1.2, TC18.txt L3932-3980 (RC5 baseline; identical on RC1)

requirements.title: rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request()/_encode_read_response() route svr_ep_generic_cfg_ptr's own extent to render()/apply_reconfig() in both directions, the 6th and final EP0 dispatcher extent, closing issue #311
requirements.text: TC18 §12.7.5 Table 20's own svr_ep_generic_cfg_ptr field (REQ-RMAP-036) points to ep_generic_cfg (TC18 §13.2 Table 28/31), the last of the 4 originally-scoped pointed-to tables (issue #301) plus the 2 later-found ones (request-stream-cfg, issue #306; ep_generic_cfg, issue #311) to gain EP0 dispatcher routing. FIXED (issue #311 batch 5): rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() gains a 6th routing block (after Table 20 itself, HW_config, EP_ID_config, response-queue-config, request-stream-cfg) targeting [svr_ep_generic_cfg_ptr, svr_ep_generic_cfg_ptr + 12*ep_generic_cfg_count), authorizing via rcp_lifecycle_field_writable(state, RCP_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR, writer) against the row as a whole before calling rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_apply_reconfig() (REQ-RMAP-079) -- confirmed via direct primary-source verification that TC18 §13.2's own surrounding prose names no table-specific lifecycle-state override the way §12.7.6 does for HW_config (issue #308's own HW_GENERIC finding), so the generic FUNCTIONAL_W_STAR rule genuinely applies here, unlike HW_config's own narrower case. rcp_regmap_ep0_encode_read_response() gains the identical 6th extent on the read side, calling rcp_regmap_ep_generic_cfg_render() (REQ-RMAP-078) directly, matching every sibling extent's own established pattern -- no authorization gate on the read side, matching every other extent (TC18 defines no read-side access restriction for any of these tables). New dedicated tests added to both dispatcher-routing test functions (a genuine read+write round trip through the new extent, plus its own routing-boundary case) and the authorization-denial test function (RCP_CONFIGURED denies a write to ep_generic_cfg's own fully-R/W* ep_description field, proving this is a real authorization denial distinct from ep_type's own unconditional no-op). Mutation-tested 3 ways (bypassing the authorization check, loosening the write-side routing boundary, loosening the read-side routing boundary); all three caught cleanly. Closes issue #311 in full -- all 5 batches (content model, 2 boundary-conversion pairs, render(), apply_reconfig(), dispatcher wiring) complete; REQ-RMAP-073 through -079 all flip to implemented alongside this entry.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.5 Table 20 + §13.2 Table 28/31, TC18.txt L2600-2603 + L3534-3582 (RC5 baseline; identical on RC1)

requirements.title: A sequencer whose state register is manually set to 0 is disabled
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (issue #201, 2026-08-12): a sequencer whose Seq_state register has been manually written to 0 is treated as disabled (TC18 §12.7.10 Table 28, relative address 0x0000, 8 bit, R/W): no compound or compound-wait step conditioned on that sequencer becomes executable, and no advance moves it out of 0 until it is explicitly rewritten to a nonzero state. rcp_compound_start_condition_met() and rcp_compound_advance_guard() (request_compound.h/.c) both check current==0 explicitly, before their own ordinary start_state comparison -- including start_condition_met()'s own "start in any state" wildcard (start_state==0), which would otherwise treat a disabled sequencer as satisfying every step unconditionally. rcp_e2e_endpoint_in_safe_state() (REQ-E2E-018) also fails closed on a disabled sequencer, rather than reporting "in safe state" if rx_safe_sequencer_state happened to also be configured to 0. Distinct from rcp_sequencer_table_unsupported() (REQ-SEQ-004), which is the table-wide "zero sequencers implemented" case. Citation-drift fix, same lineage as issue #341: RC1's own Table 25 (SEQUENCER_config) is RC5's own Table 28 -- the catalog's stale "Table 25" citation is corrected here alongside the fix.

requirements.title: each sequencer is owned by one request stream, and only that stream may access it
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (issue #335, REQ-SEQ-013, 2026-08-13): rcp_sequencer_table_t (include/rcp/request_sequencer.h) gained a parallel owner[] byte array alongside its existing state[] array, recording each sequencer's Request_stream_index (TC18 §12.7.10 Table 28, relative address 0x0001, 8 bit, R/W*) as a 1-based rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_t row index, with 0 (RCP_SEQUENCER_OWNER_UNCLAIMED) reserved for "no client has claimed this sequencer yet" -- the same 1-based/0-sentinel convention REQ-RMAP-052's own rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_entry_t.request_stream_index already established. Design (three user-confirmed decisions): (1) fail-closed -- rcp_sequencer_access_permitted() returns false for an unclaimed sequencer regardless of requester, not open-to-anyone, since TC18 specifies the field's purpose but never how it is first established; (2) full plumbing -- mock.c gained real request_stream_cfg[]/count access (rcp_mock_server_set_request_stream_cfg(), mirroring the existing sequencers/hw_pin_map setters) and a stream_id->request_stream_index resolver (rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_resolve_index()), which also unblocks REQ-RMAP-048/049; (3) the fail-closed gate applies to BOTH attack vectors TC18's own vulnerability description covers -- direct EP0 register-map writes to Seq_state/Request_stream_index (rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request(), per-octet: Seq_state requires strict owner match, Request_stream_index permits unclaimed-or-owner-match to support first-claim and release/reassign) AND the normal compound/compound-wait admission path, which never touches the register map at all (mock.c's dispatch_plain(), admit-then-immediately-cancel via rcp_server_endpoint_cancel_single() if the admitted step's own sequencer_index fails ownership, returning RCP_ERROR_UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS) -- closing only the register-map vector would have left the more commonly-exercised protocol-native path wide open. The ownership check is explicitly skipped when rcp_sequencer_table_unsupported() (no sequencer table configured at all), a distinct pre-existing scenario this requirement does not govern. The Request_stream_index unclaimed-or-owner-match write rule is this implementation's own design choice, not itself TC18-mandated. Bonus conformance fix found and corrected in the same batch: TC18's own Table 28 SEQUENCER_config is 2 octets per sequencer (Seq_state + Request_stream_index), not the 1-octet-per-sequencer layout an earlier REQ-SEQ-014 closure had wrongly assumed and shipped -- rcp_regmap_sequencer_table_render()/_apply_reconfig() now interleave both fields correctly; see REQ-SEQ-014's own corrected text.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.10 Table 28, TC18.txt L3460-L3493 (2-octet stride: relative 0x0000 Seq_state, 0x0001 Request_stream_index)

requirements.title: svr_max_sequencers and the sequencer_state table expose sequencer availability and state through the register map
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (issue #334, corrected issue #335/2026-08-13): rcp_regmap_general_t.svr_sequencers_max reports rcp_sequencer_table_t.count (0 when sequencers are not implemented), and the sequencer_state sub-table pointed to by svr_sequencer_state_ptr exposes each sequencer's state over EP0 (TC18 §12.7.10 Table 28). CORRECTION (2026-08-13): this requirement's original closure wrongly claimed the wire layout was TC18's own "one-octet-per-sequencer Seq_state" image needing no render() step -- a direct read of TC18.txt L3460-3493 (Table 28, corrected 2026-08-13 -- see REQ-SEQ-013's own citation-drift note) shows each sequencer is actually 2 octets: relative 0x0000 Seq_state (8 bit, R/W) then relative 0x0001 Request_stream_index (8 bit, R/W*), repeating per sequencer. Any real client parsing the old 1-octet wire image per TC18's actual 2-octet stride would misread every sequencer past the first. Fixed as part of REQ-SEQ-013: rcp_regmap_sequencer_table_render() now interleaves state[i]/owner[i] into the correct 2-octet layout, rcp_regmap_ep0_encode_read_response() gained a sequencer_owner parameter and the correct sequencer_count*2u extent-length math, and rcp_regmap_sequencer_table_apply_reconfig() provides the matching write-side render->patch->reparse path. Write access (originally flagged as a separate, still-open gap) is now implemented as part of REQ-SEQ-013's own ownership-aware EP0 write dispatcher.

requirements.title: evt[2:0] selects which of the six SPI channel configurations a request uses
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-12, issue #201 Phase 5e): the SPI endpoint carries RCP_EP_SPI_MAX_CHANNELS (6) independently pre-configured channel configurations (rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_t::channels), and rcp_ep_spi_decode_transfer_request() already extracts and validates the requesting channel from the request's evt[2:0] field (rcp_ep_spi_channel_valid()), returning it for a caller to index cfg->channels[] with, per TC18 13.7.3.1/13.7.3.2 -- the same evt-bits mechanism this codebase's own dedicated SPI channel-selection investigation (issue #256, task #98) independently confirmed correct against Table 26/§13.5. This entry's own catalogue text simply never caught up to the already-implemented behavior -- same stale-catalog-entry pattern found and fixed 4+ times this session (REQ-UART-036 and others). No code change: the deviation was in the catalogue, not the code.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 (SPI row, evt[2:0] selects channel), TC18.txt L4076-4078 and §13.7.3.2 (spi_nr_cs), TC18.txt L4642

requirements.title: SPI trigger output numbering (Table 41)
requirements.text: c-RCP now implements TC18 Table 41's SPI trigger output numbering via rcp_ep_spi_trigger_signal_number() -- signal 0 'SPI execution done' (whole-endpoint, not modelled by this per-channel function), signal 1 reserved, and signals 2+2n/3+2n pairing chip select CSn with an asserted/de-asserted event (0 <= n < 16, narrowed to this module's own 6 channels, i.e. signals 2..13). The endpoint's own per-channel trigger selector (rcp_ep_spi_trigger_t) stays the deliberately-collapsed, non-wire-rendered representation described in ep_spi.h's own file header; this numbering function is a separate, additive computation resolving a (channel, CS-edge) pair to its Table 41 signal number.

requirements.title: SPI functional-config register block (Table 39/42) is fully modeled
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): rcp_ep_spi_channel_cfg_t now carries every Table 39 per-channel field this module previously omitted -- baud_rate_kbps (spi_baud_rateN, kbit/s), use_common_cs (spi_use_csN), cs_clk_leadtime/clk_cs_trailtime (spi_cs_clk_leadtimeN/spi_clk_cs_trailtimeN, in spi_clk cycles, distinct from this module's own pre-existing nanosecond-denominated inter_byte_delay_ns/inter_transfer_delay_ns), and bits_max (spi_bits_maxN); rcp_ep_spi_functional_cfg_t gained ep_status (spi_ep_status). CPOL/CPHA continue to round-trip losslessly through the pre-existing mode byte via rcp_ep_spi_mode_cpol()/_cpha() and a new inverse. rcp_ep_spi_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig() (evt[2:0] == 111b, Table 33's SPI row + §12.7.1) now serialize/parse the whole block -- spi_ep_len and spi_nr_cs are rendered from RCP_EP_SPI_EP_FUNC_LEN/RCP_EP_SPI_MAX_CHANNELS and are read-only, matching PWM_OUT's/GPIO's own EP_LEN convention. UPDATED 2026-08-11 (spec rebaseline to TC18 0.5.1_RC5): spi_nr_cs (renumbered Table 39 -> Table 42) was narrowed from a plain 8-bit count to a 4-bit "(count - 1)" field (bits [3:0], upper nibble reserved) by spec revision RC4 -- rcp_ep_spi_render_registers() now renders (RCP_EP_SPI_MAX_CHANNELS - 1) & 0x0F (0x05) instead of the plain count (0x06). See REQ-SPI-040 for the new spi_deassert_cs_pauseN bit RC5 adds to the same block.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.2 Table 39 (0.5.1_RC baseline)/Table 42 (0.5.1_RC5), TC18.txt L4628-4703; spi_nr_cs width corrected per RC5 PDF p.96 (051RC4 tag, ticket unlabeled -- "this standard limits the number of CS line per EP to 32")

requirements.title: SPI zero-fill when read_size exceeds the payload, full payload on PICO otherwise
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-12, issue #201 Phase 5e): rcp_ep_spi_encode_transfer_request()/_decode_transfer_request() now carry read_size through the ACF header's own read_size_or_segment_num field (previously unwired), and the new rcp_ep_spi_transfer_length(tx_len, read_size) computes TC18 13.7.3.3's own transfer-length rule -- max(tx_len, read_size): a caller driving real SPI hardware clocks tx_data[0..tx_len) verbatim followed by zero octets up to the returned length when read_size exceeds tx_len (the bus clocks read_size octets total), and always clocks at least the full tx_len-byte payload on PICO even when read_size is smaller (never truncated). All existing call sites (src/adapt.c's RCP_ADAPT_OP_SPI_TRANSFER, plus test call sites) updated for the new parameter; adapt.c defaults an absent rcp.spi.read_size meta key to the payload's own length, matching a request that asks for exactly what it sends back. Mutation-tested: dropping read_size on encode and bypassing the max() computation both caught cleanly; a `>` vs `>=` boundary mutation at read_size==tx_len is a provably equivalent mutant (both branches return the identical numeric value at that exact point) and needs no discriminating test.

requirements.title: SPI error state resets the EP enable bit; a clamped pin flags every response
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED, genuinely blocked by spec silence (investigated 2026-08-12, issue #336): TC18 13.7.3.3 states "If the SPI stops execution (see cs/hs bits) -- then SPI endpoint is in error state (-> spi_ep_status, already modeled as RCP_EP_SPI_REG_EP_STATUS/Table 39 -- CORRECTED 2026-08-13: RC1's own text said "->debug register)"; RC5's own correction, "051RC5 corrected TI_088", changed this to "-> spi_ep_status )"). And the SPI endpoints enable bit in the EP_config is reset," but the specification never defines what "cs/hs bits" indicating a stopped execution actually means for SPI -- every request-format table in the document (standard requests, §11.2.2.3 Trigger requests) lists both ACF header bits as fixed 0b/reserved, with only §11.2.2.4's Chained request giving cs a real, unrelated meaning ("Conditional start"). It is equally plausible the sentence instead means the SPI bus's own physical CS (chip select)/HS (handshake) hardware signal lines -- a distinct, electrical-level concept §13.7.3.1's own Table 38 already names "CS0"-"CS5" -- rather than the ACF protocol header's cs/hs bits at all. The two readings lead to entirely different implementations (an observable protocol-level condition vs. a hardware signal this pure protocol-core library has never modelled for any endpoint type), and there is no way to determine which is intended from the text as written. Filed as a genuine specification defect, not a local implementation gap: TC18_spec_defects_report.md item 56 (and its own _quadruple_checked.md review copy). The requirement's own second half -- a clamped pin setting the err flag in every subsequent response -- does not depend on this ambiguity, but the pin-electrical-state detection it requires is itself hardware this module has never modelled for any endpoint type (matching every other endpoint's own 'never itself owns a timer, thread, or ... hardware' scope boundary), so it is left unattempted alongside the blocked half rather than force-splitting one requirement into two differently-dispositioned catalog entries.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.3, TC18.txt L4740-4750 -- CORRECTED 2026-08-13, citation-drift fix (issue #341 lineage): this repo's own cached TC18.txt was a stale RC1-dated pdftotext dump, since re-extracted from the real RC5 PDF

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_render_registers()/_encode_reconfig_request() implement the generic §12.7.1 configuration request for SPI
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): TC18 §12.7.1 Figure 18 defines one generic configuration request -- evt[2:0] = 111b, byte_msg_payload = a relative register start address within the addressed endpoint's EP_func section followed by configuration data -- usable against every endpoint type. SPI's own Table 33 row confirms 111b carries this exact meaning (distinct from evt[2:0] 000b-101b, which select one of SPI's six pre-configured channels, and 110b, which is reserved/UNSUPPORTED_CMD). rcp_ep_spi_render_registers() serializes cfg's whole Table 39 block (the 6-octet common prefix plus six 8-octet per-channel blocks); rcp_ep_spi_encode_reconfig_request() encodes an ACF_ABB write request (op=WRITE, evt=111b) carrying a 16-bit big-endian start address followed by data, matching PWM_OUT's/GPIO's own encode_reconfig_request() shape.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints + Figure 19 (renumbered from Figure 18 by the RC5 rebaseline), TC18.txt L2844-2860; §13.5 Table 33 (SPI row), TC18.txt L4076-4078

requirements.title: rcp_ep_spi_apply_reconfig()/_reconfig_strerror() apply the addressed configuration write and never return NULL for a status message
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, issue #256 Group I): rcp_ep_spi_apply_reconfig() decodes the address+data payload TC18 §12.7.1 defines and patches cfg's Table 39 register block at octet granularity, then adopts the whole block atomically -- a write whose start_address+length exceeds RCP_EP_SPI_EP_FUNC_LEN is rejected and cfg left entirely unchanged (RCP_EP_SPI_RECONFIG_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE), matching §12.7.1's own 'such a payload is to be ignored' rule; octets landing on a read-only register (EP_LEN, NR_CS, or a channel's own reserved octet) are silently skipped while the rest of the span is still applied. rcp_ep_spi_reconfig_strerror() never returns NULL, including for an unrecognized error code.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 Configuration of endpoints, TC18.txt L2844-2860

requirements.title: spi_deassert_cs_pauseN (Table 42, new in spec revision 0.5.1_RC5) is modeled
requirements.text: FIXED 2026-08-11 (c-RCP-AUDIT-06, spec rebaseline to TC18 0.5.1_RC5): spi_deassert_cs_pauseN is a new configuration bit (bit 4 of a channel's own +0x02 cfg octet, ticket NXP_100) with no counterpart at all in the 0.5.1_RC baseline this module was originally built against -- "0b: no de-assertion during break / 1b: de-assertion during break" during the pause window spi_cs_clk_leadtimeN/spi_pause_minN/spi_clk_cs_trailtimeN define. rcp_ep_spi_channel_cfg_t gains a new deassert_cs_pause field (RCP_EP_SPI_CFG_BIT_DEASSERT_CS_PAUSE); rcp_ep_spi_render_registers()/parse_registers() (the rcp_ep_spi_apply_reconfig() inverse) render/parse it, leaving every pre-existing cfg bit (clk_polarity/clk_phase/cs_polarity/use_cs) untouched -- the same 'new field, existing fields left alone' rule already established for every prior Group I register-block fix this session.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.2 Table 42, TC18.txt L4663-4665, spec revision 0.5.1_RC5 PDF p.96 (ticket NXP_100, tags 051RC5 "new configuration, optional" + "added for clarification")

requirements.title: A disabled endpoint still executes configuration requests immediately
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_submit() inspects a request's own evt[2:0] (TC18 §12.3.1.3): 111b -- Table 33's own universal per-row 'EP_func configuration write' meaning, §12.7.1 -- is executed immediately even while the endpoint is disabled, including the write that would set ep_enable itself; any other evt[2:0] value (an operational request) is still queued, as before. Applies to an ABB (Standard) request AND to a GBB (Conditional) request of any kind except Compound Wait: a Compound Wait request's own evt[2:0] means an entirely different thing under §13.5.1 (an 8-way comparison-operator selector, not a configuration-write signal -- see acf.h's rcp_acf_compound_wait_match()), so rcp_server_endpoint_submit() peeks the GBB frame's own request_type (rcp_acf_peek_gbb_request_type(), REQ-ACF-032 -- added specifically to close this gap, since nothing in this codebase previously let a caller classify a GBB frame's request kind without already knowing, and calling into, one specific conditional-request module's own decoder) and excludes Compound Wait by name via the pre-existing rcp_request_type_is_compound_wait() predicate (request_compound.h); every other GBB request_type (Compound, Triggered, Chained, Timed) is treated the same as an ABB request. A GBB frame whose request_type cannot be peeked at all (too short, or genuinely not one of the six currently-defined values) is conservatively queued, the same fail-safe default this function already applies to a too-short ABB frame. Compound Wait itself remains queued unconditionally, a deliberate, permanent carve-out per §13.5.1 -- not a remaining gap.

requirements.title: Queuing a request on a disabled endpoint still emits the requested acknowledge
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-12, issue #201 Phase 5e): TC18 §12.3.1.3: "Nevertheless if requested an acknowledge us sent after storing the request." evt[3] is TC18 §13.5's own universal (endpoint-type-independent) acknowledge-request bit -- new rcp_acf_evt_requests_acknowledge() (acf.h) checks it, and new rcp_acf_build_acknowledge_response() builds a genuine Acknowledge (evt = RCP_ACF_EVT_ACKNOWLEDGE). rcp_server_endpoint_submit() gained a new out_ack parameter: when the request is queued (ep->ep_enable is false) and its own evt[3] requested an acknowledge, *out_ack is set to that Acknowledge response, addressed to the request's own byte_bus_id/transaction_num; left zeroed otherwise. Deliberately scoped to submit() itself, not admit(): admit()'s own two internal submit() call sites currently pass NULL for out_ack, so the mechanism is complete and directly testable but not yet propagated to admit()'s own callers (mock.c's real dispatch) -- a separate, not-yet-attempted integration step, matching this codebase's established disposition for primitives whose dispatch-side wiring is a distinct concern (e.g. REQ-GPIO-033, REQ-ADC-031). REQ-SRV-015's own separate gap (distinguishing a configuration request from an operational one) is now fully resolved for both ABB/Standard and GBB/Conditional requests (excluding Compound Wait, a deliberate permanent carve-out, not a gap) -- see that requirement's own text.

requirements.title: Cyclic heartbeat: empty NTSCF-only PDU on an empty response queue
requirements.text: PARTIAL: c-RCP models the response-queue periodicity register (rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t::flush_time_us) and, as of REQ-RMAP-064/065 (issue #200 Group 4), provides the primitives to recognize the trigger and construct the empty PDU -- rcp_respqueue_should_flush_by_time() (include/rcp/respqueue.h) fires identically whether the response queue is empty or not, and rcp_avtp_encode_ntscf(hdr, NULL, 0) already produces a valid empty PDU (an NTSCF header carrying no ACF messages at all), the exact case TC18 13.7.1.1 requires when the flush period elapses with an empty queue. c-RCP is a protocol library, not a scheduler; actually emitting the heartbeat -- scheduling this composition against a real clock and driving a real transport with it -- is still left to the integrator driving rcp_avtp_transport_t. COMPOSITION WIRED 2026-08-14 (tc18-gap post-backlog audit): new rcp_mock_server_check_response_queue_heartbeat(srv, response_stream_index, mac, now_us, out_heartbeat) (mock.h/mock.c) is the single call this requirement's own text said a caller had to compose by hand -- it tracks each response stream's own last-transmit moment (the same 'has_previous' idiom REQ-SRV-018's own edge detector already establishes: the first check per stream only seeds, never fires) and, on a genuine Flush_time expiry, builds and returns the real empty NTSCF heartbeat AVTPDU via rcp_regmap_response_queue_stream_id()+rcp_avtp_encode_ntscf(). mac is a new caller-supplied parameter -- this module stores no interface MAC of its own, the same 'this library never invents a value it has no way to know' discipline REQ-SRV-018's own source_ep and REQ-ADC-033's own base_clk_hz already establish. STILL PARTIAL, unchanged boundary: c-RCP remains a protocol library, not a scheduler -- calling this function periodically against a real clock, and sending the returned bytes over a real transport, stays the integrator's own job, exactly as this requirement's own text already stated. 6 new tests (test_mock.c) prove the composition end to end against a real decoded AVTPDU (not just that primitives COULD combine, which test_flush_time_trigger_and_empty_heartbeat_are_composable() already proved) -- first-check seeding, exact-threshold firing, timer reset after firing, flush_time_us==0 never firing, non-monotonic now_us rejection, and out-of-range response_stream_index rejection. The seeding short-circuit, the non-monotonic guard, and the flush-time comparison were all mutation-tested and caught cleanly. Two edge cases were investigated but are honestly NOT independently mutation-proven, only verified by code inspection: the response_stream_index bounds guard (an out-of-range 1-based index, without the guard, lands on a still-zeroed adjacent array slot that behaviorally mimics the correct 'nothing due' outcome either way, so a black-box test cannot distinguish the guard's presence from its absence), and the allocation-failure retry path (rcp_avtp_encode_ntscf(), src/avtp.c, calls plain malloc() rather than this codebase's own pluggable rcp_malloc() hook, REQ-SEQ-002's own fault-injection mechanism, so failure cannot be injected without a separate, out-of-scope avtp.c migration).

requirements.title: RC Server trigger signals 0/1: PTP time-sync established and lost (Table 37)
requirements.text: PARTIAL (issue #201, 2026-08-12): rcp_server_gptp_trigger_evaluate() (server.h/server.c) now derives TC18 Table 37's own trigger signal 0/1 from a genuine gPTP lock transition -- signal 0 (RCP_SERVER_GPTP_TRIGGER_ESTABLISHED) on a false->true edge, signal 1 (RCP_SERVER_GPTP_TRIGGER_LOST) on true->false (signal 2 stays unimplemented -- it is 't.b.d.' in the specification itself, not a local gap). A caller-owned rcp_server_gptp_trigger_state_t tracks the previously observed lock state, the same architecture already established by rcp_ep_adc_trigger_state_t (ep_adc.h) and rcp_e2e_seq_tracker_t/rcp_e2e_stream_fault_tracker_t (e2e.h). Composed by hand with the pre-existing rcp_server_endpoint_notify_trigger(), the derived signal correctly arms a stored triggered request whose own trigger_source_ep/trigger_signal_nr selection matches it. Deliberately still PARTIAL, not IMPLEMENTED: nothing in this library's own dispatch loop calls evaluate()+notify_trigger() together automatically on every tick yet -- the same 'primitive complete, dispatch wiring deferred' disposition already established for REQ-GPIO-033/REQ-ADC-031/REQ-SRV-016 -- a caller still has to drive both calls itself each time it observes a newly changed gptp_locked value. DISPATCH WIRING CLOSED 2026-08-14 (tc18-gap post-backlog audit): new rcp_mock_server_notify_gptp_lock_state(srv, locked, source_ep) (mock.h/mock.c) drives srv's own caller-owned rcp_server_gptp_trigger_state_t against one newly observed gPTP lock state and, on a genuine edge, reports the derived signal through this test double's OWN ALREADY-EXISTING rcp_mock_server_notify_trigger() broadcast -- the same primitive REQ-SRV-015's own per-endpoint-type triggers already reuse -- rather than reimplementing its own iterate-every-registered-endpoint loop (an early draft did exactly that, caught during implementation and replaced with delegation to the existing helper). A caller wanting this signal delivered now has ONE call to make per newly observed gptp_locked value, instead of composing evaluate()+notify_trigger() by hand. Proven end to end -- not just at the server.h primitive level this requirement's own prior text already covered -- by 3 new tests reusing test_conditional_dispatch.c's own real fixture/submit/tick machinery: a stored Triggered request genuinely arms and executes on an ESTABLISHED edge, the two Table 37 signals (ESTABLISHED/LOST) are not conflated, and source_ep is a real passthrough to notify_trigger() (proven in both directions -- a mismatched source_ep does not arm, a matching one does), not a hardcoded value. Both the edge-detection short-circuit and the source_ep passthrough were mutation-tested and caught cleanly -- the source_ep mutation required strengthening the original test (which only ever exercised source_ep=0, so a hardcoded-0 mutant was invisible) with a genuine match case using a nonzero value.

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() stores each COMPOUND_WAIT request's own evt and byte_msg_payload, and rejects a reserved evt
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() shall, for a decoded RCP_SCHED_KIND_COMPOUND_WAIT request, reject it (RCP_SERVER_ADMIT_REJECTED) when rcp_acf_compound_wait_evt_valid() is false for its decoded evt (TC18 §13.5.1: evt[2:0] = 011b is reserved -- "request shall be ignored and an err-response with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD shall be sent"), and otherwise store that request's own decoded evt and an owned copy of its byte_msg_payload (rcp_server_pending_t's compound_wait_evt/compound_wait_target) independently of every other pending request on the same endpoint.

requirements.title: Each pending COMPOUND_WAIT request is evaluated against the caller-supplied current status independently of any other pending request
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_select_due()/rcp_server_endpoint_complete() shall evaluate a pending RCP_SCHED_KIND_COMPOUND_WAIT request's execution condition via rcp_acf_compound_wait_match(), passing that specific request's own stored evt/byte_msg_payload (not any other pending request's) together with ctx->current_status/current_status_len; two requests pending on the same endpoint with different byte_msg_payload targets shall never be conflated by a single shared result.

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_pending_count() reports the conditional-request store's current occupancy
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_pending_count(ep) shall return the number of conditional requests currently held in ep's request store.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.2 ("Each endpoint receives request via its dedicated EP request storage."), TC18.txt L3647

requirements.title: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() reports RCP_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_CMD for a compound-wait request's reserved evt
requirements.text: rcp_server_endpoint_admit() shall, when rejecting a decoded RCP_SCHED_KIND_COMPOUND_WAIT request because rcp_acf_compound_wait_evt_valid() is false for its decoded evt, write RCP_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_CMD to *out_error (when non-NULL) so a caller can build and send a real TC18 error response (rcp_acf_build_error_response()) for this case, per TC18 §13.5.1's explicit requirement that such a request's err-response carry error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD.
requirements.tc18: §13.5.1 ("request shall be ignored and an err-response with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD shall be sent"), TC18.txt L4150-4151

requirements.title: A request carried under a TSCF header is postponed until the header's presentation time
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-14): rcp_mock_server_dispatch_tscf() (mock.h/mock.c) is a new, additional dispatch entry point -- identical to rcp_mock_server_dispatch() in every other respect, but taking tv/avtp_timestamp/gptp_reference_now and threading them straight through to rcp_server_endpoint_admit() (this requirement's own already-implemented admission/due-selection machinery, closed in the prior batch). This is the dispatch-layer wiring this requirement's own text named as its remaining scope. Design: dispatch_plain_inner()/dispatch_plain() (mock.c's own internal, static shared core, called by every one of rcp_mock_server_dispatch()/_dispatch_e2e()'s combined 130+ existing call sites) gained the same three parameters, but as a NEW function, not a signature change to any existing PUBLIC entry point: rcp_mock_server_dispatch()/_dispatch_e2e() both now call through explicitly with tv=false, so every one of their own existing callers keeps its exact prior behavior (mutation-tested -- flipping either passthrough to tv=true broke 15 pre-existing tests, caught cleanly). Only rcp_mock_server_dispatch_tscf() supplies real values. A caller who received a real TSCF-wrapped frame decodes it one layer up via rcp_avtp_decode_tscf() -- this function itself never touches the outer AVTP/TSCF framing, only the already-unwrapped ACF payload, matching every sibling dispatch function's own established convention. 2 new tests: tv=false behaves byte-for-byte like plain dispatch(), tv=true postpones a standard request (RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_PENDING, not executed immediately) -- the exact remaining gap this requirement's own text described. Mutation-tested (the tv passthrough itself), caught cleanly. NOT covered by this batch, left as a natural, narrower follow-on: rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame()/_dispatch_frame_e2e() (TC18 12.9.1.1 multi-request-per-frame dispatch) have no TSCF-aware twin yet, and rcp_mock_server_dispatch_e2e() itself still does not thread its own existing avtp_timestamp parameter (used today only for E2E CRC/sequence unwrap) into TSCF admission gating -- both are straightforward extensions of the same dispatch_plain()-level plumbing this batch built, not a new open design question. FIXED 2026-08-14 (issue #422, c-RCP-AUDIT-11): the gate itself had a real, independent conformance defect -- rcp_server_endpoint_admit() returned RCP_SERVER_ADMIT_CANCELLATION for a Cancel request (kind==RCP_SCHED_KIND_CANCELLATION) unconditionally, before tv/presentation_gate_ns (already resolved earlier in the same function) were ever consulted, so a cancellation admitted under a TSCF header with a future presentation time still applied immediately -- TC18 §11.2 names Standard, Conditional, AND Cancel with no carve-out ("If received under TSCF header all of them shall be executed earliest at the given presentation time"). Cancellation admission now routes through the same shared gate helper Standard already used (admit_standard_under_tscf_gate() generalized to admit_under_tscf_gate(), parameterized by kind/request_type, rather than duplicated a third time); mock.c's rcp_mock_server_tick() now calls apply_cancellation() instead of the ordinary endpoint handler whenever the due stored request's own kind is RCP_SCHED_KIND_CANCELLATION. Two new tests (tests/test_conditional_dispatch.c) prove a cancellation admitted with tv=true and a future presentation time is deferred (not applied on receipt, request store still holds every entry) and then actually executes -- removing its targets -- once that presentation time has passed. Mutation-tested: reverting only the admit()-side fix (leaving the new tests in place) made both new tests fail, confirming they exercise the real defect, not a tautology.

requirements.title: Standard requests, and timed requests under a TSCF header, are sent as ACF_ABB
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-14): rcp_timed_encode_request_tscf()'s own encoder-side correctness is unchanged (still correct, still directly tested) -- what closes this requirement is the decode/admission side REQ-TIMED-012's own text named as this pair's shared remaining gap. rcp_mock_server_dispatch_tscf() (mock.h/mock.c, REQ-TIMED-012's own new entry point) gives a caller who decoded a real TSCF-wrapped ACF_ABB frame (via rcp_avtp_decode_tscf(), avtp.h) somewhere real to hand that header's own tv/avtp_timestamp fields, reaching rcp_server_endpoint_admit()'s own already-implemented presentation-time gate -- a server built on this library can now genuinely honour the presentation time rcp_timed_encode_request_tscf() transmits, for the first time. See REQ-TIMED-012's own text for the full implementation detail (shared dispatch_plain() core, mutation-testing, and the narrower dispatch_frame()/_dispatch_e2e() follow-on scope this batch deliberately left open). FIXED 2026-08-14 (issue #422): see REQ-TIMED-012's own text for the full detail of the Cancel-request gate-bypass defect this pair shared and its fix -- the presentation-time gate this entry's own text describes as already reaching rcp_server_endpoint_admit() was, until this fix, still silently skipped for one of the three basic request kinds TC18 §11.2 names.

requirements.title: The WakeUp message carries the wake-up source that caused the wake
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED, FIXED 2026-08-12 (issue #201 batch 8): TC18 §12.4.1 requires the repetitive wake response to convey both a WakeUp message and the WakeUp source. New rcp_ep_wakeup_encode_wakeup_message_with_source()/_decode_wakeup_message_with_source() (ep_wakeup.h) provide this as an additive, 3-byte-payload extension (opcode + a new rcp_ep_wakeup_source_t classification byte + a source_index byte) alongside the pre-existing, unchanged 1-byte plain pair -- zero blast radius on any existing caller, since the plain rcp_ep_wakeup_decode_wakeup_message()/rcp_ep_wakeup_is_wakeup_echo() still tolerate (though do not require) the longer payload. Covers all 3 wake-source classes TC18 §12.4.1's own text names: a configured wake-source pin (RCP_EP_WAKEUP_SOURCE_IO, with a source_index into rcp_ep_wakeup_functional_cfg_t::sources[]), 'the dedicated wakepin' (RCP_EP_WAKEUP_SOURCE_WAKEPIN, named separately in that text from the configured pin table), and a TC14/TC10 network wake-up request (RCP_EP_WAKEUP_SOURCE_NETWORK), plus RCP_EP_WAKEUP_SOURCE_UNKNOWN for a caller with no source information to report. The client that requested sleep can now learn which wake source actually woke the server.

requirements.title: The WakeUp endpoint's functional config carries the WakeUp repetition time
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-14 (issue #341 lineage): the real, wire-derived repetition interval is now available. This requirement's own prior text correctly named TC18 §13.7.2.1's own '(flush_time)' parenthetical as the actual mechanism, and correctly identified that reusing rcp_regmap_response_queue_cfg_t::flush_time_us (a DIFFERENT table's field, TC18 §12.7.9 Table 24, REQ-RMAP-064) required a cross-endpoint architectural decision this codebase would not make unilaterally -- that decision is now made, following this session's own established composition pattern (mirroring rcp_mock_server_check_response_queue_heartbeat(), REQ-RMAP-065/SRV-017): new rcp_mock_server_wakeup_repetition_interval_us() (mock.h/mock.c) resolves a WakeUp endpoint's own 1-based request_stream_index through srv->request_stream_cfg[]'s own rx_resp_stream_index (REQ-RMAP-049's already-authoritative request-stream -> response-stream association) to the associated response_queue_cfg[] row's own flush_time_us, composed entirely from existing primitives -- no new wire field, no new table. Kept in mock.c rather than ep_wakeup.h itself, preserving that module's own 'nothing... is touched here' layering promise (its own file header) -- the same boundary every other cross-endpoint composition this codebase already respects. ep_wakeup.h's own in-memory repetition_time_us field is unchanged -- it remains a caller-settable fallback for when no request/response stream is configured yet, not the authoritative source once one is. Mutation-tested: the response-row resolution and the request_stream_index range guard were each independently weakened and confirmed to fail the new tests, then restored.

requirements.title: A refused sleep/standby request is answered with an error response carrying REQUEST_CANCELED
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED, FIXED 2026-08-12 (issue #201 batch 6): TC18 §12.5 requires a refused sleep/standby request to be signalled as an error message with error code REQUEST_CANCELED (RCP_ERROR_REQUEST_CANCELED, include/rcp/errors.h:55), not the old positive-form SleepCMD response carrying the module-local RCP_PWRMODE_ENTRY_REFUSED value. rcp_ep_wakeup_encode_sleepcmd_response(..., RCP_PWRMODE_ENTRY_REFUSED, ...) now returns a genuine ACF Error Response (via rcp_acf_build_error_response()) carrying that numbered wire code; rcp_ep_wakeup_decode_sleepcmd_response() recognizes an error response carrying specifically that code as the refused-entry case (any other err code is RCP_EP_WAKEUP_ERR_BAD_OPCODE, not silently reinterpreted). A conformant RC Client watching for an error response now sees the refusal, and the numbered wire code is genuinely carried on the wire.

requirements.title: WakeUp endpoint is fixed to endpoint number 1
requirements.text: PARTIAL, UPDATED 2026-08-12 (issue #201 batch 5): TC18 §13.7.2.1 fixes the WakeUp endpoint's own EP_Nr (regmap.h's EP_ID_config row field, rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_entry_t::ep_id, TC18 §12.7.8 Table 23) to 1, distinct from RCP_EP_WAKEUP_EP_TYPE (this codebase's own internal ep_type tag on a different table -- their numeric value both being 1 is coincidental, not a TC18 identity). New RCP_EP_WAKEUP_ENDPOINT_NUM constant (ep_wakeup.h) names the required value, and rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_ep_type_has_fixed_ep_id() (regmap.h/regmap.c) is a dedicated diagnostic checking a whole EP_ID_config table against it -- same shape and same disposition as REQ-RMAP-057/058's own sibling diagnostics for this table's other two TC18 §12.7.8 recommendations. Remains PARTIAL, not fully implemented: like those two siblings, this is a read-only diagnostic, not enforcement -- nothing in this codebase's own EP_ID_config write path (rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_apply_reconfig()) rejects a write that would violate the invariant; byte_bus_id itself (the wire routing address every rcp_ep_wakeup_* entry point still takes as a plain caller-supplied parameter) is correctly left unconstrained by this fix, since TC18 §13.7.2.2 states byte_bus_id is 'also defined via the EP_ID_map' the same way as any other endpoint. CLOSED 2026-08-13 (tc18-gap backlog PR G, issue #336): rcp_regmap_ep0_decode_write_request() now enforces this invariant at write time, not merely diagnoses it after the fact. New static ep_id_map_write_keeps_fixed_ep_id() (src/regmap.c) peeks what a write's own touched row(s) would become -- via the same render-then-patch half of rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_apply_reconfig()'s own idiom, stopped short of committing -- and the dispatcher denies the whole write (RCP_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, table left entirely unchanged) if any row whose own caller-supplied ep_types[i] equals the caller-supplied fixed_ep_id_target_ep_type would end up with an ep_id other than the caller-supplied fixed_ep_id_required_ep_id. Same caller-supplied-target design as the pre-existing rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_ep_type_has_fixed_ep_id() diagnostic (this section's own sibling function): regmap.c keeps no dependency on ep_wakeup.h and does not hardcode RCP_EP_WAKEUP_EP_TYPE/RCP_EP_WAKEUP_ENDPOINT_NUM -- a real caller supplies ep_wakeup.h's own concrete values. ep_id_map_ep_types may be NULL to skip enforcement entirely (no enforcement configured), matching this dispatcher's own established NULL-means-absent convention (sequencer_state/sequencer_owner, optional_cfg). Proven via a dedicated dispatcher-level test: a violating write denied with the table left unchanged, an unconstrained row's identical write applied normally, a same-value write (already-compliant) applied normally (not an unconditional deny), and the NULL-disables-enforcement fallback. Both the check's own row-offset (ep_id, not request_stream_index) and its wiring into the dispatcher were mutation-tested and caught cleanly. byte_bus_id itself remains correctly unconstrained by this fix, unchanged from this entry's own prior text.

requirements.title: WakeUp functional-config register block (Table 36) incl. write-1-to-clear wup_status
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-14 (issue #341 lineage): rcp_ep_wakeup_wup_status_t redesigned from a single aggregate latch bit to a genuine per-source 16-bit bitmask -- BREAKING CHANGE, matching TC18 §13.7.2.2 Table 36's own 'Indication of wake-up source, writing "1" clears the flag. Each bit represents a wake-up source' exactly, closing this requirement's own last remaining gap. rcp_ep_wakeup_wup_status_latch_source(s, i)/_clear_source(s, i) replace the old index-free _latch() (removed); _clear() still clears the whole mask at once, and the new _source_is_latched(s, i) query complements the existing whole-mask _is_clear(). rcp_ep_wakeup_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig() now render/parse the FULL wup_status word (bits [15:RCP_EP_WAKEUP_MAX_SOURCES] always 0), applying TC18's own write-1-to-clear rule bit-by-bit -- a write naming only some sources clears only those, leaving the rest latched, which the old single-bit model could not even express. Every existing call site (tests) updated to the new per-source API; mutation-tested (the per-bit clear, the parse loop's own bit-by-bit application, and the render-side masking were each independently weakened and confirmed to fail, then restored).
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.2 Table 39, TC18.txt L4494-4514; address-collision resolution confirmed against both the 0.5.1_RC baseline PDF and the 0.5.1_RC5 revision PDF (identical, unfixed by the spec committee, unlike MDIO's own Table 56/59 collision)

requirements.title: Wake-up source pin behavior encoding (Table 40)
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-14 (issue #341 lineage): all 6 of TC18 Table 40's own IO_SRC[15:11] values are now representable, closing this requirement's last remaining gap. rcp_ep_wakeup_source_cfg_t gains two new, purely-additive fields, trigger_on_rising_edge/ trigger_on_falling_edge (both false by default -- every pre-existing LEVEL-mode caller's own behavior is completely unchanged). The pre-existing level-only rcp_ep_wakeup_source_asserted() predicate is deliberately left entirely unchanged (edge detection needs previous-pin-level state a pure per-call function cannot carry, and redesigning it would ripple into every existing caller's own calling convention, exactly as this requirement's own prior text predicted) -- instead, a NEW, separate, stateful predicate pair closes the gap: rcp_ep_wakeup_source_edge_asserted()/_any_source_edge_ asserted(), each taking an explicit caller-owned rcp_ep_wakeup_source_edge_state_t (the same caller-owned 'has_previous' idiom this codebase already establishes elsewhere, e.g. lifecycle.h's rcp_server_gptp_trigger_state_t) -- the very first observation only seeds previous_level, never fires, avoiding a false-positive edge from an arbitrary starting level. rcp_ep_wakeup_render_registers()/_apply_reconfig() now render/parse all 6 IO_SRC values (RISING_EDGE/FALLING_EDGE/BOTH_EDGES joining the pre-existing INACTIVE/HIGH_LEVEL/ LOW_LEVEL); only the genuinely reserved range (0x06-0x1F) remains unrepresentable, correctly so, since TC18 itself defines no meaning for it -- a write encoding one still leaves that slot's own enabled/active_high/trigger_on_*_edge unchanged (an honest 'cannot apply' outcome) while pin_number still updates. Mutation-tested: the first-observation seed guard, the any_source_edge_asserted() no-short-circuit contract (caught only after a genuine differential 3-call test replaced an initial, insufficiently discriminating one), and the render-side EDGE-over-LEVEL precedence were each independently weakened and confirmed to fail, then restored.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.2 Table 40, TC18.txt L4528-4541 -- CORRECTED 2026-08-14, citation-drift fix (issue #341 lineage): the previous citation ("Table 37, TC18.txt L4128-4139") pointed at an unrelated section (§13.5.1's own compound-wait evt-field text) -- a genuine citation-drift artifact, not re-verified since this requirement's own 2026-08-11 text was last touched. Re-verified directly against the current RC5 TC18.txt before trusting it.

requirements.title: The per-stream watchdog is kicked by every request received on that stream
requirements.text: The RC Server's request-reception path shall call rcp_watchdog_keeper_kick() for a request stream's stream_id on every request successfully received on that stream, so that the per-stream watchdog measures the gap between consecutive requests from that RC Client (TC18 §12.7.7, "the watchdog is reset with each request received from this RC Client"). IMPLEMENTED: rcp_mock_server_dispatch()/_dispatch_frame() (mock.c) now also call rcp_watchdog_keeper_kick() for stream_id on every request they receive, unconditionally before lifecycle admission is even attempted -- TC18's own rule is about RECEIPT, not successful validation or execution, so a request this call goes on to reject (unknown byte_bus_id, wrong lifecycle state) still kicks, mirroring rcp_mock_server_dispatch_e2e()/_dispatch_frame_e2e()'s own identical ordering, corrected 2026-08-12 (issue #201). Fixed 2026-08-13 (issue #334): both functions widened to take an explicit stream_id parameter -- TC18 §13.6's plain-vs-safe command mode distinction is only about whether CRC32 protection is applied, not about which AVTPDU header fields are present, so plain command mode's own AVTPDU always carries a real stream_id too, confirmed against the primary source before widening. dispatch_e2e()'s own delegation calls route through a new internal dispatch_plain() helper rather than the public dispatch() wrapper, so a request already kicked once by dispatch_e2e()'s own top-level kick is never kicked twice for the same receipt. NOTE (deliberately out of scope, not a remaining gap in this request-reception path): server.h's own core rcp_server_endpoint_submit() (the lowest-level receive path, exercised directly by test_tc18_gaps_server.c's own test_watchdog_overflows_despite_continuous_requests()) has no stream_id concept at all -- server.h is deliberately layered below the AVTP/stream concept entirely (it operates on one rcp_server_endpoint_t, not a multi-endpoint RC Server), so a caller reaching an endpoint through that primitive directly, bypassing the reference server's own dispatch functions entirely, is already bypassing every other stream-scoped RC-Client behavior along with the watchdog, not uniquely this one; see rcp_mock_server_set_watchdog_keeper()'s own doc comment.

requirements.title: rcp_watchdog_default_config() returns the documented default
requirements.text: rcp_watchdog_default_config() shall return poll_interval_ms = 10.

requirements.title: rcp_watchdog_keeper_destroy() closes the poll thread and releases every owned resource
requirements.text: rcp_watchdog_keeper_destroy(k) shall be a safe no-op when k is NULL; otherwise it shall close k (joining the background poll thread if one was started) and then free its states, callbacks, and callback_ctx arrays and destroy its mutex before freeing k itself.

requirements.title: Plain versus safe command mode is selected per endpoint in the generic endpoint config and gates CRC enforcement
requirements.text: Each endpoint shall be addressable in exactly one of two modes selected by a bit in its server-owned generic endpoint configuration: plain command mode, in which requests carry no CRC32 trailer, and safe command mode, in which every request must carry a valid CRC32 trailer and a request without one, or with a mismatching one, shall not be executed (TC18 §13.6). IMPLEMENTED: mock.c's rcp_mock_server_set_endpoint_req_crc_enable() sets this test double's own in-process gate (its type-erased dispatch layer has no way to read rcp_regmap_ep_functional_cfg_t's ep_req_crc_enable field generically across endpoint types, so it keeps its own copy -- the same reasoning every other config field this module models already follows), and rcp_mock_server_dispatch_e2e() consults it: plain mode executes an unprotected request unchanged, safe mode rejects one (RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_CRC_ERROR, request never even reaches rcp_server_endpoint_admit()).

requirements.title: Safe command mode changes nothing but the appended CRC trailer and the length accounting
requirements.text: A request in safe command mode shall be byte-identical to the same request in plain command mode in its AVTPDU header fields, its ACF message type, its byte_message_info header and its byte_msg_payload, differing only by the appended CRC32 trailer and by the length-accounting adaptation that trailer requires (TC18 §13.6). IMPLEMENTED: rcp_e2e_wrap() copies acf_frame verbatim, adapts only acf_msg_length via its private adapt_acf_msg_length(), and appends four octets; rcp_e2e_unwrap() reverses exactly those two steps.

requirements.title: Each ACF message in a multi-ACF AVTPDU carries and is verified against its own CRC32
requirements.text: When an AVTPDU carries more than one ACF message, a separate CRC32 shall be computed, appended to and verified for each E2E-protected ACF message individually, never one CRC across the whole AVTPDU payload (TC18 §13.6). IMPLEMENTED: rcp_e2e_wrap()/rcp_e2e_unwrap() already worked at this granularity; rcp_mock_server_dispatch_frame_e2e() now composes that across a real multi-member frame -- each member, split via rcp_sched_split_frame_members(), is routed through rcp_mock_server_dispatch_e2e() independently, so a corrupted trailer on one member neither blocks nor is masked by another member's valid one.

requirements.title: CRC coverage begins with stream_id (8 octets) and avtp_timestamp (4 octets), big-endian
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_compute_crc() shall return the same value as rcp_e2e_crc32() over the concatenation of stream_id as 8 big-endian octets, avtp_timestamp as 4 big-endian octets (IEEE 1722's own field width), and acf_frame[0..acf_frame_len), in that order (TC18 §13.6).

requirements.title: An NTSCF-framed message contributes an all-zero avtp_timestamp to the CRC
requirements.text: When the enclosing AVTPDU carries an NTSCF header (which has no timestamp field of its own), the avtp_timestamp contribution to the CRC32 shall be four all-zero octets (TC18 §13.6). rcp_e2e_wrap_framed()/rcp_e2e_unwrap_framed() enforce this: a caller passes is_ntscf_framed=true and the wrapper forces the zero contribution regardless of what avtp_timestamp it was given. The lower-level rcp_e2e_compute_crc()/rcp_e2e_wrap()/rcp_e2e_unwrap() primitives remain general-purpose (a plain uint32_t avtp_timestamp, since they serve both TSCF- and NTSCF-framed callers) and still trust the caller to pass 0 for NTSCF traffic -- the framing-aware wrappers are the conformant entry point for a caller that already knows a message's framing.

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_wrap() adapts acf_msg_length by +1 quadlet before computing the CRC, and rcp_e2e_unwrap() reverses it
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_wrap() shall increment the acf_msg_length field of the copy it returns by one quadlet before computing the CRC, so the CRC is computed over the length-adapted frame and a conformant receiver reads a length that already includes the trailer; it shall fail safe (data=NULL, len=0) when the frame is shorter than the two octets holding that field or when the adapted value would exceed the field's 9-bit maximum (0x1FF). rcp_e2e_unwrap() shall decrement it by one quadlet on the copy it returns, so the result is byte-identical to the frame the sender passed to rcp_e2e_wrap(). CLOSED 2026-08-14 (issue #420): this +1-quadlet adaptation itself was already correct and is unaffected by the sibling REQ-E2E-042 fix -- pad_len(x) is invariant under adding a whole quadlet, so the adapted acf_msg_length value doesn't change -- but rcp_e2e_wrap()/_unwrap() now place the CRC32 trailer immediately after the real (unpadded) payload rather than after acf.c's own trailing 0x00 pad octets, matching TC18 Figures 20/21's own byte order, so "byte-identical to the frame the sender passed to rcp_e2e_wrap()" above now also holds for a non-quadlet-aligned real payload, which it previously did not on the wire (only internally, since the pre-fix bug was self-consistent between this module's own wrap()/unwrap() pair).

requirements.title: AVTPDU data length grows by 4 octets for every E2E-protected ACF message it carries
requirements.text: An AVTPDU carrying E2E-protected ACF messages shall have its ntscf_data_length (NTSCF header) or stream_data_length (TSCF header) increased by 4 octets for every ACF message in its payload that is E2E-protected (TC18 §13.6). IMPLEMENTED: rcp_avtp_encode_ntscf()/rcp_avtp_encode_tscf() already satisfied this correctly and automatically -- both recompute the length field from the actual payload buffer they are given (never from a caller-supplied value), so the adjustment is right whenever the caller concatenated rcp_e2e_wrap()'s own output per protected member first. As of this fix, that rule also has its own named, pure, directly-testable expression: rcp_e2e_data_length_for_protected_members(protected_member_count), returning protected_member_count * RCP_E2E_CRC_LEN (saturating on overflow) -- usable by a caller wanting to pre-size a buffer or independently cross-check a peer's own encoded length.

requirements.title: A fragmented message's CRC covers the first fragment's AVTPDU/ACF header plus every segment's payload
requirements.text: For a fragmented request or response the CRC32 shall be computed over the stream_id and avtp_timestamp of the FIRST AVTPDU and the FIRST fragment's ACF header, followed by the concatenated byte_msg_payload of ALL segments in order; the resulting CRC shall be appended only to the last segment's message, and only that last message's acf_msg_length and only that last AVTPDU's data-length field shall be adapted (TC18 §13.6). PARTIAL (was not-implemented): rcp_e2e_compute_fragmented_crc() (e2e.h/e2e.c) now computes exactly the required span -- stream_id + avtp_timestamp + the first fragment's ACF header + the full concatenated payload of every segment, the same running-CRC technique rcp_e2e_compute_crc() itself already uses for its own three regions. What remains not implemented: nothing in this codebase calls it yet. c-RCP's documented integration (fragment.h) still only ever wraps the final fragment's own encoded bytes via rcp_e2e_wrap(), and mock.c has no fragmented-message dispatch path at all (protected or not) to wire the new primitive into -- a materially larger, separate architecture item (building fragmented-message dispatch in mock.c from scratch) than adding this one CRC-arithmetic primitive. CLOSED 2026-08-14 (tc18-gap backlog PR E, issue #336): rcp_mock_server_dispatch_e2e_fragment() (mock.c) is the real caller this entry's own text said was missing. It feeds each ms=1 fragment's decoded payload into a per-request-stream rcp_fragment_reassembler_t (fragment.h), remembers the first fragment's own encoded header bytes, and on the final (ms=0) fragment computes the real fragmented CRC via rcp_e2e_compute_fragmented_crc() -- stream_id + avtp_timestamp (NTSCF-framed traffic forces this to 0, matching rcp_e2e_wrap_framed()'s own rule) + the remembered first header + the full concatenated reassembled payload -- exactly the span this requirement specifies, verified against the actual trailer bytes on the wire, not rcp_e2e_wrap()'s own (wrong, single-frame) formula. On mismatch: the identical stream-fault-tracker / stream_status[] / broadcast-safe-state consequences rcp_mock_server_dispatch_e2e()'s own CRC-mismatch branch already applies. On match: a synthetic complete ACF message (the final fragment's own decoded header + the full reassembled payload) is dispatched via dispatch_plain(), so every existing admission/conditional-request/response-building behavior applies unchanged past this point.

requirements.title: The ms bit decides whether a message carries a CRC32 trailer in its last quadlet
requirements.text: A message whose ACF header ms bit is 0 shall carry the CRC32 in its last quadlet, and a message whose ms bit is 1 shall carry no CRC32 at all, the CRC appearing only on the final (ms=0) fragment of a multi-segment message (TC18 §13.6). ONLY A CALLER CONVENTION in c-RCP: rcp_e2e_fragment_carries_crc() takes an abstract is_last_fragment boolean and neither reads the ms bit itself nor is invoked anywhere in src/ — the ms-to-is_last_fragment binding lives only in fragment.h's file header prose. CLOSED 2026-08-14 (tc18-gap backlog PR E, issue #336): rcp_mock_server_dispatch_e2e_fragment() (mock.c) now reads the ms bit itself to decide trailer handling, closing the gap this entry's text named -- an ms=1 fragment is decoded and fed to the reassembler with no CRC trailer expected at all; an ms=0 fragment arriving while the reassembler is collecting is treated as carrying the CRC32 in its own last RCP_E2E_CRC_LEN octets, verified via REQ-E2E-038's fragmented-CRC formula. rcp_e2e_fragment_carries_crc() itself is still a standalone, uncalled arithmetic helper (its own is_last_fragment abstraction was never the missing piece) -- the real ms-bit binding this requirement describes is now enforced directly in the new dispatch function instead. FIXED 2026-08-14 (issue #445, c-RCP-AUDIT-24): the 2026-08-14 REQ-E2E-042/issue #420 fix moved the CRC32's own wire location (rcp_e2e_wrap()/_unwrap(), e2e.c) to sit immediately after the REAL (unpadded) payload, [header][real payload][CRC32][pad], but this function's own final-fragment CRC extraction was not updated alongside it and kept assuming the trailer was always literally the frame's last RCP_E2E_CRC_LEN octets -- correct only when a final fragment's real payload happened to already be quadlet-aligned (pad_octets == 0, true of every existing test vector at the time), wrong whenever it was not, spuriously rejecting a legitimately-CRC'd request with RCP_MOCK_DISPATCH_CRC_ERROR. Now pad-aware: the extraction reads real_len = fragment_len - RCP_E2E_CRC_LEN - pad_octets from the same peek_hdr.pad field (byte_message_info octet 2 bits 7:6) this function's own 8-octet peek already decodes, mirroring rcp_e2e_unwrap()'s identical real_len derivation, and reads the trailer at fragment[real_len..real_len+4) instead of fragment[fragment_len-4..fragment_len).

requirements.title: Requests and responses use one identical CRC scheme
requirements.text: The CRC32 coverage span, parameterization, length adaptation and trailer placement shall be identical for requests and for responses: rcp_e2e_wrap() and rcp_e2e_unwrap() shall take no direction parameter and shall behave identically whichever direction a frame travels in (TC18 §13.6).

requirements.title: A CRC mismatch on a protected stream generates an error response as well as skipping execution
requirements.text: When a request arrives on an E2E-protected stream and its CRC32 does not match, the RC Server shall not execute the request AND shall generate an error response carrying the CRC-mismatch wire error code (RCP_ERROR_POCI_FAILURE, 12 — the code TC18 §12.9.6 Table 30 assigns a CRC mismatch, spelled CRC_ERROR in §13.6's prose) (TC18 §13.6). IMPLEMENTED: rcp_e2e_unwrap() already reported RCP_E2E_ERR_CRC_MISMATCH and rcp_e2e_wire_error() already mapped it; rcp_mock_server_dispatch_e2e() is now the caller and error-response emitter that were missing -- on a mismatch it never calls rcp_server_endpoint_admit() at all (not admitted, not merely not-executed) and builds a genuine TC18 §12.9.6 Error Response (err=1, rsp=1, payload=RCP_ERROR_POCI_FAILURE, byte_bus_id/transaction_num carried through from the request) via rcp_acf_build_error_response().

requirements.title: CRC coverage excludes the byte_msg_payload's pad octets; the trailer lands immediately after the real payload, with padding appended after it
requirements.text: The CRC32 shall be computed over the byte_message_info header and the byte_msg_payload's REAL (unpadded) bytes only -- excluding any 0x00 quadlet-alignment pad octets acf.h's rcp_acf_pad_len() appends -- and the resulting CRC32 trailer shall be placed immediately after the last real payload byte, with any quadlet-alignment padding appended strictly AFTER the complete trailer (TC18 §13.6 Figures 20 and 21: "a CRC32 is calculated ... across ... the entire payload (except padding)"). rcp_e2e_wrap() still enforces that acf_frame_len itself is a whole quadlet (matching acf.c's own already-padded encoder output), rejecting (zeroed rcp_bytes_t) any acf_frame_len that is not. CLOSED 2026-08-14 (issue #420): previously rcp_e2e_wrap() computed the CRC over the WHOLE already-padded acf_frame -- including the pad octets it should have excluded -- and appended the trailer directly after that, producing the wire order [header][payload][pad][CRC32], the reverse of Figures 20/21's [header][payload][CRC32][pad] and non-conformant for any payload whose real (unpadded) length isn't already a multiple of 4 bytes (e.g. Figure 20's own worked 6-byte-payload example). rcp_e2e_wrap()/_unwrap() now read acf_frame's own wire-format "pad" field (byte_message_info octet 2 bits 7:6, acf.h Figure 7 -- the same field acf.c's encoders already populate with the true pad-octet count) to locate the real/pad boundary, needing no new parameter and no change to acf.c: the CRC32 is computed over, and the trailer placed immediately after, only the real prefix, and the original trailing pad octets are re-seated after the trailer instead of before it. Total wire length and the +1-quadlet acf_msg_length adaptation (REQ-E2E-036) are unchanged, since a whole quadlet's worth of trailer never changes how many pad octets are needed to reach the next quadlet boundary -- only the byte ORDER and the CRC's coverage span change.
requirements.tc18: §13.6 Figures 20 and 21 ("a CRC32 is calculated ... across ... the entire payload (except padding)"), TC18.txt L3854-3863, L3872-3881

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_stream_fault_init() starts a fault tracker in the not-faulted state
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_stream_fault_init(f) shall set f->faulted to false.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("rx_enforce_e2e ... 0b: stream is not blocked..."), TC18.txt L2861-2864 -- the initial, not-yet-faulted state this register default implies

requirements.title: rcp_e2e_stream_fault_is_faulted() reports the tracker's current state
requirements.text: rcp_e2e_stream_fault_is_faulted(f) shall return f->faulted unchanged.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("rx_enforce_e2e ... 1b: stream is blocked until released, when CRC check at EP fails."), TC18.txt L2865-2867

requirements.title: CRC-error safe-state escalation (rx_enforce_e2e's second consequence)
requirements.text: IMPLEMENTED (issue #335, 2026-08-13): TC18 §12.7.7 Table 24's own 0x000D.0 rx_enforce_e2e description names two distinct consequences for its 1b value in the same sentence -- "stream is blocked until released, when CRC check at EP fails" (REQ-E2E-021's rcp_e2e_stream_fault_on_crc_error()/rcp_e2e_stream_fault_t) AND "Safe state will be entered" -- both are now wired. rcp_e2e_crc_error_should_enter_safe_state() (e2e.h/e2e.c, ADDED 2026-08-10) is the pure per-cause decision (rx_enforce_e2e carries no separate _safestate_enable bit of its own; the single bit gates both consequences at once). The stream-wide half closed this batch, matching REQ-E2E-030's own fix exactly: dispatch_e2e()'s CRC-mismatch branch (mock.c) now also calls rcp_mock_server_broadcast_safe_state() (mock.h/mock.c, issue #335) via rcp_regmap_ep_id_map_byte_bus_ids_for_stream() (regmap.h/regmap.c) and rcp_regmap_request_stream_cfg_resolve_index(), purging every non-safety-tagged request queued on every byte_bus_id bound to the affected stream via EP_ID_config -- not merely the one endpoint whose own CRC check failed. Proven end-to-end by test_tc18_gaps_e2e.c's test_crc_error_on_one_endpoint_broadcasts_safe_state_to_stream_siblings() (positive) and test_crc_error_does_not_broadcast_without_an_ep_id_map() (negative control).
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("rx_enforce_crc ... 1b: stream is blocked until released, when CRC check at EP fails and Safe state will be entered"), TC18.txt L3239-L3243 -- CORRECTED 2026-08-13, citation-drift fix (issue #341 lineage, own follow-up self-check after PR #379's issue #335 batch left this citation untouched -- only status/text were updated there, not tc18). Table 24's real current location is TC18.txt L3217-L3293 ("Table 24: Request stream configuration"), not L2865-2882 as this citation previously said. Line numbers corrected to the real current location; the underlying technical claim is unchanged, re-verified directly against the fresh text before touching this citation.

requirements.title: rx_stream_status aggregate blocked-status bit (new in TC18 0.5.1_RC5)
requirements.text:
PARTIAL (2026-08-13, issue #201/#336): the cross-cutting per-stream aggregate-latch primitive this entry's own prior text said the codebase lacked now exists. New rcp_e2e_stream_status_t (e2e.h/e2e.c) reuses rcp_e2e_stream_fault_t unchanged for the CRC cause (composition, not duplication) and adds three sibling bool latches (seq_blocked, wd_blocked, overflow_blocked) of the identical shape for the other three fault classes; rcp_e2e_stream_status_note_crc_error()/_note_seq()/_note_wd()/_note_overflow() latch each cause from a result the caller already computed via this module's existing rcp_e2e_seq_evaluate()/_wd_evaluate()/_overflow_should_enter_safe_state() (composed, not re-derived); rcp_e2e_stream_status_rx_blocked() is the pure aggregate read -- true iff ANY of the four latches is set, TC18's own "either...or...or...or" wording read as a logical OR, the same reading this module's own crc/seq/wd/overflow evaluators already use independently. Each cause has its own independent reset (rcp_e2e_stream_status_reset_crc()/_seq()/_wd()/_overflow()) since TC18 gives each fault class its own distinct release condition with no basis to assume one clears another. Remains partial, not implemented: src/mock.c has no per-endpoint-type dispatch of any kind (confirmed via direct grep) to actually call these note_*() functions from a live evaluate()-then-latch path, or to expose rcp_e2e_stream_status_rx_blocked() as a real register read -- the same disposition already established for REQ-CANCEL-012/REQ-ADC-037/REQ-TIMED-012/REQ-GPIO-035/REQ-GPIO-036/REQ-CANEP-030/REQ-ISELED-025. See regmap.h's own "TC18 0.5.1_RC5 terminology drift" file-header note (task #97), updated to reflect this, for the full investigation this entry is part of.
